Michael Carrick addresses Lisandro Martinez 'truth' with firm response to outside noise

Michael Carrick has maintained that the pundits who comment on Manchester United's situation don't know the truth as he rejected certain opinions about the club

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has rejected the outside perception of Man Utd

Michael Carrick insists the comments that those outside of Manchester United make are not "the truth" as he defended Lisandro Martinez in the aftermath of his fiery remarks.

‌



The Argentine criticised the club's technical director Jason Wilcox and their summer recruitment after their loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night. He's since come out and acknowledged he went about things the wrong way after talking with senior figures at the club.

But his interview came with United desperately out of form and Martinez's outburst has seen several pundits raise questions over the unity at the club and whether the dressing room are privately frustrated with how the summer was handled.

Carrick though maintains that, just because pundits and ex-players choose to cast their opinion on the current state of affairs, it doesn't mean they're correct.

He said: "Just because people talk from the outside, that doesn't mean it's the truth. The squad today in training was in a fantastic place - that's the truth."

United, who have endured their worst start to a campaign in 40 years, will look to get back to winning ways when they head to Leeds on Sunday. "I don't need results," he quipped. "We all need results. It's not about me; Manchester United is bigger than an individual, so please, I don't go into every day thinking about me. It's not about any individual player; it's about this football club and its history."

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez's interview in midweek has seen Man Utd in the headlines for the wrong reasons

Carrick's latest defeat came in the Spanish capital, but he has praised the way the team stuck at it despite going behind in the opening minute. They remained in the fight and missed several chances to level the contest before Atletico scored late, but the display was proof of the spirit that still exists.

"There's a lot of things that can impact the group in a lot of ways," he said. "From the game itself, you talk about the spirit and belief in the group, the way we started that game, it would have been easy for the game to have got away from us. The way we started to shows there's an underlying spirit."

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson has only had good things to say about boss tipped to replace Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson has only had good things to say about boss tipped to replace Michael Carrick

Sir Alex Ferguson has made his thoughts clear on the top-tier manager being linked with Manchester United

View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson is a big fan of Antonio Conte (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

Antonio Conte as Manchester United boss would go down well with Sir Alex Ferguson, judging by the managerial great's previous comments about the Italian. With Michael Carrick under mounting pressure following a poor start to the season, there has reportedly been dialogue between United and Conte's representatives.

‌



‌



The 57-year-old is said to be interested in the job should Carrick depart. Conte has even dropped a public hint that his next role could be with a club like United.

‌



In a recent interview with The Athletic, the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss, who left Napoli in the summer, said he sees himself managing a fallen giant, a term that fits United. He said: "There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history.

‌



"I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more. Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete."

There is great mutual respect between Ferguson and Conte. In 2017, after Conte led Chelsea to the title, United's greatest-ever manager hailed his energy and ability to mould a team in his image.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Ferguson told Sky Sports: "[He's] Fantastic, you see his energy on the pitch. There's a true saying that the team mirrors the manager, and that's what they've done with him.

"His team have stayed top of the league for so long. They lost to Arsenal and Liverpool early on, but since then they've been up."

‌



View 3 Images Ferguson and Conte get on well (Image: Michael Steele/Getty Images)

Conte was also interested in the United job in 2021 amid Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's poor start to the season. Despite Conte being out of work, United kept faith with the Norwegian for a few more weeks before eventually sacking him. By then, however, Conte had taken charge at Spurs.

For now, Carrick remains in situ as United gear up for Sunday's trip to Leeds United, the last match of Ruben Amorim's tenure in January. Lisandro Martinez will be part of the squad after apologising for his explosive post-match comments following Tuesday’s Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

‌



View 3 Images The pressure is mounting on Michael Carrick (Image: Getty Images)

Martinez has held "positive" talks with Carrick and club chiefs regarding his remarks, in which he accused the club of lacking ambition and questioned their summer recruitment. The Argentina international admitted his interview "did not help" with keeping the club united and said he is "fully focused on winning together."

It is understood United will not make any disciplinary action against Martinez public, but he has reportedly been fined. The 28-year-old is in the final year of his contract and could leave at the end of the season.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Mikel Merino nearly died as he relives tragic day - 'I'm lucky to be alive'
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Mikel Merino nearly died as he relives tragic day - 'I'm lucky to be alive'

Mikel Merino, the Arsenal midfielder, has recalled the tragic evening he almost lost his life after the Borussia Dortmund team bus was hit with a bombing attack

View 2 Images Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino has admitted he is "fortunate to be alive" after escaping a near-death experience during his time at Borussia Dortmund.

‌



‌



Merino was at Dortmund in April 2017 when their team bus was hit with explosives before a Champions League quarter-final tie against Monaco. Dortmund were on their way to the Signal Iduna Park when three pipe bombs went off and smashed the windows of their bus.

‌



Although there were no fatalities, defender Marc Bartra was one of two injured in the attack. He was taken to hospital where he was diagnosed with a fractured and badly cut wrist.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

But Merino has now revealed he could have died in the bombing as he was due to sit next to Bartra on the coach. Speaking to The Players' Tribune, Merino said: "I think I have an angel on my shoulder. I'm actually fortunate to be alive at all.

"I was 20 and playing for Dortmund when three pipe bombs went off right next to our bus on the way to a Champions League match. A lot of young people probably would not even believe that it happened, or how bad it was, but it marked us all.

‌



"There was a deafening noise, and then I remember the bus nearly tipping over. I looked behind me and saw blood on the floor. Smoke, screams. I remember being at the hospital later that night, waiting for Marc Bartra, who had his wrist badly cut up.

"The next day, someone told me that a huge piece of shrapnel was lodged in the headrest of the seat next to Marc. My usual seat. That day, the seat was empty.

View 2 Images Mikel Merino during his time at Borussia Dortmund (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"My legs were feeling a bit tight, and the seats in the front reclined. So I sat up there instead, and it may have saved my life. So yeah, I just have this belief that things happen for a reason."

Merino added that the incident nine years ago helped him cope with his injury absence for Arsenal last season. The 30-year-old fractured his foot last January and he ended up having two screws inserted into his left foot.

Article continues below

He said: "The specialist who did the scan had never seen a stress fracture in that part of the foot. He'd been doing this for 30 years. He had called five of the best specialists in the world, and none of them had seen it either.

"Nobody knew how my foot would recover, or if it would recover at all. Part of me feared that I would never play football again. I put all the meat on the barbecue, as we say in Spain. They told me they could drill two screws into my foot to give it support. I was like, vamos, put 'em in."

Sports.content:
Arsenal eye shock transfer for Bayern Munich flop with backroom figure leading the charge

Arsenal could make a surprise move in January to sign Bayern Munich's Kim Min-jae, who has found game time hard to come by but has an admirer at the Emirates

View 2 Images STAVANGER, NORWAY - OCTOBER 13: Minjae Kim of FC Bayern Munich following the team's remis in the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Viking FK and FC Bayern München at Viking Stadion on October 13, 2026 in Stavanger, Norway. (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images)

Arsenal are eyeing a surprise January move for Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae as they look to plug holes in their backline.

Mikel Arteta has several injury concerns, the most notable of those being William Saliba. The Frenchman was injured at the World Cup and is yet to play this season.

Piero Hincapie is also expected to be sidelined for a number of weeks with an ankle injury and that has left the Premier League champions scouring the market for potential replacements, despite the well documented depth in their squad.

Bayern star Kim has emerged as a target with Bild reporting he's on the verge of leaving the Bavarians in search of a fresh challenge. Arsenal's interest in him is reportedly being driven by Maurizio Micheli, the defender’s former mentor at Napoli, who now works as the head of scouting at the Gunners.

Kim joined Bayern from Napoli £43.5million back in 2023, a move that made him the most expensive Asian footballer in history. He's gone on to make 122 appearances, winning multiple honours, but injury problems and a serious competition for places have seen him slide down the order.

Vincent Kompany currently has Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah ahead of the South Korean in the pecking order and as a result has only played two Bundesliga games this season.

Bayern are therefore open to the prospect of selling both Kim and Alphonso Davies, another player linked with a departure, in order to raise funds as they consider making additions in January.

View 2 Images William Saliba sustained a back injury against Spain at the World Cup (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Arsenal did land Ezri Konsa during their summer recruitment drive. The Englishman arrived from Aston Villa, where he had continued to excel, and he's capable of filling in across several positions. Even still Arteta is keen to consider fresh arrivals come the New Year.

Ben White is another versatile member of Arsenal's defender, as is Jurrien Timber, with both players performing impressively whether deployed centrally or on the flanks.

Sports.title: Man City cult hero making fortune from inflatable banana business amid 114 charges scandal
Sports.content:
Man City cult hero making fortune from inflatable banana business amid 114 charges scandal

The Manchester City away end against Liverpool was packed with inflatable bananas as City came out as 3-0 winners

View 2 Images A Manchester City cult hero is cashing in on the inflatable banana craze (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Former Manchester City player Imre Varadi has seen business boom thanks to a revival of the inflatable banana craze from the 1980s and 1990s. The cult hero is affectionately known as ‘Imre Banana’.

‌



‌



He joined the club in the 1980s, with fans taking inflatable bananas to away games. It eventually died down, but has seen a revival amid the guilty verdict handed down to City over their Premier League charges.

‌



City are appealing the decision, meaning that the wait for a final outcome goes on. If they are unsuccessful, then the club could face a big punishment, which could include points deductions or even being expelled from the Premier League.

‌



In their first game since the news of the verdict, the away end at Anfield was full of inflatable bananas. It’s something that Varadi has been able to cash in on, having launched his own company selling them.

“The craze has taken off again,” he told The Sun . “It will be 40 years next year since it began and is ingrained in City’s history, so I’m proud to be a part of it.

“I launched my own company - as now the inflatable business is a billion-dollar industry. And I’m the actual ‘Imre Banana’ who played for City, wore the No 9 and scored goals for them!

‌



“To see so many bananas in the away end at Anfield was really special. And this weekend’s game against Ipswich is just going to be unbelievable.

“I’m getting thousands of orders from all over the world - demand has absolutely gone through the roof.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Man City fans have revived the inflatable banana craze. (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

The 67-year-old will be a special guest at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday as the club host Ipswich Town. The match will be the first Premier League encounter at home since the verdict was announced.

“The club want to see the entire Etihad holding bananas!” Varadi added. “City invited me and my family to the game and are giving us the VIP treatment.”

‌



The striker played for City for two years between the years of 1986 and 1988, before leaving to join Sheffield Wednesday. In his time at the club, he scored 19 goals and provided one assist in 59 appearances.

City were one of several English clubs Varadi played for during his long career. He made the most appearances for Newcastle United, but also played for Leeds United, West Bromwich Albion and Everton, among others.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Florian Wirtz's biggest issue identified as Andoni Iraola admits dilemma
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Florian Wirtz's biggest issue identified as Andoni Iraola admits dilemma

Liverpool's latest news round-up includes a verdict being made on Florian Wirtz's biggest struggle

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola's side bounced back after their first Premier League defeat of the season (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool bounced back from their 3-0 defeat to Manchester City with an emphatic 6-3 victory over LASK. The Reds earned their second Champions League win of the season on Wednesday against the Austrian side.

‌



‌



It was an impressive performance from Andoni Iraola's side, albeit with some questionable defending late on that saw the European minnows score three past Alisson Becker in the last 30 minutes.

‌



Bradley Barcola netted the first senior hat-trick of his career, while Lewis Koumas scored his first goal in the prestigious competition. Florian Wirtz registered an assist in the match, but his struggles have been discussed, while the Spanish boss opened up about the dilemma he faces within his squad.

‌



Mirror Football delves into the latest stories coming out of Anfield...

Wirtz's biggest issue

Steven Gerrard claimed that Florian Wirtz's total lack of confidence is behind his inconsistency at Liverpool. The 23-year-old has failed to live up to expectations at Anfield since joining the club in a £116million deal last year.

Wirtz had his best performance of the season in midweek, assisting Bradley Barcola's second goal of the game, but he remains without one himself in the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Chelsea leading race for £100m-rated Alex Scott as Bournemouth face January decision READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola learns key lesson as Bradley Barcola makes Liverpool mark in goal fest READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The former Reds captain opened up about Wirtz's situation on the Stick to Football podcast, but insisted the German star can still come good at Liverpool. "I am not denying that he is underperforming and that we should have seen a lot more given his price tag," Gerrard said.

"But I just think there is a chance, and it's happened previously, that players can turn it around. I think he's got the talent to turn it around, but his confidence is shot at the moment."

‌



View 3 Images Florian Wirtz remains without a goal this season (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Iraola reveals dilemma

Liverpool's six-goal offering in Austria included four goal contributions from defenders Jeremie Frimpong and Ronald Araujo. The Dutchman notched two assists and a goal, while the summer signing netted his first goal for the club.

Five of Araujo's nine appearances have come at right-back due to Frimpong's weaknesses in defence and Conor Bradley being sidelined due to injury. However, they played alongside each other on Wednesday and Iraola admitted the stark contrast between their styles at right-back makes a marked difference in how the rest of the team performs.

‌



View 3 Images Andoni Iraola opened up about an issue with Liverpool's selection (Image: AP Photo/Denes Erdos)

He said after full-time: "It is clear the difference in the team when we play with Jeremie and Ronald. The demands we put on the players are completely different. Jeremie helps us more offensively as he can arrive in the final third positions, but that does leave more space behind because you can’t cover everything.

"Ronald is the opposite because he is more comfortable defending as a centre-back, but he doesn’t give us the runs in behind, overlaps, or the options that Jeremie does. It is about us seeing what we need from the game, but we need to keep them both in a good place so we have those options during games. Until we recover Conor, I am happy to have those options."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Bayern Munich transfer interest emerges as club forced to issue statement
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Bayern Munich transfer interest emerges as club forced to issue statement

Arsenal have been linked with a new transfer target ahead of Mikel Arteta's side facing Nottingham Forest in the Premier League

View 2 Images Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is preparing his team for Premier League action this weekend (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Arsenal are preparing to face Nottingham Forest on Sunday but off-the-pitch matters have also captured attention ahead of the weekend. Mikel Arteta's side will look to put pressure on league leaders Manchester City as they seek to retain the Premier League title.

‌



‌



The Arsenal boss could be without several of his players through injury after both midfielder Martin Zubimendi and full-back Piero Hincapie picked up ankle issues during a cool down after last week’s win over Leeds. The pair join Christos Tzolis and William Saliba on the club’s injury list.

‌



The latter has been a notable absentee for Arteta’s team after sustaining a back problem during the World Cup. The centre-back has returned to individual training but his manager has been coy about when Saliba, who was absent from the team’s squad photo, may be back in contention.

‌



The club’s defensive injuries have led to links with Bayern Munich star Kim Min-jae ahead of the January transfer window. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding the Gunners.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources .

‌



Fresh transfer target discussed

Bayern centre-back Kim is reportedly on Arsenal’s radar as the team contend with injured defenders. The Gunners have been without Saliba so far this season, prompting Cristhian Mosquera and new signing Ezri Konsa to slot in for the France international.

Despite the Premier League champions’ strength in depth at the back, CFBayernInsider reports that Kim is on the Gunners’ list of targets and has been discussed by the club. It is added that Arsenal’s head of scouting Maurizio Micheli previously signed Kim from Fenerbahce for Napoli in 2022.

The report details that Arsenal are potentially looking to make defensive signings in the January window and Kim may be available for the right price. The South Korean international has fallen to third in the Bayern pecking order, behind Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah, but did not wish to leave the German club this summer.

‌



Kim joined Bayern in 2023 and is under contract until 2028. The 29-year-old has made six appearances in all competitions this term, starting two of the club’s five league games.

View 2 Images Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae has been linked with Arsenal (Image: S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images)

Arsenal forced to issue statement

Arsenal were quick to ease concerns after Saliba failed to appear in the team’s official squad photo. The 2026/27 photo was taken at the club’s Sobha Realty Training Centre on Wednesday and posted on social media.

Article continues below

Saliba was not pictured alongside his teammates, with the club issuing a message to clear up confusion over the defender’s absence. Shortly after posting the photo, Arsenal stated: “Due to a medical appointment, William Saliba was not available this afternoon.”

The centre-back recently returned to individual training and Arteta spoke positively about his recovery but refused to set a timeline for his comeback. When asked if Saliba could return after the November international break, the Arsenal manager said: “I don't know, we're still talking about weeks, and when that happens it's very different whether he would play just before, or after that, because it's a very specific injury that he processes."

Sports.title: 'We've moved on' - Martinez in Man Utd squad to face Leeds
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez is set to be in Manchester United’s squad for Sunday's trip to Leeds United after his incendiary post-match outburst earlier this week.

Head coach Michael Carrick insisted he was "telling the truth" that the club has moved on in a press conference dominated by questions about Martinez after he called out director of football Jason Wilcox over a lack of investment in the transfer window.

Martinez, whose outspoken comments came after Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox. CEO Omar Berrada and Carrick, on Thursday before making an apology over the timing and public nature of his criticism.

Asked about Martinez on Friday ahead of Sunday's trip to Leeds, live on Sky Sports, Carrick said: "He's released his statement and realised he made a mistake.

"That's enough for us to move on with. From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done is enough to move on."

Carrick also confirmed that Martinez, who was reportedly fined as a punishment, would be travelling with the squad to Elland Road.

'I'm telling you the truth' - Carrick insists case closed

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

United's record goalscorer Wayne Rooney, who was Carrick's teammate at Old Trafford for more than a decade, said Martinez's comments had the potential to "rip the dressing room apart".

But Carrick, who is under mounting pressure with United on a five-game winless run, was adamant that the spirit of the group remains strong ahead of two tough away games against Leeds and Como.

Questioned why people would believe that with everything that has been said, Carrick added: "There's a lot of people saying a lot of things. Pros and ex-pros, that doesn't mean they know what's going on here.

"The players totally believe me. Just because people talk on the outside doesn't make it the truth. I am telling you the truth.

"The squad [on Friday] was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while, actually. It's plain and simple. It's not affected [the spirit], I'm telling you. We're in a good place."

He added: "As a group we've moved on. It's really not a drama for the group. The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits.

"It was pretty simple. We understood the situation. Licha understood he made a mistake. We have a really good feeling from the club. We can see in the group we want to do something with this situation.

"We've moved on. Genuinely. There is a freshness about the group."

Should Wilcox speak more often in public?

Martinez directly called out United's "technical director" in his post-match interview in Madrid, putting director of football Wilcox firmly in the top spotlight.

Since replacing Dan Ashworth to assume his current role, Wilcox has only done one extended interview, which came nearly a year ago after a run of three wins, and it was with the club's in-house media.

Asked if Wilcox, who has been criticised by fans for his lack of communication, should speak up more, Carrick said: "I don't think it's for me to say whether he should or not.

"I've got no problem sitting here, talking to you guys and leading the group, leading the team, leading the football club from this position. We're all in it together."

Analysis: Carrick handled situation well – but talking needs to be on the pitch

Sky Sports' Pete Gill:

"As a player, Michael Carrick was unflustered and calm. In Friday's press conference, he has been no different.

"He offered a straight bat to the inevitable questions about Martinez and only seem ruffled when it was suggested that he needed a result against Leeds - "we need a result" interjected the United head coach.

"Ultimately, though, United's talking needs to be on the pitch. And if there was one jarring note in the presser, it was Carrick's insistence that all is well at United that stood out.

"United are not, in his words, "in a good place". They can only be if they arrest their alarming slump in form, starting at Leeds on Sunday."

'Doubts over Martinez future'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dave Reed updates fans on which Manchester United players will be out of contract in the summer.

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

Manchester United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Sky Sports News has been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Sports.title: 'One of the best weeks of my life' - Kartal feeling fresh ahead of Wuhan semi-finals
Sports.content:
British star Sonay Kartal says she is due a couple of new tattoos after enjoying "one of the best weeks" of her life by reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open.

Kartal claimed one of the biggest wins of the career as she beat world No 6 Elina Svitolina on Friday.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, seized her first match-point opportunity to complete another stunning victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open quarter-final between Sonay Kartal and Elina Svitolina

Kartal, who made her breakthrough by reaching the fourth round of last year's Wimbledon, advanced to the last four of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.

"Definitely one of the best weeks of my life," she said. "You could say, results-wise, that is definitely the best for me so far.

"I'm very happy to be backing up the level each day. I think it's pretty easy for a player to come out and play a blinder for just one match. I'm very happy that I managed to keep the consistency. I've got some of my best wins this week."

Kartal added she is due a couple of new tattoos. She had one booked in but was forced to make a last-minute cancellation after heading to the Billie Jean King Cup with Great Britain.

Asked if she would get one done if she won in Wuhan, the Brighton-based star replied with a smile: "I would have to have a think. I can't make a rush decision."

Back injury and protected ranking

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the match between Kartal and Jasmine Paolini

Kartal, using a protected injury ranking to play, has previously peaked at No 44 in the rankings and started the Wuhan Open at No 170, but she has skyrocketed 83 places to No 87 in the live rankings with her run to the semi-finals.

She is assured of adding 390 points to her total, meaning she is guaranteed to be the new British No 2 behind Katie Boulter (No 58), moving past Fran Jones (No 98) and Emma Raducanu (No 109).

Having missed more than six months, Kartal admitted she would not be able to walk without some form of pain but found it "pretty smooth sailing" after a couple of months.

And now she is feeling fit and healthy again.

What is a protected ranking?

A protected ranking is a provision that allows tennis players to enter tournaments using a frozen or averaged ranking after a long-term absence from the sport



A protected ranking can only be used to gain automatic entry into a tournament's main draw or qualifying rounds



On the WTA Tour, it is typically based on their exact ranking at the official start of their absence



The player must be physically sidelined and unable to compete in any tennis event for a minimum of six months



A protected ranking is not permanent. It is only valid for a specific timeframe or a limited number of tournaments



"My back is great," Kartal said. "I wouldn't have made the return if it wasn't great.

"I think the body is feeling it having not played a tennis match for six months, and when you're on tour, your body gets used to the aches and pains and demands of matches each week. I'm definitely more sore in areas.

"I think if there's one thing I've learned in the six months - it's sometimes patience is the better option. And the heroic thing to do is not play every single week. I feel great and I'm ready to get going for the remainder of the year."

The challenge of Ostapenko

She'll next face Latvian world No 34 Jelena Ostapenko, who beat Diana Shnaider in her quarter-final.

The pair have met twice before, with both matches coming on grass in the space of six days in June 2025 - Ostapenko won at Eastbourne, but then Kartal came out on top at Wimbledon.

Image: Jelena Ostapenko faces Kartal for a spot in the Wuhan Open final

"I've enjoyed playing her," said Kartal. "I think we're equal on the scoreboard. But I think there's a level of respect that she shows me.

"She's playing great this week having had a few tough matches, so she's definitely on form. I'm excited for another battle.

"I feel it's going to be a completely different game style to the people that I've played the past few days. I'm ready for a long one if it's needed."

Sports.title: Arteta: Arsenal will take new team photo including Saliba
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta says Arsenal will take a new team photograph including William Saliba after the defender's surprise absence from the one published this week.

Arsenal supporters were left baffled by Saliba's omission from the official 2026/27 picture as the club revealed he was unavailable to attend due to a medical appointment.

Saliba is yet to play this season because of a back injury but the 25-year-old remains a key player, having made 184 appearances for the club, which heightened the intrigue around his omission.

"What happened was that we have tried to do that picture three times already and we had to cancel it last minute for different reasons," explained Arteta ahead of Arsenal's away trip to Nottingham Forest, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

"We had some commercial obligations, we had some people who flew over to do that, so we decided to do that picture.

"We will have another picture with the whole family.

"Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we'll announce that as well."

Arteta replied "yes" when asked to confirm that Arsenal planned to retake the picture and insisted Saliba was "completely fine" about the situation.

He said: "Well, it wasn't in his hands. But Willy is normally happy about everything. He knows how loved he is. He was taking some banter from the players and he is completely fine."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Predictions for this weekend's games on Sky with Kevin Davies, who makes some bold calls

Saliba resumed training on the grass earlier this month and Arteta added that he is progressing positively, with a scan scheduled for next week as he edges closer to a return to action.

"I think next week we have another MRI with him to see how the healing process is going," he said.

"But every sign so far has been very, very positive. It will be good to have him."

Arteta added that Martin Zubimendi is in contention to return against Forest after injuring himself in the warm-down following the Leeds game along with Piero Hincapie, who will be out for another one or two weeks.

Christos Tzolis, meanwhile, underwent an MRI scan on Thursday to assess his recovery from the hamstring injury he suffered on international duty with Greece.

"It's progressing really well," Arteta added of the winger. "Another one that hopefully we can have back in a few weeks."

Arteta 'far from happy' about photo gaffe

Sky Sports News reporter Gary Cotterill at Arsenal's training ground:

When it comes to facing tricky questions, Mikel Arteta has things easier right now than his counterparts on both sides of Manchester, but it's not all plain sailing at Arsenal.

In a week of warm-down injuries, incomplete team photos and job-cut announcements, the Arsenal manager knew there would be some tricky issues to deal with.

As if that wasn't enough, the off-field issues continued as the tough questions started.

A few minutes into the news conference the microphone under Mikel's mouth stopped working.

It meant his answer underlining that Arsenal are no longer the set piece kings - 20 of their 21 goals so far this season have come from open play - had to be repeated.

Sports.title: Why Henderson-Caicedo axis is the midfield solution for Chelsea after James blow
Sports.content:
"They give presence." Xabi Alonso sat up a little more in his press conference seat and pointed to his chest. "They give stability."

Chelsea have made an erratic start under the Spaniard but last Saturday the midfield partnership of Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson brought control and balance to the team in a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth.

"For me, it's fundamental that we get that area strong," Alonso told the media after that game, well aware of how Chelsea's excellent attacking play in the early weeks of the season has been undermined by a leaky defence, exposed in end-to-end contests.

The answer lies in the middle of the pitch.

Alonso, a star central midfielder himself during his playing days, has used a variety of players and combinations in that area through his first six Premier League games.

Chelsea midfields in the Premier League this season vs Bournemouth: Neto, Henderson, Caicedo, Chavarria (3-4-2-1)

Neto, Henderson, Caicedo, Chavarria (3-4-2-1) vs Brentford: Neto, Henderson, Barco, Chavarria (3-4-2-1)

Neto, Henderson, Barco, Chavarria (3-4-2-1) vs Hull: Lavia, James (4-2-3-1)

Lavia, James (4-2-3-1) vs Arsenal: Neto, James, Lavia, Hato (3-4-2-1)

Neto, James, Lavia, Hato (3-4-2-1) vs Brighton: Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato (3-4-2-1)

Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato (3-4-2-1) vs Fulham: Gusto, James, Lavia, Hato (3-4-2-1)

Reece James has been a regular selection. But the Chelsea captain's knee surgery, which is going to keep him out for the coming months, necessitates Alonso settling on a different option.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Xabi Alonso says influential Reece James injury won't affect Chelsea's January transfer plans.

The Caicedo-Henderson combination could be the partnership he takes forward, with Everton away up next. They showed their character and quality last time out.

Caicedo's return to fitness was always going to be a key element to the solution. The Ecuadorian had been limited to just 14 minutes of football this season before playing 72 against Bournemouth.

His impact on the team was clear at Stamford Bridge. He topped the tackles won and interceptions metric for Chelsea, and also used the ball efficiently, posting a 96.4 percent passing accuracy, the best of any starter from either side.

Image: Moises Caicedo's stats vs Bournemouth

"With him, we have a better midfield area," said Alonso plainly.

"When you are better in the middle, you have a more complete team, and I think that is something to build around.

"He's going to be a key player for us. We knew that, and we have seen today."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Chelsea and Bournemouth.

But if Caicedo delivered his expected attributes, Henderson delivered a couple of sensational surprises, whipping in two brilliant long-range goals. His influence with his all-round game - at 36 years of age - may be an even bigger surprise to his critics.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jordan Henderson and Cole Palmer reveal how they came to the decision for Henderson to take the free-kick against Bournemouth that ended up flying into the top corner.

The former Liverpool captain's controversial switch to Al Ettifaq in 2023 and subsequent struggles at Ajax seemed to be spelling the end to his career. But after Brentford brought him back to these shores, England boss Thomas Tuchel saw the situation differently, taking Henderson to the World Cup.

Now Alonso is giving him an even more prominent role.

"We signed him for everything - if he's able to score two beauties, as today, we are more than happy for him," smiled Alonso when asked about the player of the match.

Image: Jordan Henderson was named player of the match in Chelsea's win over Bournemouth

Henderson was everywhere against Bournemouth. He covered 11.9km, the most of any player, despite setting the record for being the oldest Chelsea player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game.

"Apart from the goals, he's done many, many good things," said Alonso.

"A very 'midfielder' performance, always being involved in the action, always giving solutions to the team-mates."

Follow Everton vs Chelsea with Sky Sports We'll keep you up to date with Everton vs Chelsea on Saturday; kick-off 12.30pm. Stay across the game with our live blog for team news, in-game updates and analysis. Then from 5.15pm you can watch FREE match highlights on the Sky Sports website and App.

The wider impact was crucial. Alonso described Chelsea's display as "a very complete performance" and said Henderson and Caicedo bring the best out of players around them.

"Both, in terms of qualities, are different, in terms of the positioning as well. I think that they help each other well," said Alonso.

"And they give presence, they give stability. You know that they are going to be the ones that are going to be helping the rest, not just for his qualities, because they understand the game, they can play in shorter spaces, but as well, defensively, they give good balance."

Alonso made a point of referencing Romeo Lavia and Valentin Barco in his post-match assessment last Saturday and he did the same in his pre-Everton press conference on Friday. They are two players who have also been deployed in central midfield this term.

Squad depth is going to be important, even if Chelsea are not involved in Europe this season. But the Caicedo-Henderson axis could be his winning formula.

Everton away on Saturday will be the next test to see if the pair can continue to bring cohesion and control to Alonso's Chelsea.

Sports.title: Is Mahomes entering Brady-like second half of career?
Sports.content:
Have you forgotten about the career Patrick Mahomes is putting together?

NFL fans and media tend to adopt a short-term view.

The hottest new star takes the headlines over the productive veteran. Those who win too much become villains, and those who beat them are heroes. Before you know it, the new heroes are winning too much for our liking.

Mahomes has been through this story arc: the incredible, exciting first season as the AFC quarterback who could finally knock Tom Brady off his throne. The Super Bowl win that rejuvenated a franchise. Then came the flag-drawing, fan-ire-inciting run to an almost 'three-peat' that turned most of the NFL world against the Mahomes/Travis Kelce/Taylor Swift media storm.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Kansas City's Week One win against Denver

Mahomes was too good for too long. "You either die a hero, or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain," or something along those lines.

Then last season happened. Career low in quarterback rating. Career high in sack rate. A losing season (heaven forbid) along with a season-ending ACL tear. Josh Allen is Superman, Brock Purdy has reached a new level, Trevor Lawrence is breaking out. Is Mahomes... under the radar?

A special career start

Let's remind ourselves of Mahomes' first eight seasons as an NFL starter.

Patrick Mahomes' record by season Season Record Playoffs Other 2018/19 12-4 Lost AFC Championship NFL MVP 2019/20 11-3 Won Super Bowl 2020/21 14-1 Lost Super Bowl 2021/22 12-5 Lost AFC Championship 2022/23 14-3 Won Super Bowl NFL MVP 2023/24 10-6 Won Super Bowl 2024/25 15-1 Lost Super Bowl 2025/26 6-8 Missed playoffs Tore ACL Week 15 2026/27 4-0 ?

It is unprecedented. Not since the second half of Tom Brady's remarkable career has a quarterback and team achieved this consistent level of success.

As mentioned above, we are always drawn to the hottest new star in the league, and Mahomes' first season was arguably the greatest campaign by a quarterback in their first as a starter.

After sitting behind veteran Alex Smith in his rookie year, Mahomes exploded with 5,097 passing yards and 50 touchdowns in 2018. Only Peyton Manning had reached those marks in a single season before, and Mahomes was named MVP.

Image: Mahomes lifts the Lombardi Trophy in 2020

It didn't take long for him to get his first Lombardi Trophy as part of a stretch that saw the Chiefs reach seven consecutive AFC Championship games, make five Super Bowls and win three.

But from new, exciting and lovable, the narrative (and style of play) changed along the way.

After that 50-TD campaign, there was a stretch where Mahomes looked unstoppable, culminating in another 5,000-yard year in 2022, with an MVP award and Super Bowl win to boot.

From 2023 onwards, his passing numbers dropped. He stopped going deep (at least compared to before). The defense also got better and although it didn't stop the team's success, we'd become used to 'video game numbers'.

It was widely celebrated when the Chiefs fell off last season, as if other teams finally knew their chance had come. That might not last long.

Will post-ACL Mahomes match Brady's 'second career'?

Image: Tom Brady defeated Mahomes in Super Bowl LV

There is a notion that you can take the first half of Tom Brady's career and that would be enough to put him in the Hall of Fame. You could take the second half alone and say the same. Put them together and there's no denying he is the best to do it.

Somewhere in that first half, Brady tore his ACL and missed an entire campaign. The Patriots lost their opening playoff games in both seasons after he returned. Would he ever return to his Super Bowl-winning ways?

Eight seasons and eight AFC Championship appearances followed, with three Vince Lombardi Trophies and two Super Bowl losses along the way.

Safe to say he didn't 'lose it' after the injury.

Brady was 31 when he suffered that season-ending knee injury. Mahomes is 31 in his comeback season this year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Chiefs topped the Colts in overtime in Week Two

From a talent perspective, there is already an argument to be made that no one tops Mahomes. Has there ever been a better start to a career? What separates Brady is his longevity: 23 years in the league, 48 games in the playoffs, seven Super Bowl wins.

Mahomes needs to play another decade and double his Super Bowl victories to even get close to Brady's career, but if the start of this season is anything to go by, he is right back to his very best.

His quarterback rating (106.2) is at its best since 2020, his TD rate (7.0) is the closest to 2018, and his yards per attempt of 8.8 fits in more with his early-career run than recent seasons. He is playing aggressive and clean.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mahomes and company topped the Raiders in their most recent outing

The Chiefs are 4-0 and putting up 412 yards per game (second-highest in the league) and 29.5 points per game (fifth). There's no denying the addition of running back Kenneth Walker is a big factor in the reinvigoration of the Chiefs' attack, but it that is also allowing Mahomes to be himself.

The Bills, Ravens and Jaguars have started out hot at 4-1, yet the Chiefs are the only team to remain undefeated in the conference (albeit with the benefit of a bye). Are we kidding ourselves that anyone other than them will represent the AFC in SoFi Stadium in February?

Kansas City will aim to go 5-0 when they face their divisional rival and 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday, live on Sky Sports, and don't be surprised if the winning doesn't stop anytime soon.

Sports.title: Carrick includes Martínez in squad; Maresca feels ‘no stress’; Watford sacking reports ‘fake news’: football – live
Sports.content:
38s ago 10.54 EDT Ipswich’s Gary O’Neill has revealed what he thinks of the situation regarding Manchester City’s Premier League future, and their appeal against guilty verdicts for breaching the league’s financial regulations. And it is, to summarise, nothing much: double quotation mark I suppose any off-field situation, not just this one, that rumbles on or takes a while, everyone involves in the competition wants sorted, because we want everything to be decided on the pitch. You just want clarity. But as far as I’m concerned, it’s so far away from a priority for me to even know or care what is happening at Manchester City. Share

7m ago 10.48 EDT An update to the story about Spain’s football federation being fined for some supporters’ Islamophobic chants: the RFEF are to take the case to CAS. This just in from Reuters: “Throughout the proceedings, the RFEF has maintained that it acted immediately, diligently and effectively from the moment it became aware of the incidents,” a high-ranking official in the RFEF told Reuters. “Furthermore, the ⁠measures taken ensured that the chants were not repeated and that the spectators present ​in the stadium themselves expressed their ​disapproval of such behaviour.“ The official said ​the federation considered the sanctions particularly severe, arguing that comparable capacity restrictions had not ​been imposed automatically in more ‌serious cases or ​those involving previous disciplinary ​offences. Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment. The chants were detected by the RFEF’s monitoring systems and immediately reported to the match officials, the official said, adding that security was reinforced in the affected section of the stadium. “The Federation cooperated fully with the relevant authorities to identify those responsible.“ Share

19m ago 10.36 EDT Oliver Glasner has spoken ahead of Nottingham Forest’s game against Arsenal on Sunday, and has revealed exactly what he thinks about the Gunners. To summarise: they are good. double quotation mark Huge credit to Mikel Arteta and to Arsenal. It’s now a team that has been built over years, at the beginning finding a core and then always adding the right pieces. It’s not only the quality it’s the mentality. In every game this season they’re outrunning the opposition. The effort, the mindset Mikel created there is incredible and this makes it so tough to play against them. And of course they have so many world-class players they can react from the bench. This is what we are facing. The structure, how they are playing, everybody knows and analyses but the way they are executing it makes it so difficult. It’s a huge challenge. But on the other side that’s exactly what we need to improve our game, and to show that we are ready. Share

25m ago 10.29 EDT Mikel Arteta has explained why Arsenal took their official team photo this week without William Saliba, who had a doctor’s appointment when the photographer turned up: View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s men’s first-team squad for the 2026-27 season. Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images double quotation mark What happened was that we tried to do that picture three times already and we had to cancel it last minute for different reasons, and we had some commercial obligations so we decided to do it. We will retake the picture with the whole family. Willy, normally he’s happy about everything and he knows how loved he is and he is completely fine. Share

33m ago 10.21 EDT Spain have been fined and told to partially close the stadium hosting their next international friendly after Islamophobic chanting was heard during a match against Egypt earlier this year, writes the Press Association. A section of Spain fans chanted “whoever doesn’t jump is a Muslim” during the friendly in Barcelona on March 31, with anti-discrimination messages displayed on the big screens and announcements made at half-time urging fans to stop the chants. The Spanish federation (RFEF) sought to have the disciplinary process thrown out, in part on the grounds that the word Muslim is the accepted term for a follower of Islam. However, Fifa’s disciplinary committee concluded the chants “clearly use religious identity as a means of distinguishing and discriminating against the opposing side” and said a reasonable and objective observer would see the word “Muslim” used in this context “as a marker of exclusion and ridicule”. The RFEF has been fined $20,000 (£15,000) and ordered to close 15% of the stadium for their next men’s senior team friendly, or fill that percentage of seats with community or special interest groups, such as families, students and anti-discrimination organisations, subject to Fifa’s approval. Spain star Lamine Yamal said at the time he found the chants “intolerable” as a Muslim himself, adding: “I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people. Football is to be enjoyed and encouraged, not to disrespect people for who they are or what they believe in.” Share Updated at 10.22 EDT

The sanctions relate to incidents at the RCDE Stadium near Barcelona, home of Espanyol, where some Spain fans chanted, “Who doesn’t jump is a Muslim” during a World Cup warmup ⁠match. After the second occurrence ​of the chant, the stadium ‌announcer issued a ‌warning and the scoreboard displayed a message against discriminatory behaviour. The Spain ‌winger Lamine Yamal, who is Muslim, condemned the chants at the time, describing them as disrespectful and intolerable and calling those responsible “ignorant and racist“. Spanish police launched an investigation the next day while world governing body Fifa later started disciplinary ‌proceedings against the Spanish soccer federation (RFEF). The RFEF argued that the word “Muslim” was “neither insulting nor pejorative“, adding the ​fans’ conduct should be assessed under Fifa’s Article 17, which covers political, ideological, religious or offensive messages, rather than Article 15, which deals with discrimination and racist abuse. However, Fifa’s’s disciplinary committee ⁠rejected that argument, saying Article 15 does not require ​the explicit use ​of a slur and ​that a term can be discriminatory when used ​in context as “an ‌insult, taunt, ​or marker ​of inferiority“. Fifa fined the RFEF and ordered the closure of at least 15% of available seats for Spain’s next friendly. Sports.title: Infantino told by top Fifa figures to scrap or depoliticise peace prize after Trump furore
Sports.content:
Donald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leader awarded the Fifa peace prize after Gianni Infantino was told at Thursday’s meeting of the Fifa council to make major changes or scrap the controversial award.

The Guardian has learned that several council members demanded the award be abolished and others called for the prize to be depoliticised, with Fifa’s football social responsibility committee to make a recommendation before the next council meeting in Doha on 16 December.

Infantino announced the peace prize had been handed to the social responsibility committee at the start of Thursday’s meeting. Council members returned to the subject later in a series of questions about possible conflict of interests at Fifa.

There is a strong view among council members that the peace prize in its current form is tainted by association with Trump, with some raising concerns that the US president could object and create a diplomatic storm if he does not like the identity of its next recipient.

Fifa’s 22-person social responsibility committee is dominated by representatives from countries loyal to Infantino so abolition may be avoided on the grounds it would represent a humiliation for the Fifa president, although there is a widespread acceptance that change is required.

One council member told the Guardian the most likely outcome discussed is the reinvention of the peace prize as an award for an individual within football who has delivered exceptional work promoting social harmony and responsibility, with a provision stating it cannot be given to a politician.

Article two of Fifa’s statutes prohibits any political or governmental interference in football, one of several reasons why honouring Trump last year triggered such a backlash from many members.

Fifa announced the creation of its peace prize last November with a stipulation that it would “reward individuals who have taken exceptional and extraordinary actions for peace and by doing so have united people across the world”.

Trump was given the award at the men’s World Cup draw in Washington last December, with Infantino presenting the US president with a golden trophy, a medal and a certificate, but the process behind his selection has never been made public.

The social responsibility committee is expected as part of its review to set strict parameters for any surviving award, and to provide details of a nomination and selection procedure.
