Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League table is taking shape for 2026-27. The defending champions, Manchester City, have five wins from five games but more intriguing stories lie elsewhere. Why are Arsenal struggling, who is performing better than results suggest, and in which way are two promoted teams smashing expectations? Here are three key data points.

Arsenal have two major flaws

Opta made Arsenal third favourites to win the WSL before a ball was kicked. Their win at Brighton combined with Chelsea’s draw against Aston Villa in week one meant Renée Slegers’ side rose to narrow favourites. The four games since, from which Arsenal took two points, have torpedoed their title chances.

One reason for their slump is a continuation of a problem from last season. The stats section of our Arsenal pre-season preview highlighted draws in 2025-26 that they deserved to win based on expected goals. That trend has continued this season with positive xG margins of 2.2 and 1.2 in their home games against Crystal Palace (0-0) and Manchester United (1-1) respectively.

Had Smilla Holmberg not scored with her only shot of the campaign in the 95th minute against United, the situation would be even worse. While players inevitably have a small sample of shots at this point, Arsenal’s finishing woes are a collective problem. Only Lisa Baum and Alessia Russo have also scored, with the latter 1.28 goals below her expected goal tally. Scoring three goals in the international break may help Russo’s confidence.

A physical deficiency may also be contributing to Arsenal’s struggles. Gradient Sports award players an athleticism score, a single metric which incorporates stamina, explosiveness and game context. There are 125 WSL players with a score who have played at least 270 minutes this season. Steph Catley is Arsenal’s highest-ranked player, at 31st, and their only representative above 59th. Every other club has at least two players in the top 50, with Chelsea having five. West Ham possessing seven shows this is not a decisive factor in success but Arsenal fans may wonder whether their side need to increase the physical intensity.

Brighton are ones to watch

Brighton were predicted by Opta to finish seventh. As they are ninth, that forecast looks reasonable enough. Yet the underlying data suggests they deserve to be third, 0.1 expected points behind City. The Seagulls endured a case of wastefulness more extreme than anything Arsenal have offered up when they drew 1-1 with Villa. Despite an expected goal count of 3.17 to 0.03 in Brighton’s favour, Lynn Wilms’s 89th-minute goal robbed them of a victory.

Brighton also drew at Birmingham when leading the expected goals by 1.5 and missed four Opta-defined big chances in their 2-0 defeat at London City Lionesses. If they can make their dominance count, Brighton look capable of at least matching the fifth-place finish they secured in 2024-25.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Two promoted teams have an unexpected weapon

Productive pressing tends to belong to better teams. Opta’s high turnover metric records when a team win the ball to begin a new sequence of open-play possession within 40m of the opposition goal. If you sort the 2025-26 WSL by the number of high turnovers that led to shots, the five clubs with the fewest were those that finished in the bottom five. The standings were slightly more jumbled if you looked at the percentage of high turnovers that generated shots, to assess effectiveness and efficiency, but the top four teams for this finished in the WSL top five. Promoted London City had the fourth-least productive press by this measure.

Two of their successors are upending these correlations. Palace are third for shot-ending high turnovers, with 12, behind Chelsea (17) and Tottenham (15). The percentage of their possession regains in the final 40m that led to shots is the highest in the division (33.3%), with their fellow promoted side Birmingham (28.6%) next in line.

The West Midlands club are tied with Tottenham for most goals from high turnovers, on three (while Palace have two). Birmingham’s goals were all scored by Océane Hurtré, helping propel her to joint-first in the golden boot race, with five goals.

The 22-year-old French attacker won the ball for two of the three high-turnover goals, including one at Manchester City. Hurtré’s others came in the first and eighth minutes of matches against Palace and Brighton respectively, illustrating the benefit that pressing opponents early can bring.

Sports.title: Álvaro Arbeloa’s push to make Fulham free-flowing is floundering already
Sports.content:
Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions.

Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices.

The worrying shift under Arbeloa was evident during Fulham’s collapse against Ipswich last weekend. The west Londoners were 1-0 up and looking good for their first league win of the season when Arbeloa weakened his midfield by replacing Shea Charles with Manuel Ángel in the 70th minute.

It was a strange way to shut up shop. Charles is physically imposing, has impressed since joining from Southampton and was doing well alongside Sander Berge. The 22-year-old Ángel is 5ft 7in, was making his Premier League debut and has little experience of senior football. Ipswich’s comeback to win 2-1 was not a surprise, particularly when Arbeloa’s other rejigs included bringing on Rodrigo Muniz and switching from a 4-2-3-1 system to a flat 4-4-2 in an attempt to defend the lead.

The subsequent floundering felt inevitable. Emile Smith Rowe, another late substitute, was slow to close down Abdoul Ouattara when the Ipswich right-back equalised. Fulham have dropped eight points from winning positions. They are managing games badly and their physical shortcomings were exposed by Ipswich, whose winner came from a poorly defended free-kick and left Fulham in last place before facing Hull at home on Saturday.

Arbeloa needs a win. Relegation fears are growing and there are whispers that the Spaniard’s job is under threat. Fulham had a tricky start – they have already faced Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United – but the Ipswich game was supposed to mark a turning point. It was the first of three consecutive meetings with the promoted sides and, with Coventry, Hull and Ipswich surpassing expectations, it is easy to see Fulham’s aim to move to a more expansive style under Arbeloa backfiring.

Questions have to be asked over the decision by the Khan family to appoint someone whose experience of management was limited to an interim spell in charge of Real Madrid last season. Fingers will be pointed at the succession planners. Tony Khan, director of football and son of patriarch Shahid, has faced fierce criticism in the past. Silva offered stability. There was always a fear the project would fall apart once the Portuguese was gone.

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García struggled to make an impression at Ipswich. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

It does not help Arbeloa to lean on his time at the Bernabéu. He responded to a question about pressure after losing to Ipswich by saying: “I played for the best team in the world … I have coached the best team in the world.” But the optics are awkward. Arbeloa did not win anything as Madrid’s manager, his comments risk making it seem his current employers should be grateful to have him and eyebrows have been raised at three of the 43-year-old’s summer signings coming from his former club.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ángel, César Palacios and Gonzalo García were all promising young Real Madrid players, all share representation with Arbeloa and are now adapting to a new league. Palacios, an inventive passing midfielder, is 21 and Garcia, a nimble forward, is 22. They deserve to be given time, although the clock is ticking. García, signed for £40m, has one league goal from 18 shots and struggled against Ipswich, winning few duels and pressing ineffectively.

Supporters are growing restless. They wonder why Kevin, the Brazilian winger, is being used on the right rather than the left. They feel Arbeloa is chopping and changing too often. They worry about the team conceding costly late goals against Sunderland, Crystal Palace and United. Fulham were ridiculously open in their opening game, the barmy 3-2 defeat by Chelsea, and their expected goals against is 10.3 in six games. They have lost two of their main goalscorers, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, and are struggling to fill the void.

Equally there is an argument that Arbeloa needs time to implement a new style. There are suggestions some players are unsure about the manager’s tactics. Some stalwarts have been sidelined – Joachim Andersen, the influential Denmark centre-back, is not suited to playing a high line and has lost his spot to David Affengruber – but perhaps a refresh was required. Fulham have looked to lower the age of their squad, in part because of a need to comply with financial regulations, and there is nothing intrinsically wrong with trying to play more exciting football.

There have been encouraging spells. After flirting with European qualification in each of the past four seasons, only to fizzle out and finish in the bottom half, Fulham can be forgiven for wondering how to take the next step. At the same time the fear for supporters is that a club operating with one of the league’s smaller budgets have forgotten what it takes to survive. Silva’s teams could attack but were gritty and streetwise. At the moment Arbeloa looks naive. Fulham lost £45m in the past financial year and spent a lot on the Riverside Stand refurbishment. The Khans need Premier League survival. Arbeloa has big ideas but might not make it past this month without a huge improvement.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Henderson’s return to Merseyside

A lively reception awaits the former Liverpool midfielders Jordan Henderson and Xabi Alonso at Everton and, in the case of the former, any jeers can be considered an unintentional tribute. They will speak of what the 36-year-old is able to produce now as much as what, and where, he delivered in the past. With two goals and an assist against Bournemouth last Saturday, Henderson became the oldest player to contribute directly to three goals in a Premier League game, and demonstrated his role at Chelsea is not simply to elevate standards off the pitch. His midfield partnership with Moisés Caicedo gave Alonso’s team balance and enabled the front three of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer to flourish. Their confrontation against an Everton defence that had impressed this season, only to litter the draw at Hull with costly mistakes, will provide a stern test of the hosts’ unbeaten start and may well be dictated by the veteran behind them. Andy Hunter

Everton v Chelsea, Saturday 12.30pm (all times BST)

2 Bees a tougher test than Lask

Still unbeaten in the top flight, Brentford are being served well by their commitment to pragmatism. Keith Andrews’ side like to sit deep, close off the middle of the pitch and force opponents to play around them, while flooding the opposition box at set pieces and throw-ins allows them to create the chances from which most of their goals arrive. In spanking six past Lask, the Austrian champions, Liverpool showed how good they can be on the front foot, but they will face far less obliging hosts at the Gtech Community Stadium. If Andoni Iraola’s side can dominate the ball and move it quickly enough to penetrate Brentford’s rearguard, they could win comfortably. However, the Bees’ efforts to turn the afternoon into a saloon brawl and capitalise on dead-ball situations may help to maintain their unbeaten run. Barry Glendenning

Brentford v Liverpool, Saturday 3pm

3 García needs to find finishing touch

Gonzalo García has one league goal from 18 shots this season. The striker joined Fulham from Real Madrid in the summer and has looked promising in patches. García is 22 and capable of getting on the end of chances. He has an expected goals tally of 3.60 but is underperforming with his finishing. The challenge is to become more clinical. Fulham, bottom of the league, have six goals in six games and García is without a goal since scoring on his debut, against Chelsea. Álvaro Arbeloa has put a lot of faith in his fellow Spaniard. The head coach is under increasing pressure and winless Fulham need García to fire when they host Hull. Jacob Steinberg

Fulham v Hull, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Fulham’s Gonzalo García (second left) attempts a shot on goal against Manchester United. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

4 City still free-flowing after guilty verdict

Even when losing for the first time this season in Wednesday’s 4-2 Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain, Manchester City appeared the real deal as they rallied from 3-0 down after 32 minutes to give the European champions a scare. Enzo Maresca deserves credit for following Pep Guardiola serenely; his City, so far, are a free-flowing attacking machine and invigorating to watch. If not for the guilty verdict against the club for serious financial breaches of Premier League rules, the perma-twinkling Italian might be more widely lauded. Ipswich last won at City in the competition in November 2000: do not expect the statistic to change on Saturday. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

5 Jaissle should find his ‘inner Rafa’

Newcastle’s latest attempt to play vertical football left Matthias Jaissle’s side horizontal at Coventry on Monday night. That 4-1 defeat has prompted quite an inquest on Tyneside, where Jaissle could do without his players falling flat on their faces once more when Aston Villa visit St James’ Park. Jaissle maintains that his vertical football is the brand of high-octane, aggressive attacking that Newcastle’s hierarchy believes should become the club’s default, and is the way fans want to see the team play. That argument is not without validity but it is also worth remembering that, less than a decade ago, under Rafael Benítez’s charge, Newcastle often played a low block bolstered by three at the back, rarely took unnecessary risks and improved steadily. Admittedly resources were thinner then but the fans almost universally adored Benítez and were heartbroken when he eventually tired of Mike Ashley’s ownership and resigned. Quite apart from making his dislike for chaotic football plain, the Spaniard was a realist who knew a gung-ho approach would spell relegation. Granted, tactical fashions have changed, but Jaissle could do worse than slow things down a bit and search for his inner Rafa against Villa. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Aston Villa, Saturday 5.30pm

6 Eyes on Kluivert and Brobbey

With nine games each scheduled for the month between international breaks, Bournemouth v Sunderland will give an early indication of how both will cope during their first experience of such a relentless Thursday-Sunday autumnal grind. Sunderland are 17th, Bournemouth are 18th, and with seven points between them after six Premier League rounds, scaling similarly dizzy heights to last season already seems a lofty goal. For both clubs, European campaigns are far too much of an exciting novelty to be considered anything like a chore. In circumstances where squad depth is crucial, the returns of Justin Kluivert for the hosts and Brian Brobbey for the visitors will be welcomed by Marco Rose and Régis Le Bris. It would be no great surprise to see either Dutch international make a game-deciding contribution in what is already a six-pointer on the south coast. BG

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bournemouth v Sunderland, Sunday 2pm

7 Brighton must buck Palace trend

Brighton’s momentum appears unstoppable at the moment, although supporters will be wary of Sunday’s showdown against Crystal Palace given their recent history. They haven’t beaten Palace since a 4-1 thrashing at the Amex in February 2024, when Roberto De Zerbi was in charge, while Fabian Hürzeler managed only a point in four encounters with the Eagles under Oliver Glasner. Both are having to juggle European commitments this season and Brighton will start as heavy favourites against Pierre Sage’s side after their superb start to the campaign. Palace have big concerns in defence, but can the Frenchman defy the odds against the Premier League’s top scorers? Ed Aarons

Brighton v Crystal Palace, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Jaouen Hadjam fires home Brighton’s final goal in their 2-0 victory at Sunderland. Photograph: Craig Cowan/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

8 Carrick confronts old nemesis Farke

Michael Carrick has lost five of his past six technical-area duels with Daniel Farke. Indeed the only time Manchester United’s manager has bested his Leeds counterpart was in a League Cup tie during his Middlesbrough tenure. If such statistics are not sufficient to put Manchester United’s currently beleaguered manager off a trip to West Yorkshire on Sunday, there is a sense that Leeds are overdue a first victory at Elland Road since 2002 against their arch-enemies from across the Pennines. One thing is certain; it will be a typically raucous latter-day War of the Roses. But, right now, while the White Rose blooms, its red counterpart is wilting alarmingly. Will Carrick survive this latest meeting with a manager who, at Championship level during his Middlesbrough days, proved something of a nemesis? He will not care to remember that last January a 1-1 draw at Elland Road proved to be Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United. LT

Leeds v Manchester United, Sunday 2pm

9 Forest a genuine threat to champions

Despite losing 3-1 to Crystal Palace last weekend, Nottingham Forest played some excellent front-foot football only to be let down by extreme profligacy in front of goal and vulnerability to their hosts’ counterattacks. Oliver Glasner attributed his side’s defeat to karma upon his return to Palace, saying: “It was like I didn’t deserve to win at Selhurst Park, because the players did everything.” When they welcome Arsenal to the City Ground on Sunday they will give the champions plenty to ponder if they can play as well again. Mikel Arteta’s side were unconvincing for 65 minutes against Leeds last weekend and failed to impress until they brought on their heavy artillery about the same time against Lille on Tuesday. If one or both of Morgan Gibbs-White and Liam Delap can convert the kind of chances they missed at Selhurst Park, Forest have every chance of getting something. BG

Nottingham Forest v Arsenal, Sunday 4.30pm

10 On-song Coventry can pile angst on Spurs

The last time Tottenham hosted Coventry in the Premier League, Steffen Iversen, Les Ferdinand and Serhiy Rebrov scored in a comfortable 3-0 win. And while Spurs fans will almost certainly have envisaged a similar scoreline when the fixtures were announced, they will now be viewing Monday night’s fixture with even more than the usual amount of apprehension and dread. Like Tottenham, Coventry’s main problem until recently was an inability to convert chances, but in their demolition of Newcastle on Monday they visibly grew in confidence and swagger as four different players took the plaudits. While it’s taken a while and they may still struggle, through back-to-back wins Frank Lampard’s side have now announced themselves as a Premier League force to be reckoned with, which is something Tottenham haven’t managed in more than two years. BG

Sports.title: Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?
Sports.content:
It was like clockwork. Manchester United dropped points against Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical statistics to make points.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Manchester United.”

Physical metrics such as distance run and number of sprints are increasingly accessible and easy to understand, so have fallen into common use. It’s become a common theme that, when a big club fail to meet expectations, pundits and commentators look to their running metrics in search of one catch-all explanation. Liverpool and Chelsea were the targets of similar judgment last season.

But is it fair? How much of a correlation is there between a team running lots and that team being successful? While the numbers may not be complex at face value, answering this question is, which probably highlights that such metrics are so nuanced in a team sport that it probably isn’t best practice to tie too much significance to the topline figures.

The first way we can assess it is by comparing the Premier League table to the rankings of distance run and high-intensity distance. Yes, this is pretty simple and rudimentary, but it’s a place to start.

Last season’s Premier League table hardly mirrors the rankings for distance covered or high-intensity distance per game. Sure, Arsenal and Manchester City were high for overall distance, but the teams who came third to eighth had middling – at best – outputs in this respect.

The teams that finished in the top 10 averaged 4,363km over the season; the teams in the bottom 10 averaged 4,332km. In the grand scheme of things, a difference of 31km between those averages is rather small.

Again, there’s a slight difference between the average high-intensity distance for top-10 teams (338.7km) and those in the bottom 10 (328.4km), but we’re talking about an increase of 3%. Similarly when perusing data from this season, it’s difficult to see much of a link.

Looking at it in relation to the table does ignore that success is relative, however. Of course Burnley were not going to finish seventh in the table just because they came seventh in the distance rankings.

Instead, we can use the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions to give us an idea of what a successful campaign might have looked like for all clubs and whether there was a trend of overachieving teams running more.

Ten teams in the Premier League last season finished at least one place higher than their likeliest final place according to the Opta supercomputer in pre-season, and they averaged 4,369km over the season; the nine clubs that finished at least a place below their likeliest final position averaged 4,308km. So again, there is a difference, it’s just very small at 1.4%.

However, Sunderland (+13 places) and Manchester United (+9 places) weren’t in the top 10 for distance covered but exceeded the supercomputer’s expectations to a greater degree than any other team; Crystal Palace (-8 places) and Newcastle (-6 places) were in the top 10 for ground covered but among the most disappointing teams relative to pre-season expectations.

We can also look at expected points, a model that simulates the goals scored by each side in each match based on the xG value of all shots and then simulates every game 10,000 times to determine the proportion that the fixtures end with a win, draw or defeat. It isn’t perfect because it’s limited by the natural pitfalls of xG, but it does give a decent barometer of performance over a season.

The teams that ranked in the bottom half for distance covered last term exceeded their xPts totals by 0.38 on average, whereas the teams that ranked in the top half for that metric claimed 1.88 points fewer than their xPts on average. In short, then, it would appear there’s very little correlation between success (at least in the ways we’ve tried to depict it) over a long period and running distance.

But that doesn’t mean we didn’t find any correlation across the board. When analysing a host of physical metrics over the course of 2025-26, the one that showed the strongest link to the final standings was distance covered in possession.

It isn’t perfect but there is the hint of a correlation between more distance run on the ball and finishing higher up the table. That doesn’t necessarily mean a certain team finished high because they ran more in possession; it’s likely a reflection of that side having more of the ball owing to possessing better players. It still felt notable, though.

But perhaps the greatest link between physical metrics and success would appear to come on a game level, rather than over a full season. Since the start of last season, there have been 86 instances in the Premier League of a team covering at least 5km less than their opponents in a game. In those 86 matches, the side that covered at least 5km less have won 10 times, and seven of those were expected victories according to the Opta supercomputer. That’s a win rate of 11.6%.

Now, there are some obvious caveats here. Most importantly, 20 of these games involved at least one of the teams having a player sent off, and that can obviously have a big impact on both teams’ physical output.

Excluding those 20 games, we are left with eight wins for the team that covered at least 5km less than their opponents from 66 matches; that means the win rate shoots up from 11.6% to a massive … 12.1%.

When we change the parameters to look at instances when one team covered between 2.5km and 4.99km less than their opponents (but excluding games with a red card), the win rate does improve to 25.8%, though that’s still not especially high. The loss rate is 46%.

This suggests, then, some relationship between the most extreme examples of outrunning the opposition and winning. But we shouldn’t jump to conclusions; we can’t be absolutely sure the additional running is any more decisive than a whole range of other factors.

Physical metrics are also often closely tied to playing style, so one team’s output in a match can directly affect that of their opposition. The reason many like to lean on these figures is probably because, on the face of it, they are so simple to understand and very easy – rightly or wrongly – to attribute to effort, especially if you’re talking about a team that have lost.

But the fact there’s no strong correlation between distance run over a full season and success arguably suggests the answer over the long term isn’t to run your team into the ground, instead knowing when to up the intensity for maximum effect.

Jürgen Klopp perhaps summed it up best right at the start of his Liverpool reign. “We don’t have to run 115km per match to be successful. You don’t have to run like crazy if you have the ball. It is only the start. We must know how to turn the screws in the right moment; better thinking, better timing. But if we play a much better team and you are not ready to run more than them, then you are crazy.”

Pep Guardiola added to that in his final season at Manchester City. “It’s about when you have to run. Running just to run? I can go to the track and ask the marathon guys to play for us. It’s not about that, it’s when you have to do it. Last season when some players ran it was useless. The most important thing is the combination of both things.”

Intent and timing. When the going gets tough, intent potentially overrides all else in the eyes of the average fan. To be seen to be lacking effort, whether that reflects reality or not, is a cardinal sin in a struggling football team. But rarely is “just run more” the answer.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
Sports.content:
An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations.

Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.”

Bournemouth’s new head coach has described the chaos of English football, midfield areas that can resemble a rolling maul, but he has pledged to learn and adapt. “I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation,” Rose said. “If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it’s hard to beat us. That’s what we should take into the next game.”

Missing Eli Junior Kroupi so far this season, and lately Alex Scott, are regrettable problems within a small squad. Selling Scott for £80m in January, as has been speculated, speaks to the financial balancing act clubs such as Bournemouth must perform to progress. Following the 5-1 loss to Chelsea, Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Sunderland was prioritised in team selection though the second-half introduction of key men, including Rayan, proved decisive.

“Everyone deserves to play and it’s good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad,” said Rose, who revealed Smith had given a speech to his teammates after the loss at Stamford Bridge. “That’s my captain.”

View image in fullscreen Rayan doubles Bournemouth’s lead six minutes after coming off the bench. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Smith supplied the first proper chance. Marcus Tavernier, cutting inside, shanked that wide before a Ben Gannon-Doak cross from the byline saw Rodríguez misjudge the flight. The summer signing, still raw at 22, finds decent positions only for his touch to betray him. His penalty, following an inadvertent handball from Jon Gorenc Stankovic, was his first goal and should help his confidence.

Graz, fourth in this season’s Österreichische Bundesliga, hardly exuded ambition, a defensive trio often morphing into a shell-like five. Amid such squeezed space, after a corner, Bournemouth had the ball in the net, for what seemed an own goal though it had struck Bafode Diakité’s arm. Tavernier struck the outside of a post, before Graz at last began to advance. The away contingent celebrated a penalty, but Belmin Beganovic was shown a yellow card for simulation. Fabio Ingolitsch, the Graz coach and a Rose protege, spoke to his own team’s realities by saying: “Bournemouth is the team with the biggest market value in the Europa League.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another Smith cross supplied Evanilson’s goal, a header full of neck muscle looping off the angle for a first European goal celebrated in Boscombe. “Many more to come from him,” said Smith of the perpetual motion No 9. Graz fans sang whatever the game state, that being the continental way, but there became more to encourage them beyond the break. Simon Seidl’s shot whistled wide, Jürgen Heil struck a post before Jacob-Peter Hödl forced a remarkable reflex save from Djorde Petrovic on the rebound. The spectre of Premier League travails, where positive play has been unrewarded, loomed as Graz interchanges became crisper.

The 70th-minute triple introduction of Rayan, Justin Kluivert and Ryan Christie proved to be Rose’s successful method of locking down midfield and increasing his team’s attacking threat at the same time.

Rayan, a decent finisher when coming inside, snatched the contest from Austrian reach. Daniil Khudyakov, Graz’s Russian goalkeeper, first flapped at a corner and then got only a weak hand to the Brazilian’s drive through the proverbial forest of legs. Bournemouth’s European homecoming had been coupled with the victory the occasion had demanded.

Sports.title: Noah Sadiki stunner earns Sunderland dramatic late win against Torreense
Sports.content:
Three minutes into stoppage time Noah Sadiki hurdled a set of advertising hoardings, sprinted across a running track and hurled himself towards the ecstatic Sunderland fans.

Just as those supporters’ long-awaited party in Portugal had looked in peril of falling a little flat, the Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder capitalised on excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka to half-volley an eye-catching first goal for Régis Le Bris’s side.

It ensured a largely unconvincing Sunderland came from behind to secure a second straight Europa League win and their relief was evident as every outfield player followed Sadiki in vaulting those hoardings to join the celebrations.

“It was a difficult game,” said Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, with considerable understatement. “Torreense are a good team.”

With their home ground too small to accommodate European football, Leiria’s stadium stood in. It proved quite some substitute. An arena overlooked by a 12th-century castle constructed to defend this attractive medieval town against reconquest by the Moors created an imposing backdrop to Sunderland’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years.

Back in 1973 they were second division FA Cup holders. Torreense know the feeling. Having provoked widespread shock by beating Sporting to win the Portuguese Cup last spring, Luís Tralhão’s second-tier side relish their underdog status.

After winning at Lillestrøm last month, Torreense aimed to keep the surprises coming and duly left a heavily rotated Sunderland trailing at the break. Le Bris had left, among others, Xhaka, Le Fée and Nordi Mukiele on the bench ahead of Sunday’s vital Premier League trip to Bournemouth. This reshuffle permitted Luke O’Nien, a survivor from League One days, to captain Sunderland at a ground transformed into a sea of red and white. Although only 4,000 official tickets were allocated to the visitors more were readily available locally and estimates suggested the formal allocation had doubled.

As the sun dropped and the temperature fell from a high of 28C those fans watched a disjointed first half on Sunderland’s part. It seemed telling that the normally fairly impassive Le Bris looked distinctly, and unusually, irritated and frustrated at times.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland supporters enjoy their club’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years. Photograph: Ana Brigida/AP

Granted his humour was hardly helped by the referee’s penchant for detecting phantom Sunderland fouls but ominously Malick Fofana, a £30m summer signing from Lyon, struggled wide on the left. Ditto Nilson Angulo on the right wing.

Torreense, 15th in Portugal’s second tier might not have been threatening Robin Roefs’s goal but they succeeded in blocking and clearing pretty much everything that came their way. Indeed Tralhão’s defence looked almost as well fortified as that ancient castle towering over them.

Admittedly, midway through the first half Timur Tutierov, Sunderland’s centre-forward, thought he had headed the opener but that effort was disallowed due to shirt pulling on Omar Alderete’s part.

Then, with the interval fast approaching, Le Bris adopted hand-on-hips mode as Torreense reminded everyone precisely why they have built such a giantkilling reputation by scoring with their first shot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It came from centre-back Volnei Feltes. With Sunderland losing concentration and standing off, he was permitted to advance unopposed before cutting in on his right foot and sending a sublime 20-yard curler into the top corner.

Although Angulo forced Lucas Paes into a fine save he, like Fofana, was soon replaced as Le Bris made a quadruple substitution involving the introduction of Le Fée, Xhaka, Mukiele and Reinildo.

This infusion of quality left Torreense a little groggy and the midfielder Jules Ahoka –a highly impressive 20-year-old £8.5m summer buy from Royal Antwerp – was able to equalise by heading his first goal for Sunderland courtesy of Mukiele’s deft dink.

View image in fullscreen Jules Ahoka scores Sunderland’s first goal against Torreense. Photograph: Luis Loureiro/Shutterstock

When the lively Tutierov went down in the box, the referee immediately pointed to the spot. However, a linesman’s flag indicated an offside so it seemed there would be no penalty. Or at least not until the video assistant referee intervened – lengthily; the eventual conclusion was no offside, no foul and no penalty.

No matter; when Le Fée dinked a gorgeous ball into the box and Xhaka played it into Sadiki’s path, the scorer waited for it to drop across him before applying the expert finishing touch on the half-volley.

Sports.title: FIFA could scrap controversial Peace Prize won by Donald Trump after just one year
Sports.content:
FIFA could scrap controversial Peace Prize won by Donald Trump after just one year

FIFA could scrap their controversial Peace Prize just 12 months after creating the award, talkSPORT understands.

U.S president Donald Trump was the recipient of the inaugural award at the World Cup draw held in Washington DC last December.



2 Donald Trump was handed the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize in December 2025, with Infantino lavishing praise on him Credit: Getty

But a FIFA Council meeting held in Zurich on Thursday concluded that its football social responsibility committee will now decide what meets the conditions of an annual prize.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino awarded the Peace Prize to Trump ahead of the 2026 World Cup.

However, it was not signed off by the FIFA Council, the governing body’s decision makers.



FIFA launches new decision-making process

The changes will see former Inter and Argentina defender Javier Zanetti lead a 22-person committee to ascertain whether or not the award should remain.

The assessment could see committee members ban the awarding of the Peace Prize to politicians, should the award remain.



Reports claim that the idea of having a Peace Prize was not completely dismissed during the meeting although questions were raised on its future.

A final outcome is expected in December when the football social responsibility committee meets at the next FIFA Council meeting, in Doha.



Debbie Hewitt, FIFA vice-president and president of the English Football Association further detailed the committee’s task.

“There’s a decision taken to look at the peace prize and to take that through the social committee,” she told reporters.

“That was another issue that was raised: whether there should have been one, how the decision was taken to award it, and whether there should be another one. And those questions will be answered through the social committee.”

2 Infantino has been under intense scrutiny for various issues since the award's inception last December Credit: Getty



FIFA previously announced that the yearly prize will ‘reward individuals who have taken exceptional and extraordinary actions for peace’.

The award would also represent those who have ‘united people across the world’.

FIFA further claimed that it ‘will be presented to individuals who, through their unwavering commitment and their special actions, have helped to unite people all over the world in peace and consequently deserve a special and unique recognition’.

The awarding of the Peace Prize to Trump was later heavily criticised after the U.S. President launched air strikes in Iran.



Trump was given a golden trophy, a medal and a certificate as part of the presentation.

The voting procedure behind his award has never been revealed.

Sports.title: Alan Brazil names two new contenders Man United should consider if they sack Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil names two new contenders Man United should consider if they sack Michael Carrick

Manchester United should consider two former Premier League bosses should they decide to part ways with Michael Carrick.

talkSPORT’s Alan Brazil believes the Red Devils should look no further than Mauricio Pochettino and Kieran McKenna if they are looking for a successor to Carrick in the near future.



3 Michael Carrick is struggling to replicate last season's heroics Credit: Getty

The Manchester United boss is under increasing pressure after an underwhelming start to the season.

United were beaten 2-0 by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, leaving them with just two wins from nine games across all competitions.

The defeat was followed by defender Lisandro Martinez’s bombshell post-match interview in which he slammed director Jason Wilcox for a below-par summer transfer window.



Carrick was handed the permanent reins at Old Trafford in the summer after taking over from Ruben Amorim on an interim basis.

He revamped United’s fortunes, leading the club to a third-placed finish and crucially, Champions League qualification.



He also inspired United to wins over Manchester City and Arsenal.

While reports claim that Carrick retains the support of the club’s board, the Manchester United boss knows that he must pick up points quickly to turn his side’s fortunes around.

Failing that, two standout names should be at the top of the list, according to Brazil.



Ex-Prem duo top Brazil's list

“There are some names about,” the Sports Breakfast host said.

“Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte. Pochettino – would he come back?

3 Mauricio Pochettino has been sounded out by Brazil as a good fit for United Credit: Getty

“He's still a big Tottenham man but he would come back in my opinion.

“Kieran McKenna’s about, he knows about United.”

Pochettino is currently manager of the United States Men’s team.

He has been heavily linked with a return to the Premier League with Manchester United a possible destination for the Argentine.

Pochettino previously confirmed that United had shown a strong interest in him in the past.

The 54-year-old even recalled a famous lunch meeting requested by Sir Alex Ferguson during his time as Tottenham boss.



3 Kieran McKenna has close ties to Manchester United Credit: Getty

He later claimed that the ‘ideal scenario’ to take the job failed to materialise at the right time.

Meanwhile, McKenna is currently taking a career break from football management whilst working as a UEFA technical observer.

McKenna stepped down as Ipswich manager in June after guiding the club back to the Premier League – a third promotion in five years.



Despite stepping away from management, he has continued to be linked with managerial vacancies, including interest from Fulham.

Prior to his time at Portman Road, McKenna spent over five years at Manchester United between 2016 and 2021, progressing from the youth academy to first-team assistant.

Sports.title: Harry Kane told ‘no brainer’ contract decision as Ballon d’Or favourite given Alan Shearer record reminder
Sports.content:
A Premier League return makes little sense for Harry Kane, he has everything he needs at Bayern Munich.

That's the view of talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook, who has backed the England captain's decision to stay in Germany after agreeing terms on a new contract with Bayern.

4 Harry Kane is amongst the favourites for this year's Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Kane is set to sign a three-year deal that will keep him in Bavaria until the summer of 2029.

He was due to be a free agent at the end of the season, which prompted speculation over a return to the Premier League.

Before joining Bayern in 2023, the 33-year-old netted a staggering 280 goals in 435 appearances for Tottenham, making him the club's all-time record goalscorer.

Of his Spurs tally, 213 of Kane's goals came in the Premier League, putting him second only to Alan Shearer in the all-time charts.

With Shearer's record standing at an unmatched 260 top-flight goals, there has long been talk over whether Kane would return to England to try and better this number.

While a clause in the striker's previous Bayern deal gave Spurs had a first refusal to re-sign him, his new contract would appear to rule out him coming back to the Premier League.

Kane will be 36 by the time the three-year deal in place expires, with his long-term future in football likely to be in question then.

Premier League snobbery?

talkSPORT's Crook has insisted a return to the Premier League was never in Kane's best interests, highlighting his stellar time at Bayern.

The English ace has scored 154 goals in all competitions for the German giants, winning back-to-back Bundesliga titles, while his historic 61-goal campaign last season now places him among the favourites for the Ballon d'Or.

Asked if the possibility of Kane breaking Shearer's record was now over, Crook told talkSPORT: “Maybe. But the question I would ask - is it Premier League snobbery that we seriously thought he would come back?

4 Kane enjoyed a stellar 2025/26 season for Bayern and England Credit: Getty

4 But Kane's contract decision now means Alan Shearer's Premier League record is safe for now Credit: Getty

“He's playing for one of the biggest clubs in Europe. He's playing for a team who are pretty much nailed on to win the league every year in Germany. They're going to go deep in the Champions League.

“Why would he come back? He's not going to go and join Arsenal because of his Tottenham connections. We don't know what's happening with Manchester City with their points deductions."

With Crook a diehard Manchester United fan, he was even willing to admit that a move to Michael Carrick's struggling side would make little sense for Kane's career prospects.

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent also claimed the Bundesliga's intensity has helped his England career - with Kane notching six goals in the recent international break.

He continued: “Why would he go to Man United when he's at Bayern Munich?

“I think he's done absolutely the right thing. His family love it in Bavaria. The fans love him.

4 Kane started in all four of England's games over the extended international break, scoring six goals Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

“He's scoring goals. I think it actually helps his England form that he's playing in a slightly less demanding league week in week out.

“It's a no-brainer for me.”

Crook's co-host Sam Matterface agreed, saying: “He's got no reason to leave because, for him, England is everything and Bayern Munich gives him the best platform to improve as a player has improved him as a player No doubt.

“But also to manage his fitness in such a way that he can perform on the biggest stage. He’s been a revelation since he's been there.”

He later added: “He'll probably not catch Alan Shearer's 260 premier league goals. But to be honest, I think he's more obsessed with doing it for England.”

Sports.title: When is Cristiano Ronaldo playing next as Al Ahli v Al Nassr is postponed?
Sports.content:
When is Cristiano Ronaldo playing next as Al Ahli v Al Nassr is postponed?

Three Saudi Pro League matches have been postponed, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr.

The matchweek nine fixtures have been changed following an escalation in tensions where Houthis, in neighbouring Yemen, have launched missiles targeting Saudi Arabia infrastructure.

2 Ronaldo is dialled in on defending the title he won in the 2025/26 season with Al Nassr Credit: AFP

At least 13 people were killed when a missile hit Riyadh's airport on 10 October.

A statement from the league read: "The Saudi Professional League (SPL) has rescheduled three fixtures for logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches.

"Two fixtures; Al Riyadh against Al Hilal and Al Ittihad against Al Shabab will now be played on Saturday, December 19, 2026, while Al Ahli versus Al Nassr will be played on Saturday, March 6, 2027.

"The remaining games in Matchweek 9 will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes.

"In making the decision, the SPL took into consideration the mandatory minimum rest period between matches in addition to organisational and operational requirements for the matches.

"The changes are made in accordance with approved regulatory procedures for managing the competition's schedule, factoring in clubs' various logistical considerations for matches."

When is Cristiano Ronaldo playing next?

Ange Postecoglou takes his side to Neom SC on Tuesday, October 20 at 7pm (BST).

Al-Nassr currently sit third in the Saudi Pro League on 19 points, winning six out of eight games so far.

Ronaldo has scored four goals domestically and one in the AFC Champions League and was notably moved by the recent events in the country.

Before and after the AFC Champions League win over Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh, which was delayed due to a security alert he was emotional as he paid his respects to those who have been killed.

How can I watch Ronaldo's next match?

You can stream Al-Nassr vs Neom live on talkSPORT.com.

You can stream every available game live on talkSPORT.com for a small fee, giving you the chance to follow the action as it happens -wherever you are.

Who will Ronaldo be playing against?

Following massive investment in the club, Neom SC found themselves securing back-to-back promotions winning the Saudi First Division League in the 2024/25 season.

They are managed by former PSG and Lille head coach Christophe Galtier, who has won Ligue 1 once with both sides.

Additionally, former Arsenal striker Alexandre Lacazette and West Ham forward Said Benrahma play for the Saudi outfit.

2 Ronaldo scored against Neftchi in the AFC Champions League and was paid tribute to victims of the attack after the game, which had a delayed start due to a security alert Credit: AFP

Sports.title: Man United boss Michael Carrick issues Lisandro Martinez squad decision for Leeds clash
Sports.content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has confirmed that Lisandro Martinez is available for selection this weekend.

Martinez slammed the Man United board after his side were beaten by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday in a bombshell interview.



2 Martinez is available for Man United's clash against Leeds despite his outburst towards the club's board Credit: Getty

But Carrick has now drawn a line under the drama amid reports that the defender, who apologised in a statement revealing positive talks with the club on Thursday, has been fined.

"It's done,” the United boss said in his press conference ahead of the Premier League clash against Leeds on Sunday.

“We've moved on from that. It was one of those things. As a group we've moved on. It's really not a drama for the group. The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits.



"It was pretty simple. We understood the situation. Licha understood he made a mistake. We have a really good feeling from the club. Results wise it hasn't gone our way, but the spirit and togetherness. We can see in the group we want to do something with this situation.

We've moved on. Genuinely. There is a freshness about the group.

"He [Martinez] is available."

What did Martinez say?

Martinez's rant came pouring out during his post-match interview with Amazon Prime Video in Madrid earlier this week.



It was reportedly sparked by a decision to play Ayden Heaven at left-back in the Champions League game Man United lost 2-0.

He said: "I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.



"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

2 Martinez took aim at Man United's board in an outburst that is said to have been sparked by Heaven playing at left-back Credit: Getty

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."

Martinez added: "Last season we created a base to build an amazing team. It's annoying and disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team get an amazing result here."



On whether Carrick has not been backed enough, he continued: "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas. I can't say more. It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

What else has Carrick said on the outburst?

Martinez called out United's technical director Jason Wilcox specifically, asking why the club didn't sign more players.

In his press conference, Carrick was asked whether he thinks Wilcox should speak out more publicly, with senior players in the Red Devils squad understood to also be frustrated.



He replied: "I don’t think that’s for me to say. I’ve got no problem with how it is for me sitting here and talking to you guys and leading the group and the club from this position.

"We’re a really tight-knit group."

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez’s outburst ‘triggered by Man United team selection’ in new revelation
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez's furious rant at the Manchester United hierarchy was reportedly sparked by the decision to play Ayden Heaven at left-back.

The Argentine defender called out the Red Devils' director of football Jason Wilcox in an explosive interview following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday in the Champions League.

5 Martinez did not hold back on his assessment of United as he called out the board for their transfer business Credit: Getty

Martinez slammed the Man United board for a lack of investment during the summer transfer window.

The 28-year-old doubled down in a statement on Wednesday, insisting: "My words reflect how I feel," before issuing an apology on Thursday evening.

And the root cause of his public outburst has now reportedly been identified, with Michael Carrick's backline selection causing an issue.

Heaven decision angers Martinez

With Luke Shaw United's only senior left-back option, his absence from the Atletico clash forced centre-back Heaven to deputise.

According to the Sun, the decision angered Martinez, who felt asking Heaven to play out of position proved the board has failed to provide a squad capable of competing at the highest level.

Left-back was identified as a priority position in the summer by Carrick, but he was unable to land top target in Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

With this deemed too expensive a move, the Red Devils then saw their deadline day enquiry for Manchester City's Rayan Ait Nouri dismissed.

Instead of strengthening at left-back, United spent just £153m on midfield trio Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

But with United now set for weeks without a specialist left-back after Shaw limped off in their 1-1 draw with Tottenham on Saturday, Martinez was left angered by a lack of squad depth.

A source told the Sun: “Martinez was furious because he thinks having to play Ayden at left back away in Madrid shows how ill-equipped the squad is. It doesn’t have enough depth.

5 Ayden Heaven has made just 30 senior appearances for United and played in an unfamiliar role against Atletico Credit: Getty

5 Martinez did not hold back on his assessment of United as he called out the board for their transfer business Credit: Getty

“And the fault of that lies squarely with the board.”

The source added that Martinez was not criticising Heaven directly, but rather the 20-year-old not playing in his best position.

While Martinez initially appeared to stand by his explosive interview comments, he has since revealed that he and senior personnel at United have patched things up.

In a statement on Thursday, the 2022 World Cup winner said: "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise."

talkSPORT understands that Martinez has been fined by the club.

5 Martinez has been fined by United for his outburst, but all parties consider matters to be closed Credit: Getty

Has Martinez reaction been justified?

Martinez's explosive comments have had a mixed response, with some sympathetic to his frustrations amid a lack of summer transfer activity at United.

Meanwhile, the club's all-time leading goalscorer Wayne Rooney slammed the Argentine's rant as 'disrespectful to his teammates'.

But former Manchester United assistant coach, Rene Meulensteen has claimed there has been an overreaction to Martinez's outburst.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Meulensteen said: “I think some things have been taken out of context a little bit because I don't think that Martinez said anything bad about the current transfers or the players, he just said that they weren't backed enough.

“And sometimes after football [matches], you know, the emotions run high, they haven't won in five games.

“I think it was just an outburst of emotions and negativity where he felt that possibly again Michael Carrick was coming under scrutiny, maybe he wanted to protect him, but it is not to say that I agree with what he did, absolutely not.

5 Rene Meulensteen served as assistant manager at Man United between 2008 and 2013 Credit: Getty Images - Getty

“But sometimes you need to look at what he said, and I think if you take that into context, I think there's plenty of people that would agree with him.

“So, yeah, what is going to happen? Obviously, he apologised, then you have to sit down with him.

“I don't think he necessarily put Michael Carrick in a bad position, but Michael has to obviously deal with it and make sure that maybe in some ways [he] uses it to his advantage, because the only thing that needs to happen now with Man United, everybody has to step up.

“Everybody has to step up and the best way to do it is on the against Leeds.”

Where to watch Nottingham Forest v Arsenal as Premier League confirm controversial referee decision

Arsenal will look to continue their positive momentum and try to catch Manchester City at the top of the Premier League with a win in Nottingham this Sunday.

The Gunners have won five of their six Premier League games so far this season and have eight wins from nine in all competitions.



3 Bruno Guimaraes netted a superb 70th-minute winner against Leeds last weekend Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's side had to work hard to comeback against Leeds and Lille last week in separate competitions.

Meanwhile, Forest have struggled and were beaten 3-1 by Crystal Palace last time out, with Oliver Glasner being humbled by his old side.

Sports.title: Where to watch Leeds v Manchester United as under-fire Michael Carrick faces must win after chaotic week
Sports.content:
Where to watch Leeds v Manchester United as under-fire Michael Carrick faces must win after chaotic week

Michael Carrick is facing his biggest managerial test at Manchester United and a tense game against rivals Leeds is up next.

United have had an inconsistent start to the season, and had a further knock after a 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night.

3 Leeds have scored seven goals this season Credit: Getty

That is a continuation from a home draw with 10-man Tottenham last weekend, which meant Carrick has led his team to the club's worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Additionally, centre-back Lisandro Martinez took aim at sporting director Jason Wilcox mid-week about the lack of investment during the summer transfer window.

He said: "I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director. I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."

Leeds, meanwhile, will hope to get back on track at Elland Road after they lost their unbeaten streak in a narrow 2-1 defeat to Arsenal last weekend.

The Whites produced an encouraging performance and went ahead through James Justin but couldn’t hold onto their lead for long.

The last clash between these two sides in Leeds resulted in a 1-1 draw, which proved to be the last straw for Ruben Amorim.

Sports.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dead aged 31: Former Sale Sharks star suffers heart attack at team hotel in France on eve of Champions Cup clash with La Rochelle
Sports.content:
South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dead aged 31: Former Sale Sharks star suffers heart attack at team hotel in France on eve of Champions Cup clash with La Rochelle

Hyron Andrews, a former Sale Sharks lock, has died of a suspected heart attack in news that has shocked the rugby world.

On Friday morning, French media reported a Lions player had been found unresponsive in a shower stall at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso Hotel just outside of La Rochelle – where the South African side are due to play a European Champions Cup game on Saturday.

Just a few hours later, the Lions confirmed the passing of Andrews, 31. Emergency services arrived but were unable to save him and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Andrews only returned to his native South Africa to join the Lions this summer after departing English club side Sale for whom he made 45 appearances. Of those, 19 came for the Sharks last season.

‘The Lions Rugby Company is deeply saddened by the passing of player Hyron Andrews while on tour with the 10bet Lions ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and Vodacom United Rugby Championship fixtures,’ the Lions said in a statement.

'This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community. The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family and his loss will be felt profoundly by his team-mates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him.

Lions player Hyron Andrews, 31, has died of an apparent heart attack in La Rochelle, a day before the two sides were due to meet in the European Champions Cup

'Our deepest and most heartfelt condolences go to Hyron’s wife, Maiglin, their young sons, and the entire Andrews family. We hold them in our thoughts during this time of unimaginable grief and ask that their privacy be respected as they mourn.’

The Lions have confirmed that their scheduled clash with La Rochelle will go ahead as planned, with the team’s players keen to pay tribute to Andrews on the field.

Reports in the French media said a psychological support unit had been set up for the Lions franchise's players and staff, as well as the hotel personnel.

Rudolf Straeuli, Lions chief executive, said: ‘We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family having recently joined us this season.

'On behalf of our chairman, Mr Altmann Allers, the board and everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to Maiglin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect.’

The Lions added: ‘The Lions Rugby Company will communicate further details regarding an appropriate tribute in due course. In honour of Hyron, the 10bet Lions will fulfil their opening match of the Investec Champions Cup against La Rochelle tomorrow evening South African time. May Hyron rest in peace.’

Andrews' former employers Sale said: 'Everyone at Sale Sharks is devastated to learn of the death of our former player Hyron Andrews. Hyron was a much-loved member of the squad during his time with us and everyone at the club is united in sending their love, thoughts and heartfelt condolences to his wife Maighlin, their beautiful boys and the rest of his family and friends and everyone at Lions Rugby.'

PREM Rugby also said in a statement: 'Everyone at PREM Rugby and our clubs is deeply saddened by the passing of Hyron Andrews and we extend our heartfelt sympathies to his family and friends.

'Our thoughts are also with Hyron’s team-mates past and present, everyone at the Lions and Sale Sharks, and the wider South African rugby community at this very difficult time.'

'This is terrible and distressing news. Our hearts go out to Hyron’s family and the whole Lions rugby community,' said Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union.

'There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maighlin and for his extended family, friends, team-mates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.

'Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.

'His untimely passing is a devastating loss and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

'The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maighlin and all those mourning his loss. May they find strength, comfort and peace in the memories they shared with him and in the support of those around them.'

South African star Andrews played for Sale in England before leaving at the end of last season

In a bizarre coincidence, Andrews’ tragic passing occurred on the 10-year anniversary of the death of Munster legend Anthony Foley.

A former Munster coach and captain, Foley died in his sleep on October 16, 2016, at the age of 42 in Paris on the eve of a European tie against Racing 92 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs.

Ronan O’Gara, the current La Rochelle head coach, was an ex-Munster team-mate of Foley’s. Reports have suggested O’Gara headed to the team hotel of the Lions to offer the team’s grieving players and support staff emotional support.

European Rugby organisers said: ‘It is with deep sadness that EPCR has learned of the tragic passing of 10bet Lions player Hyron Andrews while on tour ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and URC fixtures.’

The organisation’s chairman, Dominic McKay, said: ‘The thoughts of everyone at EPCR and the wider international rugby community are with Hyron’s wife Maiglin, his young sons, wider family, friends, team-mates, the 10bet Lions and all those who knew and loved him at this incredibly difficult time.’

In memory of Andrews, a moment’s silence will be held ahead of every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend.

Andrews' former club boss, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, said: 'Hyron was just a brilliant guy and team-mate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with.

'He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him.

'It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maighlin to come to England but he truly made a second home in Manchester and it was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area.

'Most importantly, he was a loving husband to Maighlin and a doting father to his two gorgeous boys. It was an absolute privilege to get to know him and it’s just absolutely devastating for everyone.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists Man United have 'moved on' from Lisandro Martinez's 'mistake' - and claims squad is in a 'fantastic place' despite defender's explosive rant at club chiefs
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick insists Man United have 'moved on' from Lisandro Martinez's 'mistake' - and claims squad is in a 'fantastic place' despite defender's explosive rant at club chiefs

Michael Carrick believes Lisandro Martinez 'realised he has made a mistake' over his extraordinary outburst in Madrid, and insists the controversy will not distract Manchester United from turning their season around.

Martinez will be in United's squad to face Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday after he apologised for criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and club bosses in a television interview which landed the 28-year-old defender with a fine.

Carrick, who was in the meeting with Martinez and Wilcox at Carrington on Thursday, said: 'You're after some kind of big information about big discussions, but it was pretty simple.

'We all understood the situation and what it meant. Lisandro obviously made his statement, and he acknowledges that it was a mistake from him, and that was it really. It's really not a drama for us as a group. We've genuinely moved on.

'From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done has certainly been enough. He's released his statement and he's realised he's made a mistake. I think that's enough for all of us to move on with. We're definitely not looking back at it now.'

Former United captain Wayne Rooney claimed that Martinez’s criticism of United’s transfer policy in the summer could rip the dressing-room apart, but Carrick believes his team’s performance in a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid – and the mood in training over the last two days – suggest the opposite is true.

Man United boss Michael Carrick has given his verdict on Lisandro Martinez's explosive rant

Martinez ripped into United's hierarchy on TV after their defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday

'The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while actually,' added the United boss.

'We're living it every day, we know what it feels like. We're emotional, we're passionate, we care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe they shouldn't say at a certain time, but that doesn't distract us from what we're creating here and the environment and the spirit within the group.

'It's not affected. I'm telling you as it is. We're in a good place, and I'm really happy with the boys today.

'Results-wise, it hasn't gone to plan of late, but today was one of the best training sessions we've had. You can see there's a real sense and a feeling within the group that we want to do something about this situation.

'There's a lot of things can affect the group in all sorts of different ways. Certain situations can galvanise the group, and it's certainly galvanised the group as this week's progressed.'

Carrick also suggested that emotion got the better of Amad Diallo after the Ivorian posted a message on Tuesday night, saying 'f***ing disgrace, I have no words'.

'Again, it's a situation where there's ways of doing it,' said Carrick. 'In one way, it shows the boys care an awful lot. But yes, of course, there are ways of doing it as part of learning a little bit. I think we've just got to show that emotion in the right manner and channel it in the right manner.

'We ask for passion, we ask for emotion, we ask for fire, and we ask for players to care. There's a way of doing that. As a group, we've got to use it in the right way.'

Carrick desperately needs a reaction from his players at Elland Road after a run of four defeats and two wins in nine games this season has put him under pressure.

Old rivals Leeds will be relishing the chance to pile on more misery, but Carrick said: 'I don't need results, we all need results. It's not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual: bigger than me, bigger than any player or anyone else who works at this football club.

'I don't go into every day at work in this situation thinking about me. It's about the football club: what we stand for, what we live for, the history, the things that we need to live up to, and that's what drives us.

'So whatever is best for the football club and for the team on Sunday is the most important thing. It's a great rivalry. There's big history between the football clubs, and I think that's what makes these type of games special.

'You've got to embrace the history, you've got to embrace what it means, and you've got to embrace the past of certain games that are a little bit different. This is certainly one of them, and we'll be ready for it.'

United technical director Jason Wilcox (left) was on the receiving end of Martinez's anger

Martinez had taken aim at the United hierarchy in the wake of a fourth defeat in nine games in Madrid when he was asked if the club have backed Carrick enough.

'I don't think so,' he said. 'He does his best. You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager.

'What about other areas? Tonight it is easy to say the coach and easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.

'I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

'I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.'

On Thursday evening, after talks with United, Martinez shared a social media post apologising.

'Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager,' he said: 'It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

'Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

'The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.'

Sports.title: Billy Loughnane on realising his dream at just 20 as he gets set to be crowned youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century - and your best bets for big Flat finale Ascot
Sports.content:
Billy Loughnane on realising his dream at just 20 as he gets set to be crowned youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century - and your best bets for big Flat finale Ascot

With typical humility and understatement, Billy Loughnane adeptly recalls the formative stages of his career: 'My aim was to just have a few winners.'

The affable 20-year-old, who will be crowned the youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century on Saturday, has swiftly left behind those modest early ambitions with his career winners' tally currently standing at more than 700 and rising quicker than the price of diesel.

As Loughnane takes dead aim at the record held by the legendary Sir Gordon Richards of 269 winners in a calendar year – he equalled his personal best of 223 on Tuesday at Wolverhampton – comparisons are inevitably drawn with a similarly precocious jockey of days gone by, Frankie Dettori.

While the now retired Italian is widely regarded as one of the finest and most natural riding talents to grace British racing, Loughnane has, at this embryonic stage of his career, three Group 1 wins to Dettori's sole success at the age of 20, while it took Dettori eight years to reach 1,000 winners, whereas Loughnane has approximately 750 in half the time.

'If someone had said to me back then, that I would be Champion Jockey in four years I would have said they were absolutely crazy and asked them, "what have you been drinking!" joked Loughnane who has beaten five-time Champion Oisin Murphy to the title.

'I put a little pressure on myself, having come so far not to let it slip in the last little bit of the season, but the last two weeks have been enjoyable. It's a dream that is beginning to come true.

'At the start, I wanted to achieve becoming Champion Apprentice, I didn't for one minute think it would snowball as it has. My aim was to just have a few winners.

Billy Loughnane will be crowned the youngest Champion Jockey in more than a century on Saturday

'It has been an extraordinary couple of years really and I'm lucky that I've been able to team up with a lot of good trainers who have propelled me forward.'

One of those connections has been with Newmarket handler George Boughey for whom Loughnane has ridden nigh on 180 winners in those four seasons, including that golden trio of elite successes aboard Bow Echo this season.

As well as being a masterful trainer, Boughey has a keen eye for a talented rider and this year his Craven House Stables on Hamilton Road will house not only the Champion Jockey in Loughnane, but Champion Apprentice Jack Callan and younger brother Henry, who looks set to be crowned Champion Amateur rider.

The symbiotic relationship Loughnane shares with Boughey and the unadulterated joy the duo shared in the now retired Bow Echo's successes has been one of the most heart-warming aspects of the summer.

'George is a very good mentor as well as a very good trainer and he's become a very good friend,' reveals Loughnane.

'It was a dream come true to find a horse like Bow Echo – unbeaten in six starts, a winner of the Guineas, at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes, it was an amazing journey.

'It was gutting that injury meant we don't get to see him next year, but winning the Guineas was the best buzz I've ever had on the racecourse.

SAM TURNER'S TIPS FOR CHAMPIONS DAY AT ASCOT 12:55 – Arapaho Gold 1:30 – Highwayman 2:05 – Almeraq 2:40 – Lilt (ew) 3:20 – More Thunder (Nap) 4:00 – Calandagan 4:35 – Scoville (nb)

'There was six or seven months of him keeping us warm through the winter and when I was in Dubai, I was getting pictures of him off George all the time.

'That build up made the Guineas win extra special.'

While Loughnane is comfortable at Meydan, Longchamp or Saturday's royal venue Ascot, his love of racing was nurtured in more humble surroundings during his time 'assisting' father Mark, himself a trainer, based in Kidderminster.
