World.title: Customs deepens security partnerships to combat smuggling, protect revenue
World.content:
By Godwin Oritse

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, has intensified efforts to combat smuggling, strengthen border and maritime security, and facilitate legitimate trade through closer collaboration with security agencies and private-sector operators.



The Acting Customs Area Controller, Deputy Comptroller, Dr Nkiru Nwala, led delegations to the 13 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Eastern Naval Command, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and Shoreline Logistics Nigeria Limited on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, to strengthen institutional relationships and improve operational coordination.



The engagements focused on intelligence sharing, coordinated enforcement operations, protection of critical national assets, road safety, maritime security and compliance with Customs regulations.

Speaking during the visits, Nwala emphasised the need for sustained cooperation among security agencies to address smuggling and other criminal activities, protect government revenue and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests.

She noted that the geographical characteristics of the Command’s operational environment, which encompasses land borders, coastal communities and maritime routes, made collaboration particularly important in tackling illicit activities and emerging security threats.

At the 13 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, the Customs delegation was received by the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General P.O. Alimikhena. The discussions highlighted the strategic importance of cooperation in securing border areas, combating smuggling and protecting the nation’s territorial integrity.

The Customs delegation stressed that intelligence sharing, timely communication and coordinated enforcement operations would strengthen the effectiveness of both agencies and improve security across the region.

Similarly, at the Eastern Naval Command, where the delegation was received on behalf of the Flag Officer Commanding by the Chief of Staff, Rear Admiral S. Ibrahim, Nwala underscored the complementary responsibilities of Customs and the Nigerian Navy in securing the country’s maritime environment.

She noted that closer collaboration was necessary to prevent the exploitation of waterways for smuggling and other illicit activities, while strengthening maritime enforcement and protecting legitimate trade.

The engagement also highlighted the need for effective communication and operational coordination between the two agencies to address emerging challenges in the coastal and maritime environment.

Nwala highlighted the importance of cooperation in addressing security challenges, protecting critical national assets and ensuring the effective discharge of the agencies’ respective statutory responsibilities.

She called for stronger communication channels, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations to tackle emerging threats and safeguard national economic interests.

The Customs chief also stressed the importance of cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety, facilitating legitimate trade and securing transportation routes within the Command’s area of responsibility.

Discussions at meeting centered on the importance of safer roads and efficient transportation networks to Customs enforcement activities and the movement of goods.

Nwala noted that road transportation remained critical to Customs operations, adding that improved coordination between the two agencies would enhance operational efficiency, promote road safety and support the smooth movement of legitimate commerce.

Beyond security partnerships, the Command also engaged the private sector, visiting Shoreline Logistics Nigeria Limited to strengthen stakeholder relations and improve trade facilitation.

During the meeting, Nwala emphasised the important role of logistics operators in facilitating cargo movement, supporting supply chains and promoting efficient commercial activities.

She urged operators to uphold transparency, maintain accurate documentation and comply with relevant Customs laws and regulations, noting that compliance would help prevent infractions, improve operational efficiency and protect government revenue.

She also highlighted the need for regular engagement between Customs and logistics operators to resolve operational challenges, clarify regulatory requirements and improve service delivery.

The Command reaffirmed its commitment to balancing effective regulatory enforcement with the facilitation of legitimate trade, stressing that productive relationships with private-sector stakeholders were essential to efficient Customs administration.

The engagements align with the Comptroller-General of Customs’ strategic framework of Collaboration, Consolidation and Innovation, which emphasises stronger institutional partnerships, the consolidation of operational gains and the adoption of innovative approaches to addressing enforcement and administrative challenges.

The Command said sustained cooperation with security agencies and private-sector operators would contribute to suppressing smuggling, improving revenue generation, protecting critical national assets and facilitating legitimate trade.

The engagements further underscored the importance of a coordinated approach to border management, maritime enforcement, transportation security and trade facilitation in promoting national security and economic development.

World.title: Tinubu orders dualisation of Benin-Asaba road — Umahi
World.content:
Minister of Works, Davide Umahi.

By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Federal Government has reclaimed the Benin-Asaba Road for reconstruction as a dual carriageway following a directive by President Bola Tinubu, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, has said.

Umahi disclosed this in Asaba on Thursday during the reopening of the First Niger Bridge on the Asaba-Onitsha Road.

The development was contained in a statement issued in Abuja on Friday by the minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Francis Nwaze.

Umahi said the concession arrangement that had prevented the Ministry of Works from directly undertaking the reconstruction of the Benin-Asaba Road had been discontinued, paving the way for the Federal Government to take responsibility for the project.

“What stopped the Ministry of Works from reconstructing Benin-Asaba Road, the concessioning of that route, has been unsealed. We now have our route back to the Ministry of Works,” he said.

According to the minister, Tinubu has directed a comprehensive redesign of the 136-kilometre road as a dual carriageway, with design work already underway ahead of construction.

“The legacy of President Bola Tinubu, you will see it ongoing on this road. Never again will our people suffer on this road,” Umahi said.

He said the return of the road to the ministry would enable the Federal Government to take direct responsibility for its reconstruction and address the difficulties faced by motorists travelling between the South-South and South-East.

First Niger Bridge receives major upgrades

On the First Niger Bridge, Umahi said the ministry intervened after a content creator raised the alarm over alleged vandalism involving the removal of bolts and cutting of iron components from the bridge’s steel structure.

He said an inspection revealed dangerous tampering that could compromise the bridge’s structural integrity.

Originally built in 1966 and commissioned by then Prime Minister, Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, the bridge had suffered years of inadequate maintenance, according to the minister.

Umahi said the bridge had now received treatment similar to that carried out on Lagos’ Third Mainland Bridge, including asphalt resurfacing, median demarcation, solar-powered lighting, CCTV cameras and observation centres at both ends.

He added that three turnaround passages had also been provided to facilitate emergency operations.

“Exactly the treatment we gave to the Third Mainland Bridge is the treatment we gave to this place,” he said.

The minister commended the contractor, SKCC, for its work but identified outstanding tasks, including repainting the entire steel structure, treating rust-affected areas beneath the deck and providing canopies.

He also warned against illegal sand dredging within 10 kilometres of bridges, directing directors of works in Delta and Anambra states to enforce the prohibition or face disciplinary action.

Tinubu orders East-West Road reconstruction

Umahi further disclosed that Tinubu had ordered the reconstruction of about 400 kilometres of the East-West Road as a spur of the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

He said design work on sections of the East-West Road was nearing completion, dismissing claims that work on the coastal highway had stopped.

“Some people thought that the East-West Road was a road in the South-East. East-West Road is entirely in the Niger Delta. The coastal road is the right of the Niger Delta people,” he said.

The minister also said reconstruction of the Enugu-Port Harcourt Road had reached 90 per cent completion.

He added that work was ongoing on a 44-kilometre concrete pavement section in Port Harcourt, as well as a 107-kilometre dual carriageway project in Anambra State, where 33 kilometres had been completed.

Umahi cited the 17.5-kilometre Section 2B of the Second Niger Bridge bypass, valued at ₦172 billion, as another example of federal infrastructure investment in the region.

“These are projects that show the President’s commitment to the South-East. We cannot thank the President enough,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Hashim Movement targets 3m votes in South-West
World.content:
Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim

By Clifford Ndujihe

The South-West Coordinator of the Gbenga Hashim Solidarity Movement (GHSM), Alhaji Abass Olaniyi, says the movement is targeting more than three million votes for the Accord Party’s presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, across the region in the 2027 general election.

Olaniyi said the target was based on the movement’s internal assessment of its grassroots mobilisation prospects across the six South-West states, with Osun, Lagos and Oyo expected to account for a significant share of the projected votes.

According to him, Osun State is projected to contribute more than one million votes, while Lagos and Oyo are expected to deliver a combined 1.5 million votes.

He said Ogun, Ondo and Ekiti states would contribute the remaining votes needed to achieve the regional target.

Olaniyi expressed confidence in the movement’s ability to expand its grassroots presence through engagement with community leaders, youth groups, political stakeholders and local organisations across the region.

He also said the movement expected voters in Osun to make independent choices in the presidential election, irrespective of political alignments involving state-level leaders.

The coordinator’s projection comes amid preparations by political parties and support groups for the 2027 general election.

GHSM said it intended to translate its mobilisation efforts across the South-West into electoral support for Olawepo-Hashim and the Accord Party.

World.title: 2027: Atiku, Amaechi, Obi will play ‘kalokalo’ with your destiny, Wike tells Rivers electorate
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has warned the people of Rivers State that former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Rotimi Amaechi and Peter Obi will play “kalokalo” with their destiny, urging them to reject the trio and back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

“Kalokalo” is the Nigerian pidgin slang for playing games of chance, such as slot machines or sports betting.

The minister spoke on Friday at a Rainbow Coalition town hall meeting at Ayama in Abua/Odual Local Government Area LGA of Rivers State, before a crowd of traditional leaders, party faithful and community stakeholders.

“Don’t trust your destiny to political gamblers. Don’t trust your destiny to ‘kalokalo’ people,” Wike told the cheering crowd.

He described political gamblers as people who keep contesting for the presidency every four years, hoping to recover what they lost, without any genuine vision for the country.

He named Atiku and his Vice Presidential candidate, Amaechi, of the African Democratic Congress ADC, as well as Obi, the Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC.

“These people are political gamblers and you cannot give your destiny to ‘kalokalo’ people; you cannot hand over your destiny to political gamblers. Give (your) destiny to somebody who we know, who has tried all this, and he has done it,” he said.

Wike argued that repeated presidential runs without a clear governance plan offer no real solutions to Nigeria’s challenges.

He said leaders such as Abraham Lincoln ran several times because of a clear national vision, while Atiku keeps running out of political habit and a desire to recoup his investments.

Defending his record in Rivers State, Wike told the people of Abua/Odual that project delivery, not political rhetoric, should decide their electoral choices.

He challenged Amaechi to show what he has contributed to the LGA, and pointed to projects executed there by his administration.

The minister praised Tinubu’s administration for stabilising critical national sectors and restoring industrial harmony in tertiary institutions. He asked Abua/Odual residents to remain with the administration heading into 2027.

Wike asked residents to vote for Tinubu as President and Mr Kingsley Chinda as governor, all under the All Progressives Congress APC. He also named Mr Felix Obua for Rivers West Senatorial District and Mr Solomon Boss for Abua-Odual-Ahoada East Federal Constituency, also on the APC platform.

He further asked them to vote for Mr John Iderima, the Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate for the Abua/Odual state constituency.

Chinda, the APC governorship candidate in Rivers State, commended Wike for going from community to community to mobilise support for Tinubu and other candidates of the Rainbow Coalition.

“This is a system that we will sustain when we come into government. We have learnt from him, and we will continue. It will be a bottom-up approach; the people will decide and determine their fate in government,” Chinda said.

Earlier, Prof. Continue Eketu, who spoke on behalf of the Abua/Odual communities, described Wike as his idol and listed projects executed in the LGA during Wike’s tenure as governor.

“We have decided and agreed to vote massively for all candidates of the Rainbow Coalition,” Eketu said.

World.title: Lack of forensic labs frustrating rape cases in Jigawa — NBA
World.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Jigawa State branch, has raised concerns over the lack of forensic laboratories in the state, saying the gap is undermining efforts to secure convictions in rape and other sexual violence cases.

The chairman of the association, Barrister Hamza Umar, raised the concern at a two-day policy dialogue organised by the CLEEN Foundation, with support from the Norwegian Embassy in Nigeria, in Dutse, the state capital.

Umar said the absence of forensic facilities had made it difficult for prosecutors to obtain scientific evidence required to establish rape allegations in court.

“We cannot secure conviction when we have no forensic lab to prove rape cases scientifically. The law requires forensic evidence. We are still relying on mere confessional statements, which the court may reject,” he said.

He also criticised the alleged failure to publish the names of convicted rapists as provided for under the state’s Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Law, saying the provision had not been implemented.

The VAPP Law, signed on February 24, 2021, was introduced to address rape, sexual and gender-based violence, physical abuse and other harmful practices.

At the dialogue, stakeholders called for the establishment of at least five Sexual Assault Referral Centres across the state’s five emirate zones to improve support for survivors and access to justice.

They also expressed concern that cultural and religious beliefs continued to discourage victims from reporting sexual violence, while some families preferred to settle cases outside the formal justice system.

Earlier, the Senior Programme Officer of the CLEEN Foundation, Olaniyi Olumayowa, said the dialogue was aimed at addressing gaps between the enactment of the VAPP Law and its implementation.

He explained that the law was designed not only to punish offenders but also to protect survivors, provide compensation and ensure accountability among relevant institutions.

Olumayowa urged the Jigawa State Government to provide adequate funding for forensic laboratories, establish additional referral centres and train personnel responsible for implementing the law.

World.title: ICPC seeks public support against vote buying in Jigawa
World.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has called for collective action by government institutions and members of the public to curb vote buying and selling ahead of the 2027 general elections in Jigawa State.

The Resident Anti-Corruption Commissioner overseeing Kano and Jigawa states, Ahmad Muhammad Wada, made the call during a courtesy visit to the Secretary to the Jigawa State Government, Malam Bala Ibrahim.

Wada said public cooperation was essential to preventing electoral corruption and ensuring credible elections.

He explained that the commission was intensifying efforts to tackle electoral malpractices through enforcement, preventive measures, public enlightenment and education.

According to him, the visit was part of the ICPC’s public enlightenment campaign aimed at strengthening collaboration with relevant stakeholders in the fight against corruption.

The commissioner stressed that addressing vote buying and selling required the active involvement of government institutions and citizens.

He reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to combating electoral offences and promoting credible elections ahead of the 2027 polls.

Responding, the Secretary to the Jigawa State Government, Bala Ibrahim, assured the commission of the state government’s support and cooperation in tackling electoral offences.

He said the government was ready to work closely with the ICPC to discourage vote buying, vote selling and other forms of electoral corruption ahead of the general elections.

World.title: Man City charges: Maresca says club, players, fans are ‘more together’
World.content:
Maresca (Photo by May JAMES / AFP)

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says he feels no stress over the club’s financial charges, insisting the controversy has brought the club, team and supporters closer together.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday’s clash with Ipswich, Maresca said City were focused on their performance and could not control the debate surrounding the case. An independent commission found the club guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules; City deny wrongdoing and have appealed the decision.

“Since the noise, from my personal point of view, I can see the fans, the club, the team more together, for sure,” Maresca said.

City have won at Anfield since the verdict was announced but lost to Paris Saint-Germain in a midweek Champions League match. Maresca said the players’ response had been positive and described Saturday’s game as another opportunity to collect three points and extend their winning run.

“There is noise around the club but we need to try to make our noise. That means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow against Ipswich,” he said. “This is the way we can make our noise. A different kind of noise; we’re not able to control that.”

Asked how he was coping with the situation, Maresca said: “I’m very happy. I don’t feel any kind of stress about the outside situation because it’s something I don’t control. I just focus on how we can try to win the next games.”

The City manager said he trusted the club’s leadership and had spoken with officials about the case. He added that he preferred to wait for an outcome before judging the situation.

Maresca also described City’s 4-2 defeat by PSG as a learning experience, saying his side lost its balance after conceding twice in quick succession but responded well in the second half.

He warned that Ipswich would pose a difficult challenge after having a full week to prepare, while City played in Europe just 48 hours earlier. Victory would give City a chance to extend their league-winning run to seven matches.

World.title: Anglican Church suspends Archbishop Ibezim of Awka for 6 months
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

The Anglican Bishop of Awka, and Metropolitan Archbishop on the Niger, Most Reverend Alexander Ibezim, has been suspended from office and directed not to embark on church activities.

The Primate of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), Most Rev. Henry. Ndukuba, who announced the suspension, directed Ibezim, to proceed on six months’ leave with immediate effect while investigations into allegations and recent developments in the diocese commence.

.

Ibezim was also barred from officiating any activities of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), the Province of the Niger or the Anglican Diocese of Awka throughout the period of his leave.

Ndukuba, in a letter dated Tuesday, October 13, 2026, also announced the appointment of the Bishop of the Diocese of Aguata, the Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor, as Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province of the Niger during Ibezim’s absence.

The letter, addressed to Ibezim, stated that the decision followed recent developments in the Diocese of Awka, where the archbishop had been at the centre of various allegations and events which, according to the Primate, had raised concerns about the integrity and reputation of the Church of Nigeria.

Primate further cited a meeting with Ibezim on October 9, during which the visitation team’s report was discussed, as part of the circumstances preceding the decision.

According to the letter, the action was taken pursuant to Section 29(1) of Chapter V of the Constitution and Canons of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), 2020, which grants the Primate general authority and supervision over the Church and its inherent powers.

Ndukuba explained that the administrative measure was intended to allow a fair and thorough investigation into the allegations, while creating room for the restoration of peace and reconciliation in the Diocese of Awka.

He specifically clarified that the leave did not constitute a disciplinary sanction, but was an administrative step to facilitate an impartial inquiry into the state of affairs in the diocese.

The letter directed Ibezim to proceed on leave for an initial period of six months, or such other revised period as the Church leadership might consider necessary.

During the period, Ezeofor is to assume and exercise episcopal responsibilities and oversight of both the Diocese of Awka and the Province of the Niger.

The Primate further instructed him to prepare for and effect an immediate handover of his responsibilities to Ezeofor at his office before leaving.

Copies of the letter were also copied to Ezeofor, the Chancellor and Registrar of the Church of Nigeria, the Provincial Council of the Province of the Niger and the Diocesan Board of the Diocese of Awka.

Although the letter did not specify the nature of the allegations against Ibezim or provide details of the findings contained in the visitation team’s report, it was gathered that Archbishop Ibezim was recently accused of acting in some ways without authorization by the church.

World.title: Don’t Scare Away Electorate Through Violence, Oyo Guber Candidate Warns Politicians
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Oyo State, Adegboyega Taofeek Adegoke, has admonished politicians and their supporters not to scare away the electorate through thuggery and violence ahead of the 2027 general election.

He stated this while speaking with journalists in Ibadan, and calling on the political parties and their candidates to talk to their supporters and followers to allow peace to reign, saying thuggery and violence will scare away voters.

He warned that no member of any political party can singlehandedly bring the candidates to government, adding that they will need the people, the electorate to win elections.

On Wednesday, members of Accord Party in the state had clashed with some hoodlums at Molete area leading to the death of one person, while many sustained various degree of injuries, a situation which also caused panic among the residents of the area in Ibadan, the state capital.

Also, the All Progressives Congress (APC) alleged that their convoy was attacked by thugs in Ibadan a few weeks ago.

The Oyo ADC governorship candidate said part of the problem is the high rate of youth unemployment, noting that majority of the state population is made up of youths that are not gainfully employed, promising that if elected governor, he will provide jobs for the youth in the state.

He called on all candidates in the 2027 elections in Oyo State to ensure that they maintain and allow peace to reign.

He also called on political leaders to measure what they say at the campaigns, saying they should avoid hate speeches but tell people what they want to do and how they want to achieve them.

He said: “Anytime I go out for campaign, I don’t go out with thugs. I don’t like violence, I don’t support violence. I preach peace always.

“We should talk to our supporters, our followers to allow peace to reign. We should not scare away the electorate because without them we cannot win elections. We cannot win election with our party members alone, we need the people.

“If our youth are fully engaged, they will not be available for thuggery and violence. I want to appeal to my colleagues, that we should not allow people to turn Oyo State to an avenue for attacks, an avenue for thuggery, where hoodlums will reign supreme. We don’t want that in Oyo State.

“Our campaign should be issue based. We should not incite the people. We should measure what we say. Don’t attack one another. Tell the electorate what you want to do and let them judge you.

“That is why I said my agenda is summarised in Nine Points – ‘SOLUTIONS’. So tell people what you want to do and avoid hate speech.”

World.title: PTDF Reaffirms Continuous Funding For Research Projects in Varsities
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

The Executive Secretary, Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), Prof. Shua’ibu Shehu Aliyu, has reiterated the Fund’s commitment to strengthening research, innovation and human capital development in Nigerian universities.

The secretary said the PTDF seeks not only to support academic excellence but also to promote researches that address real national and industry challenges.

Prof Aliyu, who made this assertion at the University of Benin, Benin City, during PDTF Professional Chair in Renewable Energy: Close Out ceremony on Thursday, noted that as Nigeria’s energy landscape continues to evolve, there is a growing need for research institutions to develop practical and commercially viable solutions in renewable energy and other emerging technologies.

Aliyu, who was represented at the occasion by Ereh Iyalla, Head Gas Division, PTDF, asserted that the seminar theme – Agrowaste to Fuel: Biodiesel Development, Opportunities and Challenges for Youth Employment to the 21st Century – was timely and highly relevant to Nigeria’s quest for sustainable energy, environmental protection, economic diversification and youth employment.

The paper was delivered by Chairholder, Prof. Kensington Obahiagbaon.

Aliyu noted that: “The focus on converting agricultural waste into biodiesel demonstrates the potential of research and innovation to transform challenges into opportunities. Beyond providing an alternative energy source, such innovations can support waste management, entrepreneurship, local technology development and employment opportunities for young Nigerians.

He stated further that: “As Nigeria’s energy landscape ontinues to evolve, there is a growing need for research institutions to develop practical and commercially viable solutions in renewable energy and other emerging technologies.

“We therefore encourage researchers to ensure that reseach outcome move beyond academic publications to technology development, demonstration, industry adoption and commercialization.”

Prof Obahiagbaon, a professor of chemical engineering, in his presentation, noted that the global dependence on fossil diesel has created twin problems of gas emissions and energy insecurity.

According to him, global energy crisis, climate change, and waste management burden have made agro-waste to fuel a critical pathway for the 21st century, adding that using agro-waste as biodiesel feedstock is a core principle of the circular economy. “It converts a liability into an asset: waste becomes fuel, and waste management becomes a revenue stream.”

Speaking on the challenges and future direction of biodiesel development in Nigeria, Obahiagbaon said feedstock availability and cost, ensuring a stable and affordable supply remain crucial.

He advocated the development of sustainable standard for biodiesel production.

The Vice Chancellor, University of Benin, Prof. Edoba Omoregie (SAN), in his opening remarks, noted that in the past six years of your existence of the chair, it has proven to be a start-up for the institution.

“We will continue to partner with graduates in every field of study.”

According to him, everyone knows the importance of renewable energy.

“We are involved in this effort to try to draw attention to renewable energy as a major finding source of energy. Because of the problem of climate change, we know that it is worth looking at renewable energy sources to be able to mitigate the impact of climate change.”

World.title: Cross River Secures $20m Investment for 4,000-Hectare Oil Palm Plantation
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Cross River State Government has signed a concession agreement with ValueFronteira Limited for the development of a 4,000-hectare oil palm plantation in Ijiegu Yache and adjoining clans in Yala Local Government Area of the state, with the investor committing more than $20 million to the project over five years.

The project, which is expected to create thousands of jobs and boost agricultural production in six clans including Ijiegu, Wonye, Uchu, Ichui, Ukani and Ewor, is part of the state government’s agricultural transformation agenda aimed at strengthening food security, promoting rural development and improving livelihoods.

Speaking at a stakeholders’ meeting and site handover ceremony held in Ijiegu Yache, Cross River State, the Managing Director of ValueFronteira Limited, Maurice Ekpong, explained that the organisation would invest over $20 million within five years to establish the plantation.

He stated that the project would generate thousands of employment opportunities and significantly transform the economies of the host communities and Cross River State.

Ekpong’s announcement was welcomed by traditional rulers, community representatives, youths and women leaders, who expressed optimism that the investment would create jobs, particularly for young people, while improving economic activities and livelihoods across the communities.

The Clan Head of Wonye, HRH Mohie Damian Ododo, described the project as a dream come true, pledging the collective support of the clan heads for its successful implementation.

He also affirmed ValueFronteira as a corporate member of Yache land.

Other traditional rulers and representatives at the event included HRH Mohie Isaac Omaji, Clan Head of Ijiegu; HRH Mohie Innocent Okaiiba Aji, Clan Head of Ichui; HRH Mohie Ogar Idazor, Clan Head of Ukani; Augustine Obozor, representing Ewor Clan; and Pius Idagu, representing Uchu Clan.

In his remarks, the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor and Director-General of the Bureau of Public Private Partnerships, Dr. Francis Ntamu, assured stakeholders that the concession process was transparent and competitive, leading to ValueFronteira’s emergence as the preferred investor.

He disclosed that the project had received the full approval of the State Executive Council (SEC), adding that: “It aligns with the government’s drive to attract investment and strengthen critical sectors of the economy.”

He expressed the state government’s hope that the investment will contribute to positioning Cross River as a major agribusiness destination in Nigeria, while supporting its broader objectives of food security, rural development and economic empowerment.

“The development is expected to expand commercial agricultural activities in Yala, create employment opportunities and stimulate economic growth in the host communities,” Ntamu stressed.

The government delegation also included the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Environment and Solicitor-General of the state, Rosemary Onah, and Brian Ugbe, a Director in the Ministry of Agriculture, who represented the Commissioner for Agriculture.

World.title: NGX Group, Partners Advance Cross-Border Investment Collaboration Through Dangote Refinery Offer in Egypt, Ethiopia
World.content:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) and its partners are advancing cross-border investment collaboration among African capital markets, with engagements in Cairo, Egypt and Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, exploring how market infrastructure and institutional partnerships can improve investment access across the continent. Using the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE offer as a practical context, the discussions focused on connecting investors across jurisdictions and mobilising African capital for industrial development.

Held on Thursday, the engagements were hosted in Cairo by the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), in collaboration with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), and in Addis Ababa by the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX). They brought together exchange leaders, financial institutions and other capital market stakeholders to explore practical approaches to improving market connectivity, broadening investor participation and mobilising African capital for productive investment.

Speaking during the discussions, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, Temi Popoola, emphasized the importance of addressing longstanding structural barriers that limit investment flows across African markets. He noted that the continent possesses substantial pools of institutional capital, but stronger market infrastructure and cooperation are needed to connect these resources with investment opportunities across national borders. “Africa has substantial capital within its own markets, particularly across pension funds and insurance companies. The challenge is how to connect that capital to investment opportunities across the continent.

The Dangote Refinery offer provides a practical opportunity to address some of the infrastructure barriers to cross-border investment. Beyond a single transaction, it is about creating connections that enable African capital to finance African growth,” Popoola said.

President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, highlighted the refinery as an example of the scale of industrial investment required to strengthen Africa’s productive capacity, reduce dependence on imports and support long-term economic growth. He emphasised the importance of developing stronger channels through which African capital can support major industrial projects across the continent. He also commended NGX Group for its role in bringing African exchanges together around the initiative and acknowledged the participating exchanges for their collaboration.

Group Chairman of NGX Group, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, stressed that lasting progress would depend on sustained institutional cooperation and the development of market infrastructure that makes cross-border investment more accessible and efficient. “Our task is not simply to collaborate around one offer, but to develop lasting partnerships that support cross-border investment and capital formation across Africa. This requires cooperation among exchanges, regulators, financial institutions and businesses, alongside investment in the infrastructure and technology that make participation more accessible,” Kwairanga said.

At the Cairo engagement, Executive Chairman of the Egyptian Exchange, Omar Radwan, highlighted the potential for instruments such as Egyptian Depositary Receipts (EDRs) to provide a channel through which Egyptian investors could access selected African businesses. He expressed EGX’s readiness to work with Dangote Industries to explore a possible framework for such an arrangement.

President and Chairman of Afreximbank, Dr. George Elombi, reaffirmed the bank’s longstanding financing relationship with Dangote Industries and its commitment to supporting African industrial development. He highlighted the importance of mobilising African investment towards enterprises capable of contributing to the continent’s economic transformation.

In Addis Ababa, discussions focused on expanding investment opportunities for Ethiopian investors and strengthening Ethiopia’s participation in Africa’s evolving capital market landscape.

Chief Executive Officer of ESX, Yodit Kassa, welcomed the engagement, noting its significance for Ethiopian investors and the country’s growing capital market. “The Dangote Petroleum Refinery offer represents an important opportunity for Ethiopian investors to participate in the growth of one of Africa’s leading industrial enterprises. It also reflects the growing confidence in Ethiopia’s capital market and our readiness to work with leading institutions across the continent,” Kassa said.

The Cairo and Addis Ababa engagements followed earlier stops at the Nairobi Securities Exchange and the Botswana Stock Exchange, extending discussions on cross-border investment across multiple African markets. The discussions also highlighted the practical requirements for cross-border participation, including regulatory recognition, distribution, investor verification, settlement, custody and access to reliable information. The offer provides a real-world opportunity for exchanges, regulators, intermediaries and financial technology platforms to address these considerations and explore workable solutions within their respective regulatory frameworks. For participating markets, it also raises the question of how local savings can be channelled more efficiently into productive enterprises across the continent.

NGX Group remains committed to working with partner exchanges and financial institutions to strengthen market infrastructure, expand cross-border investment access and advance collaboration among African capital markets, contributing to the continent’s long-term economic and industrial development.

World.title: Beyond the NYSC Camp: Cross River’s rot, the locust years, and the demands of recovery
World.content:
Joseph Odok

The outrage over the dilapidated National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) Orientation Camp in Obubra is justified and overdue. Corps members have endured crumbling hostels, inadequate water, failing sanitation and facilities so degraded that the NYSC leadership has threatened or moved to suspend further postings. Capacity has collapsed from roughly 2,500 per stream to little more than 1,000, with hundreds seeking relocation. The state government’s swift decision to shut the camp for comprehensive overhaul and temporarily relocate orientation exercises to the University of Education and Entrepreneurship in Akamkpa is the correct, responsible response. Yet the camp is merely the most visible tip of a much larger iceberg of institutional and infrastructural decay that accumulated over years of announcements without delivery.​

That decay did not begin in 2023. It was deepened, accelerated and normalised during the eight years of Benedict Ayade’s administration. Those were the locust years: budgets of kinetic crystallisation, quabalistic densification, olimpotic meristemasis and quantum infinitum that promised first-world transformation while delivering near-zero performance. Signature projects (the Bakassi Deep Seaport, an international airport, Super High way, dozens of factories) were commissioned on billboards, in television studios and newspaper pages far more often than they appeared as functioning realities on the ground.

Of the much-trumpeted 38 factories, the overwhelming majority remained empty shells or stalled constructions years later. Tinapa, once a bold statement of ambition, was left to weeds and debt. The civil service grew demoralised; promotions stagnated for years; morale sank. Critical maintenance (desilting of drainage channels, upkeep of fire service assets) was neglected. Fire vehicles fell into disrepair or were effectively lost to the system without adequate replacement; today’s limited operational capacity is the product of remedial effort.of Governor Bassey Otu not inheritance.​

Floods and erosion that now regularly embarrass the state are not acts of God alone. They are the predictable consequence of years in which systematic desilting and drainage maintenance received deaf ears. The same pattern held for roads, erosion-control sites and public institutions. Projects were announced with fanfare and then left to rot or to the mercy of contractors who delivered substandard work. Most road were rather painted with tar and not asphalt and they decayed within time frame of their construction. Yala became a home of dust, Obudu and Bekwara roads are still a consequence of Ayade’s mess. Major parts of CRS were disconnected from the national grid with many communities no longer having access to electricity on a phantom promise of power plant that were nothing but avenue to loot the state. The cost of destruction is always lower than the cost of rebuilding. Cross River is still paying that price.

Those who raised these issues during the Ayade years were not always celebrated as patriots. Some were treated as enemies of the state. Critics faced arrest and prolonged detention on inflated charges. I spent 117 days in custody for the offence of speaking uncomfortable truths. Many residents, conditioned by the politics of “food on the table” and praise-singing, dismissed such criticism as personal hatred. Today some of the same voices who once defended or ignored the rot have discovered sudden rage against Governor Bassey Otu. The injustice lies less in the existence of legitimate impatience than in the selective amnesia that denies the scale of what was inherited and the direction of the current recovery effort.

A government reflects the mood of its people. Years of applause for grandiose budgets and digital inauguration ceremonies helped produce the decayed Cross River we now inhabit. The emerging public consciousness that refuses to allow leaders to sleep is healthier for democracy. It is already yielding concrete results. The rapid government intervention on the NYSC camp is one. The handling of the Denis Odama matter (where the governor directed the withdrawal of a complaint initiated by aides and secured the critic’s release) is another signal that this administration can still distinguish between accountability and vengeance.

Ongoing desilting exercises, efforts to restore fire service capacity after long neglect, recovery of Tinapa from years of limbo, road works across several corridors, and attempts to stabilise a demoralised civil service form part of a policy direction of recovery, consolidation and gradual development. These efforts sit on the foundation left by earlier administrations, including those of Duke and Imoke, and seek to reverse the damage of the intervening locust years.

None of this excuses slow delivery or substandard remedial work. Cross Riverians are right to demand higher standards. More federal transfers and improved revenue create an opportunity, yet the accumulated rot far exceeds what any single budget cycle can erase. Governor Otu must recognise the impatience of a people who have waited too long. He must cut waste deliberately, communicate more transparently about the use of public funds, and ensure that rehabilitation meets acceptable quality thresholds. Accountability and openness are not optional extras; they are the only durable foundation for the recovery agenda.

It is easier to destroy than to rebuild. The present outrage, if channelled constructively rather than as selective bitterness, can accelerate the rebuilding. Cross River deserves leaders who treat criticism as feedback rather than treason, and citizens who remember how the rot was allowed to deepen. The NYSC camp is a symptom. The cure requires sustained vigilance, honest reckoning with the past eight years of non-performance, and a government that matches the people’s rising expectations with visible, measurable, transparent action. That is the standard against which recovery must be judged.

. Dr Joseph Abang Odok, a Senior Lecturer, a Social Change Agent, a Lawyer and a Philosopher, writes from Lokoja

World.title: WACOT Renews Strategic Partnership with Edo Govt to Drive Agricultural Transformation
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor

WACOT Limited, has extended its agreement with the Edo State Government on fertilizer production through the Edo State Fertilizer and Chemical Company Limited (ESFCCL) in Auchi.

The partnership which commenced in 2017, reaffirms both parties’ commitment to boosting local fertilizer production, supporting smallholder farmers, and advancing Nigeria’s food security.

Speaking on the significance of the facility from an industry perspective, the President of the Fertilizer Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN) and Director, Corporate Affairs, TGI Group Mr. Sadiq Kassim, said: “The Auchi facility is of strategic importance to Nigeria’s fertilizer industry and national food security. It is the only plant in the South-South with the capability to produce tailored, crop-specific fertilizer blends suited to the region’s soil requirements. The facility also has the capability to produce specialised chemical blends to meet the specific needs of the North-East, where security challenges have made establishing fertilizer production facilities particularly difficult.”

Also commenting on the renewed partnership, the Managing Director of WACOT Limited, Mr. Naveen Chaurasia, said: “The renewal of this agreement is a strong statement of our long-term commitment to Edo State and to Nigeria’s agricultural transformation. Since 2017, we have demonstrated that a well-managed public-private partnership can revive moribund assets and deliver real value.”

Speaking on behalf of the Edo State government, Commissioner, Ministry of Business, Trade and Investments, Omoh Anabor, added: “This agreement involving the Edo State Government, ESFCCL and WACOT Limited represents far more than a formal transaction. It is a strategic step towards positioning Edo State as a leading destination for investment and industrial growth. This partnership demonstrates our readiness to work with credible private sector partners to unlock economic opportunities, support farmers through improved access to agricultural inputs, strengthen food security, create jobs and enterprise opportunities across Auchi and the wider Edo State.”

World.title: 2027: CSO Coalition Cautions Enugu Guber Candidates, Demands Issue-Based Campaigns
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Coalition of Civil Society Groups for Good Governance (CCSGG) Thursday cautioned governorship candidates in Enugu State against inflammatory politics and smear campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging them to present verifiable development agendas to the electorate.

The coalition, which said it comprises over 52 civil society organisations committed to promoting accountability and good governance, stated this at a world press conference themed: “Enugu State and the Politics of 2027: Putting the Record Straight.” in Abuja

Addressing journalists on behalf of coalition, Comrade Okpanachi Jacob, said the group intervention became necessary following the controversy surrounding the incident at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu, on October 10, 2026, involving supporters of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

He noted that the group investigated the matter after statements attributed to the NDC governorship candidate, Sir Christian Chinyeaka Ohaa, and others, which linked the Enugu State Government to the incident.

The coalition described the suggestion that a political rally was to be held at an international airport as deeply concerning and inconsistent with established standards for aviation security.

It noted that according to accounts released by the Enugu State Government and the Enugu State Police Command, the NDC had publicised a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the airport, was advised to secure approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), but allegedly proceeded without such approval, leading to a confrontation when security personnel restricted access.

The coalition therefore posed five questions to the NDC to answer in public interest, stating:

“Did the party obtain formal approval from the appropriate federal airport authorities for the gathering? If approval was obtained, will the party publish it for public scrutiny? What instructions were given to party members concerning access to the airport? Why was a large political gathering planned for a sensitive federal facility? What credible evidence directly connects Governor Peter Mbah or any identified state official to the confrontation?

“Freedom of association and peaceful assembly are constitutional democratic rights. However, those rights must be exercised lawfully and responsibly. Political enthusiasm does not override aviation security,” the coalition said.

It urged politicians to desist from disseminating misleading information, stressing that airports are sensitive federal facilities whose security and operations must not be compromised by partisan activities.

The coalition said Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah is not above criticism, noting that citizens, opposition parties and journalists have the right to question his policies, scrutinise public expenditure and demand transparency. However, it said criticism must be based on facts and not on demonisation or allegations unsupported by evidence.

“Accusation without evidence is not accountability. It is political blackmail capable of inflaming passions, misleading the public and undermining the peace and security of Enugu State,” the group said.

The group stressed that opposition status does not confer immunity from regulations governing airports, political gatherings and public order. Adding: “It said all political parties must notify appropriate authorities of major public activities, comply with lawful security requirements and ensure members do not engage in violence or destruction of public property.

It also called on security agencies to remain professional, impartial and proportionate, ensuring a level playing field for all parties while respecting citizens’ rights to peaceful assembly.

The coalition warned against importing thugs, arming supporters, spreading unfounded security alarms or manufacturing confrontations for propaganda, urging security agencies to investigate reports of attempts to recruit armed persons ahead of 2027.

World.title: Nigerians Can Grow Capital, Assets Through Cooperatives, Says Adesope
World.content:
Nigerians can grow their capital, assets and income through cooperative societies, the newly elected President of The Bodija (Ibadan) Unique Cooperative Investment & Credit Society, Mr Olufemi Adesope, has said.

Adesope urged managers of cooperative societies to encourage members to save and invest more consistently while developing attractive investment products and expanding their investment portfolios to ensure continuous growth in capital, assets, income and members’ return on investment.

He made the call while assuming office for the 2026/2027 Cooperative Year at the society’s ninth Annual General Meeting held at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan.

Describing his new responsibility as a call to duty, Adesope said, “We must build on our successes, learn from our experiences and deliberately position Unique Cooperative Society for greater heights.”

Speaking on the theme of the AGM, ‘Building Bridges, Empowering Members: Cooperatives in the Digital Age,’ he called for a shift from dependence on traditional cooperative activities to identifying viable businesses, property investments, community projects and other sustainable income-generating opportunities.

“The Society should continuously ask: ‘What new opportunities can create additional value for our members?’” he said.

Adesope also stressed the need to build relationships with credible financial institutions, professional organisations, businesses, technology companies, other cooperatives and development institutions.

He called for continuous training of members and leaders in financial literacy, investment, entrepreneurship, leadership and digital skills.

On the need to adapt to developments in the financial world, the new president advocated the digitalisation and automation of the society’s operations.

He said this should cover member registration, savings, loans, investment monitoring, communication, reporting and performance tracking.

“Technology should make the Society faster, more transparent, accessible and efficient,” he said.

Adesope, while commending the Board of Trustees, including the society’s foundation president and past president, Mr Olusegun Sanni and Mr Gbolahan Arogundade, respectively, for their guidance, wisdom and continuing support, said the new leadership would maintain the highest standards of transparency, prudent financial management, risk control and accountability.

He also called for measurable annual targets for membership, savings, investments, income, assets and member benefits, with regular performance reviews to ensure progress.

“ Our goal must not merely be to preserve what we have built, but to continuously grow, improve and create greater value for every member,” he said.

Also speaking at the AGM, the keynote speaker, Professor Sulaiman Adesina Yusuf of the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Ibadan, advised people seeking steady financial growth to join cooperative and credit societies and pool resources with others.

Yusuf, a professor of agricultural economics, urged members to participate regularly in the growth process and allow their collective investments to grow over time.

Speaking on the theme, ‘Building Bridges, Empowering Members: Cooperatives in the Digital Age,’ he challenged cooperative leaders to avoid the pitfalls of the past by embracing digital transformation to encourage more people to join their societies.

However, he cautioned that the human element of cooperative societies must not be overlooked in the drive towards digitalisation.

“Let us be honest with each other: a digital notice is not the same thing as meaningful participation. An app cannot manufacture trust,” he said.

Yusuf explained that technology could strengthen transparency and accountability by enabling members to access their balances, decisions and records.

“What it can do, if we build it honestly, is make trust visible: a balance a member can check, a decision a member can read, a record a member can request.

“Technology can support accountability. It cannot take responsibility for it. That responsibility still belongs to us, the leadership and the membership of this cooperative.”

World.title: Weather: Heat gives way to afternoon storms and strong winds
World.content:
Hot conditions could give way to afternoon thunderstorms and strengthening winds in parts of South Africa. Image: Unsplash

Here is what the weather has in store for KZN, the Free State, and the North West on Saturday 17 October 2026.

A heatwave with persistently high temperatures is expected in northern KwaZulu-Natal until Sunday.

Meanwhile, hot to very hot conditions will cause extreme discomfort in eastern parts of the province.

It will become partly cloudy in the afternoon with isolated showers and thundershowers in the south.

The wind along the coast will be moderate to fresh northerly to north-easterly, becoming fresh to strong southerly to south-westerly south of Durban by mid-morning spreading to Kosi Bay by evening.

The UVB sunburn index is going to be extreme.

Light northerly winds will blow in the morning before shifting to moderate to fresh southerly to south-westerly winds.



Temperatures will range from 22°C to 29°C.

The UVB sunburn index is going to be extreme.

It will be windy in the west.

Mahikeng is going to be fine, becoming partly cloudy in the afternoon.

Temperatures will range from a minimum of 17°C. to a maximum of 35°C.

World.title: Zim bus drivers face charges in SA after 65 passengers found without passports
World.content:
Two Zimbabwean bus drivers face charges in South Africa after authorities intercepted their vehicles carrying 65 passengers without passports, including 28 minors, near Polokwane in Limpopo.

The buses were stopped on the N1 on Friday morning after they were found to be overloaded, with a combined 178 passengers on board, according to the Limpopo Department of Transport and Community Safety.

Department spokesperson Mashudu Mabata the drivers would be charged and detained under Section 42 of the Immigration Act 13 of 2002 for allegedly aiding and abetting illegal foreigners.



Zimbabwean buses found overloaded

Mabata said the first bus, which had a carrying capacity of 75 passengers, was found to be carrying 88 people, exceeding its limit by 13.

Fifteen passengers on board reportedly did not have passports, including six minors and nine adults.

The bus was also found to be overweight by 1,080kg on its first axle and was issued with a spot fine.



The second bus had a carrying capacity of 74 passengers but was found to be transporting 90 people, exceeding its limit by 16.

According to Mabata, 50 passengers on the second bus did not have passports. They comprised 28 adults and 22 minors.

The two buses were escorted to the Polokwane weighbridge for further checks.



Immigration officials conduct checks

Immigration officials and K9 dogs were deployed to verify the passengers’ documentation and conduct further inspections.

Mabata confirmed that authorities would take action against the drivers.

“The two drivers will be charged and detained in terms of Section 42 of the Immigration Act 13 of 2002: aiding and abetting of illegal foreigners,” she said.



The department’s statement did not provide further details about the drivers’ court appearances or the outcome of the immigration checks.

World.title: ‘R6000 per month’: Pensioners push SASSA for a bigger grant
World.content:
South Africans are calling for a major increase to the Older Persons Grant, with some saying the current amount falls far short of what pensioners need to live with dignity.

The comments came in response to a post on The South African’s Facebook page, where grant recipients and their supporters shared what they believe a fair monthly payment should look like.

The Older Persons Grant currently pays R2 400 per month to recipients aged 60 and older.



The R6 000 call by pensioners

John Berry put forward one of the boldest suggestions in the thread, calling for the grant to more than double and for the payment cycle to change.

“Make it R6 000 rand per month on a 28-day cycle for old age pensioners this would provide them with a living income and a form of dignity,” Berry wrote.

His comment drew reactions from other users, with several showing support for the idea that pensioners deserve more than basic survival.

A 28-day cycle would mean 13 payments a year instead of 12, giving pensioners an extra payout annually on top of the higher amount Berry proposed.

‘Even if we could start off with 3000’

Not everyone aimed as high. Willie Doyer took a more modest approach, suggesting that even a smaller increase would make a difference for older persons.

“Even if we could start with R3 000,” Doyer wrote.



For many older South Africans who rely on the grant as their main source of income, that amount could cover essentials such as electricity, transport or medication.

Doyer’s comment reflects a sentiment shared by many grant recipients: a gradual increase would be welcome, even if a living income remains out of reach for now.

Pressure on the cost of living

The calls for a higher grant come as older persons continue to face rising costs for food, electricity and transport.

Many pensioners support not only themselves but also grandchildren and unemployed family members, which stretches the monthly grant even further.

SASSA grant amounts are set by National Treasury and usually adjust each year during the national Budget, with increases taking effect in April.

Until then, pensioners will continue to make do with the current amount while voicing their hopes for a bigger payout.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Heartbreaking final post from St Anne’s matric student who took her life
World.content:
St Anne’s Diocesan College matric learner Reneiloe Monkhi’s final repost about ending her life has shed light on her state of mind. Not long after, the KwaZulu-Natal teen ended her life via suicide

ST ANNE’S MATRIC LEARNER REPOSTED ABOUT MENTAL HEALTH

In a statement on their Facebook account, St Anne’s Diocesan College announced the sad passing of one of their Grade 12 learners, Reneilwe Monkhi.

The KwaZulu-Natal private school for girls revealed that the teen had ended her life via suicide. Her death came days after the school advocated for students to prioritise their mental health amid impending matric exams.



In the comments section, a few of her peers pointed to her final social media posts, particularly her telling TikTok repost.

Three days ago, Reneilwe reposted a clip of a scene from the 2012 film Disconnect, in which a suicide attempt scene plays out.

Over the video was the text: “The state ‘ll be found in soon enough”



Reneiloe’s social media accounts have since been made private.

BEST FRIEND SPEAKS OUT

Hours after her death was announced, Reneiloe Monkhi’s best friend Lihle Mnyaka shared a touching tribute to her.

The Instagram post featured photos and video clips of their friendship.



Lihle also posted pictures of St Anne’s Matric Dance, where she joined Reineiloe and other friends.

She shared: “I genuinely don’t even know how to put into words what I’m feeling. My heart is so heavy, and I still can’t believe that I’m having to write this. The world feels a little less beautiful without you in it, and I wish more than anything that things could have been different.

“I hope you know how loved you are, Riri. I hope you knew how much you mattered and how many lives you touched just by being you. You deserved so much more time, so many more memories, and so many more beautiful moments.



MATRICS 2026: HELP IS AVAILABLE

Meanwhile, SADAG are sharing their top tips to help maric students navigate their final exams and their mental health.

The organisation posts a TikTok live every Thursday, tackling topics relevant to end-of-year student stress.



They also host interactive support groups via their social media platforms.

World.title: SA Rugby: Hyron Andrews died in ‘accident’
World.content:
Lions lock forward Hyron Andrews passed away tragically on Friday while on tour with the team, and on the eve of their Champions Cup opener against La Rochelle on Saturday.

Andrews was pronounced dead after medical personnel responded to the scene.

Initial reports suggested that the 31-year-old had died of a suspected heart attack, but in the statement from SA Rugby, it was suggested that he had passed away “following an accident while on duty with his team in France”.



SA Rugby stated that he “died after falling at the team’s hotel”.

CONDOLENCES POUR IN AFTER DEATH OF HYRON ANDREWS

Andrews, who was born in Paarl and attended Hoërskool Garsfontein in Pretoria, represented the Junior Springboks in 2015 and also played for the KZN Sharks and Sale Sharks in England.

“This is terrible and distressing news; our hearts go out to Hyron’s family and the whole Lions rugby community,” said Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union.

“There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maighlin, and for his extended family, friends, teammates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.

“Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.

“His untimely passing is a devastating loss, and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.



“The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maighlin and all those mourning his loss. May they find strength, comfort and peace in the memories they shared with him and in the support of those around them.”

LIONS MATCH TO GO AHEAD

According to a statement, the Lions squad, as a group, have chosen to play on Saturday in honour of their teammate.

In memory of Andrews, a moment’s silence will be held ahead of every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend.

EPCR Chairman Dominic McKay said: “The thoughts of everyone at EPCR and the wider international rugby community are with Hyron’s wife Maiglin, his young sons, wider family, friends, teammates, the Lions and all those who knew and loved him at this incredibly difficult time.”

World.title: Lions confirm death of star lock
World.content:
In tragic news that came to light on Friday, the Lions confirmed the death of veteran lock Hyron Andrews while on tour with the team ahead of their Champions Cup and United Rugby Championship fixtures.

This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community.

“The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family, and his loss will be felt profoundly by his teammates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him,” the statement from the Lions read.



“Our deepest and most heartfelt condolences go to Hyron’s wife, Maiglin, their young sons, and the entire Andrews family. We hold them in our thoughts during this time of unimaginable grief and ask that their privacy be respected as they mourn. May Hyron rest in peace.”

Lions and rugby community at large in shock following death of Hyron Andrews

Rudolf Straeuli, Chief Executive Officer of the Lions Rugby Company added: “We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family having recently joined us this season.

“On behalf of our Chairman, Mr Altmann Allers, the board and everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to Maiglin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect.”

The Lions Rugby Company said they would communicate further details regarding an appropriate tribute in due course.

In honour of the 31-year-old, the Lions will fulfil their opening match of the Champions Cup against La Rochelle on Saturday (18:30) South African time.

Tragic incident

As reported by TheSouthAfrican, Andrews is believed to have been found unresponsive in a shower stall at the team hotel.



Emergency services arrived shortly after 10am on Friday, but were unable to revive the player, who was pronounced dead at the scene.

Although the cause of death has yet to be confirmed, SA Rugby stated that it was an “accident”.

The hotel confirmed to local website Ici La Rochelle that a psychological support unit had been set up for the Lions players and staff, as well as the hotel personnel.

Andrews – who was born in Pretoria – began his senior career at the Sharks, where he featured in more than 100 games in all competitions.

In 2024, he moved abroad to play for the Sale Sharks in England, racking up nearly 50 caps before heading to the Lions. He was also capped twice by the Junior Springboks.

World.title: What happened to Springbok legend Bryan Habana after retirement?
World.content:
During his playing days, Bryan Habana was undoubtedly one of South Africa’s biggest names in rugby.

The retired winger was renowned for his explosive pace and finishing ability at his peak and is widely regarded as one of the greatest players to have played the game.

He famously raced a cheetah in a publicity stunt that attracted worldwide attention.



Having started his professional career with the Lions, Habana joined the Bulls in 2005, where he went on to win two Super Rugby titles and a Currie Cup.

In 2010, he moved to the Stormers, helping the Cape side win the Currie Cup in 2012 before joining French giants Toulon a year later.

Bryan Habana scored 67 tries for the Springboks

Although Habana dominated South African rugby for much of his career, his greatest moments arguably came in the Springbok jersey.



At international level, he earned 124 Test caps and played a key role in South Africa’s triumph at the 2007 Rugby World Cup. His outstanding performances that year earned him the IRB Player of the Year award.

Habana continued to make history on the international stage. During the 2015 Rugby World Cup, he equalled Jonah Lomu’s record of 15 career tries at the tournament.

He finished his international career with 67 Test tries, placing him second on the all-time men’s Test try-scoring list.



What is Bryan Habana doing now?

Since retiring from professional rugby in 2018, Habana has remained involved in the sport through various ambassadorial, punditry and broadcasting roles. He has also delivered talks around the world, sharing insights from his illustrious career.

Beyond rugby, Habana has continued to pursue his philanthropic ambitions. His desire to give back to the community led him to establish the Bryan Habana Foundation.

While he may no longer be dazzling fans on the rugby field, the Springbok legend continues to use his profile and experience to contribute to the sport and make a difference beyond it.



Bryan Habana’s record of 67 tries in the Boks jersey will not be broken soon.

World.title: Three changes: Orlando Pirates’ expected starting 11 vs African Stars
World.content:
Orlando Pirates players warm up at the Orlando Amstel Arena. Image: Orlando Pirates media

African football is back with its CAF Champions League this weekend. Orlando Pirates and African Stars’ second round preliminary qualifier first leg kicks-off at the Gaborone Stadium on Saturday. Kick-off is set for 15:00.

CAF CHAMPIONS LEAGUE: AFRICAN STARS VS ORLANDO PIRATES

World.title: 'I'm dizzy' - businessman Suliman Carrim tells court
World.content:
PRETORIA - North West businessman Suliman Carrim has insisted he did not abandon the Madlanga Commission.

Carrim maintained his claim that his absence from the Commission was due to medical reasons.

He also complained about feeling ill during his appearance at the Pretoria Magistrate's Court.

" Up to now, my psychiatrist and all the reports are available. They are with the Commission. I am still not in the condition. Even what's happening to me right now, I've briefed my counsel. I've not taken my medication.

"I can feel my mouth is dry. I'm dizzy. I just told my counsel about it. I'm still under that condition. But I did say, and I need to put this on record, in my warning statement yesterday, I did say that I was going to get this medical treatment to get better to come back to the commission. It's in my warning statement."

World.title: 'He has a heart condition' - Carrim lawyer tells the court
World.content:
PRETORIA - Suliman Carrim's arrest and court appearance are already taking a toll on his health.

That is a warning from his lawyer, advocate Hendrik Potgieter.

Potgieter claimed his client has a heart condition and fears the anxiety of the case could trigger a panic attack.

Carrim was arrested at OR Tambo International Airport after failing to appear before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry multiple times.

"The accused person that appears before court, it's known and it was, now if one listens to the summary given from the Commission by my learned friend, we know that he's got a heart condition that the Commission accepted on occasions to postpone the matter because of the heart condition that he was hospitalised during that period for the heart condition.

"Your Worship, I'm informed by the accused person that the stress and the anxiety is taking a toll on him. He didn't use any medication this morning and he further states that he can feel that it might lead to a panic attack which would be detrimental to his medical condition."

World.title: Carrim to spend weekend behind bars
World.content:
PRETORIA - Suliman Carrim will spend the weekend behind bars.

This comes as his bail hearing was rolled over to Monday.

Carrim appeared at the Pretoria Magistrate's Court after being arrested at OR Tambo International Airport.

In hand, he had a one-way ticket and had five bags of luggage.

The state accuses Carrim of attempting to leave South Africa with no intention of returning.

He had repeatedly failed to appear before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

Carrim stands by his claim that his absence from the Commission was due to medical reasons.

He was trying to board a flight to the United Arab Emirates when he was arrested.

Carrim said his trip to Asia was for spiritual upliftment.

World.title: ‘Spiritual upliftment’: Where Carrim says he was headed
World.content:
PRETORIA - Suliman Carrim said his trip to Asia was for spiritual upliftment.

Carrim was arrested at OR Tambo International Airport on Thursday night.

The state accuses him of attempting to leave South Africa with no intention of returning.

He had repeatedly failed to appear before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

Carrim was trying to board a flight to the United Arab Emirates when he was arrested.

The North West businessman is appearing in court in Pretoria.

READ: Madlanga Commission welcomes Suliman Carrim's arrest

Carrim said he was heading to Saudi Arabia via Dubai to perform a pilgrimage.

"Spiritual upliftment, and from here I travel to Pakistan to my spiritual guide, where we do humanitarian work," Carrim told the court.

"I've been doing this trip for the last 16 years."

Carrim said he would've been back in Johannesburg on 27 October at 8:30pm.

World.title: Madlanga Commission welcomes Suliman Carrim's arrest
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Madlanga Commission has welcomed Suliman Carrim's arrest.



The North West businessman is appearing in court after being arrested at OR Tambo International Airport.



He had repeatedly failed to appear before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.
