World.title: A Tamaulipas teen built a fire extinguisher that puts out flames using sound
World.content:
A 17-year-old from the northeastern state of Tamaulipas is competing at an international science fair in Indonesia this week with a device she spent a year developing — a fire extinguisher that snuffs out small flames with sound instead of water or chemicals.

Ángela Karime Venegas Hernández is representing Mexico at the International Science and Invention Fair with Vortex Tech, a prototype developed with the help of her uncle, José Arturo Hernández Muñoz.

Her school, CETis 78 in Altamira, Tamaulipas, announced her participation in the fair being held this week at the University of Indonesia in Depok, near Jakarta.

Photographs shared by Mexico’s federal technical education agency showed Venegas wearing traditional Mexican clothing at the fair.

Venegas told the newspaper El País that a video of a large, roughly 4-meter (13-foot) sonic cannon extinguishing a flame — with air movement, not water or chemicals — inspired her to investigate whether she could build a smaller device.

She and her uncle, who holds a master’s degree in science, according to the Tamaulipas Education Ministry, spent about a year developing five prototypes, building on earlier experiments by others.

Just to create the first prototype — one that could extinguish a candle — took two months, not including preliminary research, she told the newspaper.

Vortex Tech uses a 12-volt battery, a frequency generator set to 30 hertz, an amplifier and a speaker. A modified bucket channels the output toward a flame.

According to Venegas’ explanation, the sound generates swirling rings of air that disrupt the oxygen supply sustaining combustion, extinguishing small flames within seconds.

The technology remains experimental. The newspaper El Universal reported that it works on small, nearby flames and does not replace conventional extinguishers for large fires.

Tamaulipas education officials said the project also includes thermal sensors designed to detect a developing fire and automatically activate the sound-based extinguishing system.

The state Education Ministry said Venegas advanced through regional, state and national competitions before qualifying for Indonesia. It also pledged support for her and her uncle/adviser’s participation.

With reports from El País, El Heraldo de México and El Universal

World.title: 2,500-year-old astronomical observatory in Puebla confirmed to be the oldest in Mexico
World.content:
A pre-Hispanic solar observatory in the municipality of Teteles de Ávila Castillo in the Sierra Norte region of Puebla has been confirmed to be the oldest in Mexico, dating back more than 2,500 years.

According to research carried out by the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), a monumental architectural complex named “Grupo E” functioned as a solar astronomical observatory and is the oldest of its kind in Mexico.

Researchers believe the settlement’s inhabitants incorporated astronomical observations into the planning of their ceremonial buildings more than two millennia ago.

Heritage Daily —a digital publication specializing in archaeology, anthropology and palaeontology — says the discovery “provides remarkable evidence of sophisticated astronomical knowledge among ancient Mesoamerican civilizations.”

INAH says it is the first discovery of its kind outside the Maya region and is comparable to the observatory at the archaeological site of Uaxactún in Petén, Guatemala, which has been identified as the first and defining archetype for ancient Maya astronomical observation complexes.

While both the Uaxactún and Teteles complexes are believed to date to the Middle Preclassic (from 1200 to 400 BCE.), the Uaxactún structure is approximately twice the size of the one in Puebla.

Researchers have confirmed that the original layout of the “Group E” settlement (also known as Tetelihtic) and the orientation of its pyramidal structures are based on an understanding of celestial bodies.

Archaeologist Alberto Diez Barroso said the ancient settlement is an outstanding example of pre-Hispanic urban planning — shaped by the observation of the surrounding landscape, such as the nearby mountain peaks, as well as the astronomical horizon — making it “a significant point of reference for Mesoamerican studies in this field.”

Tetelihtic consists of a quadrangular courtyard flanked by two platforms at its eastern and western ends. The eastern platform is elongated (90 m from south to north by 40 m from east to west), while the western structure is smaller (46 m from north to south by 27 m from east to west) and served as an observation point.

The elongated platform does not mark the equinoxes at its center, however.

“It apparently served to establish the beginning of the pre-Hispanic Mesoamerican calendar in February and the harvest period in October, making it a complex and unique feature,” Diez said.

However, the eastern platform did function as a solar calendar; observations have confirmed that, from its front, one can track the sun’s path at dawn during the equinoxes and solstices.

Archaeologists believe the finding could provide insights into the cultural relationship between the Huastec and Maya groups during the early stages of human settlement in the Sierra Norte as it serves to confirm the Maya ethnolinguistic roots of the Huastec groups.

A Maya presence at Teteles may date back as far as 3,000 years — a possibility suggested by the Puebla observatory.

With reports from INAH, Heritage Daily and Ambas Manos

World.title: Mexico targets cheap Chinese bicycles with six-month anti-dumping duty
World.content:
Mexico has imposed a provisional anti-dumping duty of US $68.60 per unit on adult bicycles originating from China, after the Economy Ministry preliminarily determined that Chinese bicycles were being sold below fair market value, harming domestic manufacturers.

The measure, which took effect on Oct. 13, will remain in place for six months and will apply to adult bicycles with a wheel size larger than 20 inches, including urban and mountain models, with or without gears, as well as unassembled units. Electric bicycles and racing or road bikes are excluded from the measure.

The decision traced back to an anti-dumping investigation requested in April 2025 by the National Association of Bicycle Manufacturers and the companies Mercurio, Veloci, Benotto and Línea Siete. The investigation formally began in August of that year.

According to preliminary results, Chinese bicycles accounted for 95% of Mexico’s imports of adult bicycles in 2024. Apparent national consumption of Chinese bicycles rose from 53% in 2022 to 61% in 2024, while the average price of imports fell 35% during that period.

In 2024, Chinese bicycles cost 27% less than their domestic counterparts. According to the Economy Ministry, this difference pressured the Mexican industry to reduce prices by 4% to stay competitive.

As more low-cost Chinese bicycles entered the country, Mexican manufacturers saw a significant drop in business. The Economy Ministry found that between 2022 and 2024, adult bicycle production fell by 34% and domestic sales declined by 32%. Meanwhile, employment dropped by 29%.

Sales revenue in the domestic market fell by 36% in the same period, while the industry’s operating profits swung into the red, a 111% drop. These figures led investigators to conclude that low-priced Chinese imports caused material harm to Mexican manufacturers.

During the six months that the preliminary duty will remain in effect, interested parties may submit evidence for or against the measures, while the investigation continues to determine whether to establish more permanent duties.

The provisional anti-dumping duty is part of a broader trend toward increased trade protection in Mexico. According to data from the Economy Ministry, imports falling under the 1,463 tariff classifications subject to new levies — approved in December 2025 — declined by 23% between January and May 2026, compared to the same period the previous year.

China, the primary supplier of the goods subject to duties, was the hardest hit, as its tariffed goods fell by 28% — from $10.1 billion to $7.2 billion.

With reports from Milenio and Diario de Tabasco

World.title: American Airlines is the latest carrier to drop service to Tulum
World.content:
American Airlines is dropping flights from Miami to the Yucatán Peninsula destination of Tulum as part of its cutback of several international routes, including its Charlotte-Los Cabos service.

American (AA) — the largest U.S. airline by passenger numbers — joins other major carriers, including Aeroméxico and Volaris, in dropping or pausing routes to the resort town on the state of Quintana Roo’s Caribbean coast.

AA had already announced that its Miami-Tulum route would be on seasonal pause through Nov. 19, after which it would continue again until Dec. 1. The current plan is to then resume service one last time from Dec. 17 to January 5, 2027, before stopping it completely.

Los Cabos is also slated for service cuts

AA ended its service to Tulum from Charlotte, North Carolina, in February, 2025, less than a year after its launch. Next year, the only AA route from the U.S. to Tulum will be from or through the Dallas/Fort Worth hub.

American has also announced plans to remove its Charlotte-San José del Cabo route from its future schedule, after its current seasonal pause. The route was originally planned to return to normal operations in November, but the schedule now reportedly shows only sporadic operations.

That limited service will end in August of 2027. A possible motive for the discontinuation is that the route’s flights on average were just 73.69% full between June 2025 and June 2026.

With reports from Simple Flying

World.title: Rachel death toll rises to 8 in Baja California as newly formed Hurricane Trudy heads for Jalisco coast
World.content:
Listen to this article

While Pacific Coast residents are still reeling from the passage of Polo, Rachel and Simon, the newly formed Hurricane Trudy threatens to bring more chaos and disruption to the region.

Eight deaths have been attributed to Hurricane Rachel, while at least four people remain missing and the military has been actively carrying out search and rescue operations. And Simon, lurking near the Jalisco coast south of the tip of the Baja California Peninsula, is expected to remain a Category 1 hurricane through Friday.

In light of the devastation, President Claudia Sheinbaum on Thursday activated the Defense Ministry’s DN-III emergency protection plan and the Navy’s “Plan Marina.”

Sheinbaum also ordered the Interior Ministry to stay in close contact with the Baja California governor in order to provide any support that may be needed, especially as Simon is expected to move toward the peninsula on Saturday.

Last month, Polo — the second most-intense Pacific hurricane on record — made consecutive landfalls on the peninsula and then mainland Mexico on Sept. 29.

Now comes Trudy, which became a hurricane before dawn Thursday.

The storm system was located about 300 miles (480 kilometers) southwest of Acapulco and 445 miles (720 km) south-southeast of Manzanillo, Colima, while registering maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 km/h), with gusts of 93 mph (150 km/h).

According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC), Trudy is undergoing a period of rapid intensification as it moves northwest at 9 mph (15 km/h) and is expected to bring heavy rains to Oaxaca and Guerrero today (Thursday).

Forecast models project it will become a major hurricane as it approaches the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend, bringing rainfall of 4 to 8 inches (101 to 203 millimeters) through the weekend across Colima and Jalisco states.

Meanwhile, Simon remains virtually “frozen” a few hundred kilometers west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, and is expected to continue orbiting in place with sustained winds of 75 mph (120 km/h) and gusts of 95 mph (150 km/h).

Sustained winds were about 130 miles (210 kilometers) per hour as the week began, and the storm’s inner core was brushing up against the Jalisco coast.

The topography of the Sierra Madre mountains appeared to temper Simon’s intensity and shrink the size of its wind field, the NHC said. Still, as the storm system weakened from a Category 4 to Category 1 it delivered heavy rain and flooding to coastal areas, including the port city of Manzanillo, Colima.

With reports from La Jornada, The Associated Press, El Economista, Meteored and CNN en Español

World.title: International tourist spending grows 8% in August despite a dip in arrivals
World.content:
International tourist arrivals in Mexico declined year over year in August for the first time in almost a year, according to official data, even as total expenditure by international tourists increased by over 8%.

The national statistics agency INEGI reported Wednesday that 3.76 million international tourists came to Mexico in August, a decline of 0.5% compared to the same month of 2025.

International tourists are classified as foreign residents who spend at least one night in Mexico during their visit to the country.

In August, 1.39 million of the 3.76 million international tourists flew into the country, a decline of 6.5% compared to a year earlier. International tourist arrivals by air declined during every month between February and August.

The remainder of the international tourists in August entered Mexico by land, with most of that cohort staying within the northern or southern border region. INEGI’s data shows that two-thirds (67.1%) of the tourists who came to Mexico in August and traveled beyond the border regions are residents of the United States.

The year-over-year decline in international tourist arrivals in August was the first annual decrease since September 2025.

Humberto Molina, an expert in tourism economics at the consultancy firm Grupo Empresarial Estrategia, attributed the decline to a range of factors, including the presence of sargassum on Mexican beaches, insecurity and a lack of tourism promotion.

International tourist expenditure increased 8.1% in August

While in Mexico in August, international tourists collectively spent US $2.16 billion, an increase of 8.1% compared to the same month of 2025.

Each international tourist spent $573.30 on average, up 8.6% from August 2025.

Individual expenditure by international tourists who flew into Mexico was more than double that amount at $1,269.60, an increase of 15.2% compared to August 2025.

International tourists who flew into Mexico collectively spent $1.77 billion while in the country, a figure that accounts for 82% of total international tourism expenditure.

Despite decline in international tourists, international traveler numbers reached a record high in August

While international tourist numbers declined 0.5% year over year in August, international traveler numbers increased 1.3% to reach 7.98 million, the highest figure on record for the month of August.

INEGI’s international travelers category includes international tourists and international day-trippers (excursionistas internacionales). The latter enter Mexico by land or sea but don’t stay the night. International day-trippers include cruise ship passengers and people who spend a few hours in Mexico after entering the country via border crossings with the United States, Guatemala and Belize.

Just over 4.2 million international day-trippers came to Mexico in August, an increase of 3% compared to the same month of last year. Around 81% of the international day trippers (3.43 million) entered Mexico by land, while 785,558 came into the country by sea. Sea arrivals increased by 12.3% compared to August 2025, while land arrivals rose 1.1%.

Total spending by international travelers in Mexico in August was $2.4 billion, a 7% increase compared to a year earlier. International tourists spent 90% of that amount, while international day-trippers contributed the other 10%.

While expenditure rose in dollar terms, it declined 5.51% annually in real peso terms, according to Banco Base analysts, who took inflation and the USD:MXN exchange rate into account. The USD:MXN exchange rate was 17 at the end of August compared to 18.66 a year earlier.

More than 32 million international tourists came to Mexico between January and August

INEGI data shows that 32.68 million international tourists came to Mexico in the first eight months of 2026, a year-over-year increase of 3.9%.

International traveler numbers rose 6.3% annually in the same period to reach 67.69 million.

In a statement, Tourism Minister Josefina Rodríguez said that data from the first eight months of the year indicates that “Mexico could end 2026 with a record in international tourist arrivals.”

“Mexico is in vogue and we’re continuing to work so that more people visit us, get to know our cultural and natural wealth and contribute to the well-being of communities,” she said.

Total expenditure by international travelers in Mexico was $24.15 billion between January and August, an increase of 0.9% compared to the same period of last year.

Mexico is one of the world’s 10 most visited countries, ranking sixth or seventh in recent years. One of the goals of the federal government’s Plan Mexico economic initiative is to make Mexico one of the world’s top five tourism destinations by 2030.

With reports from El Economista, La Jornada and Reporte Indigo

World.title: Morocco Security and Crime Explained 2026
World.content:
MOROCCO · SECURITY

Key Facts — The basics Morocco, a US free trade partner and 2030 World Cup co-host, is rated Level 2, exercise increased caution, by Washington because of terrorism, while police data show stable overall crime and falling violent crime in 2025.

— Why it matters Security underpins a tourism industry that counted 19.8 million arrivals in 2025, the 2030 World Cup shared with Spain and Portugal, and a Western Sahara mission whose UN mandate ends on Saturday, 31 October 2026.

— The numbers Police handled 779,008 criminal cases in 2025, violent crime fell 10% to 43,869 cases, police say they solved 95% of apparent crimes, and 170.8 tonnes of cannabis resin were seized.

— Who is who Abdellatif Hammouchi leads both the DGSN national police and the DGST intelligence service, Abdelouafi Laftit, last named interior minister in July 2026, belongs to the outgoing government, General Mohammed Berrid is Inspector General of the armed forces, and King Mohammed VI is their Supreme Chief.

— What to watch The UN Security Council is due to decide the future of its Western Sahara mission before Saturday, 31 October 2026, and Head of Government Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri is still forming her cabinet.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 96% chance that Aziz Akhannouch is out as Morocco’s prime minister by 31 December 2026 (16 October, 11:02 a.m. ET).

— What it means for you US visitors face a Level 2 advisory that names terrorism, not any city, as the risk, plus pickpockets, taxi harassment and scams in tourist areas, so they should enrol in STEP, avoid protests and carry evacuation insurance.

Official figures show stable crime and falling violent crime in Morocco, but terrorism plots, protests and a disputed border shape the risk. This guide maps the institutions, the numbers and the places that matter as of October 2026.

Morocco security in October 2026 rests on a large police and intelligence apparatus, a royal army and a stable statistical record. Washington rates the kingdom Level 2, exercise increased caution, because of terrorism.

For a US visitor or investor, the city, the season and the news cycle matter more than the national rating. This guide draws on police statistics, US and UK government advice, UN texts and Moroccan official statements.

Daily coverage is in the Rio Times Morocco section, with background in the Morocco politics guide and the Morocco geopolitics explainer. Newcomers can read the Marrakech city guide and the Casablanca city guide before they travel.

How Morocco Security Is Organised

The DGSN, short for the General Directorate of National Security, is Morocco’s national police. Its director general, Abdellatif Hammouchi, also heads the DGST, the domestic intelligence service.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Sudan's army chief sends Trump a message on peace” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

On Wednesday, 14 October 2026, Hammouchi signed an agreement with the National Museums Foundation, covering police escorts for archaeological items. Le360 named him as director general of national security and territorial surveillance.

The BCIJ, the Central Bureau of Judicial Investigations, is the judicial police arm of the DGST and announces terrorism arrests. The Gendarmerie Royale is a military police force, and the UK lists 177 as its emergency number.

The Royal Armed Forces answer to King Mohammed VI, who is their Supreme Chief and Chief of General Staff. General Mohammed Berrid is Inspector General and commands the Southern Zone, Hespress said on Tuesday, 6 October 2026.

Abdelouafi Laftit, interior minister in the outgoing government, was last named in that post by Hespress on Thursday, 9 July 2026. The ministry published the final results of the 23 September 2026 legislative elections on Friday, 25 September 2026.

King Mohammed VI named Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri Head of Government on Tuesday, 29 September 2026. She coordinates the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), the largest party in the new House of Representatives with 97 of 395 seats.

On Monday, 12 October 2026, the PAM, Istiqlal, USFP and PPS announced a majority under El Mansouri, without the RNI. Istiqlal is conservative, the USFP socialist, the PPS left-wing, and the RNI (National Rally of Independents) led the outgoing government.

A Royal Office statement on Wednesday, 14 October 2026 shows she is still forming her cabinet. Until it is named, who will hold the interior portfolio remains unknown.

What Official Crime Figures Show

The DGSN handled 779,008 criminal cases in 2025, a stable total, in an annual report released on Wednesday, 17 December 2025. Violent crime fell 10% to 43,869 cases, about 6% of the total.

Robbery under threat fell 24%, robbery with violence fell 6%, and burglary with aggravating circumstances fell about 12%. Police arrested 25,421 people in violent crime cases, including 10,036 who were wanted under national warrants.

The DGSN put its clearance rate for apparent crimes at 95%, its own measure of cases solved. No independent victimisation survey was found for this guide.

Drug cases numbered 106,117 and led to 134,126 arrests, including 378 foreigners. Seizures included 170.8 tonnes of cannabis resin, 1.7 tonnes of cocaine and about 1.6 million psychotropic tablets.

Police arrested 1,737 people in operations against organised criminal networks. Cases involving the synthetic drug known as boufa fell 33%, with 5.6 kg seized.

The public summary gives national totals only, with no murder count and no breakdown by city. Four Moroccan outlets published the same headline figures, but the full DGSN report could not be opened.

Tourist Areas, Petty Crime and Scams

The US State Department, on a page updated 4 June 2025, calls crime a serious concern in major cities and tourist areas. It names pickpocketing, purse-snatching and harassment of women, and says knife attacks have occurred and romance scams are common.

UK advice, updated on 19 August 2026, says petty crime is common in medinas and on beaches. It lists drive-by motorcycle theft of visible jewellery and handbags and warns that fake official guides often harass tourists.

The US advises petit taxis at night and says rideshare riders have reported harassment and violence by taxi drivers. The UK says unlicensed ride-share cars may be uninsured, so passengers should agree a fare or check the meter.

The Ministry of Tourism announced 19.8 million arrivals in 2025 and receipts of 124 billion dirhams (about US$12.6 billion) through November. Conversions in this guide use 9.83 dirhams per US$ on 15 October 2026.

Terrorism Threat and the Cells Dismantled

Washington last issued its Level 2 advisory on Monday, 21 April 2025, and names terrorism as the reason. It says attackers may strike with little or no warning at tourist locations, transport hubs, markets, shopping malls and local government facilities.

UK advice says terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Morocco, including in places visited by foreign nationals. Outside Western Sahara, neither the US nor the UK names a Moroccan city as a no-go area.

BCIJ announcements in 2025 and 2026 include three cases that show the pattern. Each announcement comes from the BCIJ alone, and suspects are presumed innocent until a court rules.

Wednesday, 2 July 2025: four suspects aged 20 to 27 were held in a cell active between Tétouan and Chefchaouen that pledged allegiance to Islamic State and ran field tests aimed at making homemade devices.

Wednesday, 25 March 2026: two suspects were arrested in Tangier and a suspected leader in Majorca, in a joint operation with Spanish police.

Monday, 6 July 2026: ten people were held in seven cities, including Agadir, Casablanca and Safi, in a cell with alleged Islamic State links in the Sahel.

The BCIJ said the July 2026 cell was at an advanced stage, with a modified off-road vehicle found near Agadir. In its March 2026 statement, the BCIJ said Morocco and Spain have dismantled more than 30 cells together since 2014.

The 2025 GenZ212 Protests and Policing

GenZ212, a leaderless youth movement organised mainly on Discord, began street protests on Saturday, 27 September 2025. It demanded reforms in education, health, jobs and the fight against corruption.

On Wednesday, 1 October 2025, more than 200 people attacked a Royal Gendarmerie post at Lqliaa near Agadir, the local prosecutor said. Gendarmes fired warning shots, then live rounds, the prosecutor said; three people died, eight gendarmes were injured and an investigation began.

On Thursday, 2 October 2025, the Interior Ministry said 354 people were injured nationwide the night before, 326 of them security personnel. It said about 70% of those involved were minors and that gendarmes at Lqliaa acted in self-defence.

On Tuesday, 28 October 2025, a Public Prosecution official said 2,480 people had been referred to prosecutors, including 1,473 held in custody. More than 3,300 others were released after identity checks, and sentences ranged from one to 15 years.

In June 2026 a Casablanca court sentenced six minors to six months each for blocking an urban highway during the protests. Morocco World News said 18 adults in the same case received sentences of up to ten months the previous week.

The Ceuta Border Surge of July 2026

On Thursday, 30 July 2026, thousands of Moroccans and foreigners, including children, tried to enter Spain’s Ceuta enclave near Fnideq. Morocco’s National Human Rights Council (CNDH) found attempts rose from June, with a peak on 30 and 31 July 2026.

On Sunday, 2 August 2026, Morocco’s Interior Ministry put the crowd at about 40,000 and recorded 11 deaths, mostly drownings. It said the surge was not spontaneous and blamed misinformation, trafficking networks and a misreading of a Spanish court ruling.

Spanish sources estimated about 50,000 entries, an unofficial figure, and Spain’s Government Delegation in Ceuta counted 72 deaths. Ceuta’s regional government announced more than 80 deaths.

By 6 August 2026 the CNDH reported, from Moroccan sources, 14 deaths on the Moroccan side and 136 injured civilians. It said 87 security personnel were treated, and 100 people were arrested, including 11 minors; 69 of those arrested face prosecution.

The ministry and the CNDH both blame online rumours that wrongly said a Spanish court ruling of 8 July 2026 barred returns. Five main online groups were closed on 30 July 2026, and Moroccan authorities restricted travel toward the north, the CNDH said.

Western Sahara and the Algerian Border

Western Sahara is a disputed territory, and the Berm is a militarised boundary running through it. Morocco controls the west, and the Polisario Front, which seeks an independent Sahrawi state, holds land to the east.

UN Security Council Resolution 2797, adopted in October 2025, took Morocco’s autonomy proposal as the basis for talks. The vote was 11 to none with three abstentions, and the MINURSO mission was extended to 31 October 2026.

China, Pakistan and Russia abstained, while Algeria did not take part in the vote. Morocco World News said the Council would hold closed consultations on Thursday, 8 October 2026, with a renewal vote expected later.

UK advice, last updated on 29 June 2026, advises against all travel within 40 km north and west of the Berm. It also advises against travel to areas south and east of the Berm, and the US warns of unexploded mines.

The land and sea borders with Algeria are closed and closely patrolled, the UK says, and crossing without authorisation is illegal. UK advice tells boat and jet-ski users to stay in Moroccan waters, as those entering Algerian waters are likely to be intercepted.

The Algeria Morocco rivalry explainer covers the dispute behind the closed border. The Morocco neighbours guide covers wider regional ties.

AFCON 2025 and the 2030 World Cup Security Test

Morocco hosted the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) from Sunday, 21 December 2025 to Sunday, 18 January 2026, in six cities. Nine judicial offices operated inside stadiums in Rabat, Casablanca, Marrakech, Agadir, Fes and Tangier.

A joint statement by the Justice Ministry, prosecutors and the DGSN counted 529 security interventions during the tournament. Of the 529, 307 were identity checks; 202 people faced stadium judicial offices, and 396 were held over suspected illegal ticket resale.

Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time on Sunday, 18 January 2026, at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat. Senegal’s players briefly left the pitch to protest a late Morocco penalty, and some fans tried to enter it.

On Tuesday, 17 March 2026, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) ruled that Senegal lost by forfeit, awarding Morocco a 3-0 win. Senegal’s federation appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), asking for the decision to be annulled.

CAS set a hearing for Thursday, 8 October 2026. No ruling was public by 16 October 2026, so the dispute over the title remains open.

Courts sentenced 18 Senegalese fans to between three months and one year in prison in February 2026. King Mohammed VI pardoned the convicted fans on Saturday, 23 May 2026, on humanitarian grounds ahead of Eid al-Adha.

FIFA appointed Morocco, Portugal and Spain as 2030 World Cup hosts at its congress on Wednesday, 11 December 2024. The African Police Cooperation Centre in Salé opened on Thursday, 18 December 2025, with liaison officers from 23 competing countries, Hespress said.

Interpol held its 93rd General Assembly in Marrakech from 24 to 27 November 2025, with more than 800 delegates from 179 countries. The police chiefs of Morocco, Spain and Germany discussed 2030 World Cup security in Madrid on Wednesday, 29 January 2025.

Hotspots and Safer Areas by City

Outside Western Sahara, neither advisory names a city as a no-go area, so risk depends on place and activity. The examples below come from official statements, police announcements and advisory text.

Marrakech: crowded medinas, souks and Jemaa el-Fnaa square are where UK advice flags bag-snatching and fake guides; Interpol held its 2025 assembly in the city.

Casablanca: Morocco’s largest city hosts the US Consulate General, which handles all US citizen services, and was one of seven cities in the July 2026 BCIJ arrests.

Tangier: a northern port city where two suspects were arrested in March 2026; the CNDH said people were told to reach Tangier before heading for Ceuta in July 2026.

Fes: the old medina draws the same warnings about fake guides and bag-snatching, and the city hosted AFCON matches with a stadium judicial office.

The north and the Rif: Tétouan and Chefchaouen saw a cell arrest in July 2025, while Fnideq was the centre of the July 2026 crossing attempts.

Agadir and the south: three people died at Lqliaa near Agadir on 1 October 2025, and the July 2026 BCIJ arrests included Agadir, Taroudant and Safi.

Visitors can plan with the What to Do in Marrakech in October 2026 guide, which lists events in the city. The Rabat city guide covers the capital, where the AFCON final took place.

Practical Safety Advice and Emergency Numbers

Police can be reached on 19 from a landline or 190 from a mobile, and the Gendarmerie Royale on 177. The US page says to dial 15 for emergency services, and the UK page gives 150 for ambulance and fire.

The US Consulate General in Casablanca handles US citizen services on +212-5226-42000, with an after-hours emergency line at +212-537-63-72-00. The US Embassy in Rabat does not offer consular services.

Medical care is adequate mainly in Rabat and Casablanca, the US says, and care outside major cities falls far below US standards. It strongly recommends insurance that covers medical evacuation.

The US and UK advisories converge on a short list of habits. These are the main ones for a first visit:

Use petit taxis at night, avoid unlicensed ride-share cars, and agree a fare or insist on the meter.

Keep bags and phones out of sight in medinas and on beaches, and avoid displaying jewellery.

Check for an official badge before hiring a guide in a medina, and refuse unsolicited offers.

Avoid protests, crowds and football stadiums on match days.

Be wary of online romances and marriage proposals, which both governments link to fraud.

Avoid photographing palaces, government buildings or diplomatic missions, which can cause problems.

Buy travel insurance with medical evacuation and enrol in the State Department’s STEP programme.

What It Means for US Readers

For travellers, Morocco is a Level 2 destination whose main official concerns are terrorism, petty crime and scams, not closed cities. The practical risks are pickpockets, fake guides and taxi disputes, so the habits above matter more than any single warning.

For investors, security shapes tourism, which brought 19.8 million arrivals in 2025, and the 2030 World Cup build-out. The US-Morocco free trade agreement has been in force since 1 January 2006, so stability in Rabat matters to US firms.

For policy readers, counter-terrorism cooperation with Spain and the Sahel link in the July 2026 BCIJ case are the points to follow. The Western Sahara vote at the UN before 31 October 2026 will set the frame for border risk.

Readers who want the wider picture can turn to the Morocco power structure explainer and the Morocco foreign players guide. The Morocco history explainer gives background, and the expat safety guide focuses on road risks.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket’s market “Aziz Akhannouch out as Morocco Prime Minister by December 31, 2026?” shows Yes at 96%. That price was read on 16 October, 11:02 a.m. ET, and about US$173,000 has traded in total.

The market pays Yes if Akhannouch ceases to be prime minister even briefly before the deadline; an announced removal counts at once. Its rules name official information from Akhannouch and Morocco’s government as the resolution source, with credible reporting as a fallback.

Akhannouch led the outgoing government, and El Mansouri, named Head of Government on 29 September 2026, is still forming her cabinet. The market was still open on 16 October 2026, and this guide takes no view on how it will resolve.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The full DGSN report for 2025 could not be opened, so crime figures rest on four Moroccan outlets that agree. The public summary has no murder count and no breakdown by city.

No 2026 source confirmed the current commander of the Gendarmerie Royale, so this guide does not name him. Police and gendarmerie headcounts, and the number of officers planned for the 2030 World Cup, have not been published.

Whether Laftit keeps the Interior Ministry depends on the cabinet, which the Royal Office has not yet announced. The Ceuta death toll remains disputed, and no official source confirms analysts’ claims that border controls were relaxed.

No findings have been published from the Lqliaa investigation, and no official total exists for people still jailed after the GenZ212 trials. The MINURSO renewal vote and its terms had not been announced when this guide was written.

The CAS ruling on the AFCON 2025 final had not been published by 16 October 2026. Its timing and outcome are not known.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Morocco safe for American tourists?

The US rates Morocco Level 2, exercise increased caution, because of terrorism, and its advisory lists no do-not-travel areas. Petty crime and scams in medinas and tourist areas are the most common problems.

Is there a terrorism threat in Morocco?

Yes, the US and UK both say attacks are possible, and the BCIJ announced a ten-person cell arrest on 6 July 2026. Suspects are presumed innocent until a court rules, and the BCIJ is the only source for these announcements.

What are the emergency numbers in Morocco?

Dial 19 from a landline or 190 from a mobile for police, and 177 for the Gendarmerie Royale. The US page says to dial 15 for emergency services, while the UK page lists 150 for ambulance and fire.

Is crime in Morocco rising or falling?

Police say violent crime fell 10% in 2025 to 43,869 cases, within a stable total of 779,008 cases. These are police figures, and no independent survey was found.

Is it safe to travel to Western Sahara?

The UK advises against all travel south and east of the Berm, and within 40 km north and west of it. The US warns of unexploded mines and border tensions.

Who runs security policy in Morocco?

The King commands the armed forces, and Abdellatif Hammouchi leads both the DGSN police and the DGST intelligence service. Abdelouafi Laftit, last named interior minister in July 2026, belongs to the outgoing government; no cabinet was named by 16 October 2026.

World.title: Tanzania Geopolitics Explained 2026
World.content:
TANZANIA · GEOPOLITICS

Key Facts — The basics As of October 2026, Tanzania, the Indian Ocean gateway for Zambia and its neighbours, is courting China, Russia, India, the Gulf and Turkey while Washington reviews ties and Brussels presses for reforms after the October 2025 election.

— Why it matters Ports, a Chinese-backed railway, uranium, graphite, rare earths and a US$42 billion gas project make Tanzania a prize for every major power, and its choices shape access to inland Africa’s trade routes.

— The numbers India trade reached US$8.6 billion in 2024-25, DP World pledged more than US$250 million for Dar es Salaam berths, and a presidential commission counted 518 deaths in the October 2025 election violence.

— Who is who President Samia Suluhu Hassan leads the ruling CCM party, Vice President Deogratius Ndejembi took office on 29 August 2026, and Mahmoud Thabit Kombo is Foreign Minister in a cabinet under Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba.

— What to watch Watch the 31 December 2026 expiry of the US trade preference law AGOA, any signing of the LNG deal, the start of Rosatom’s main uranium plant works due in the fourth quarter of 2026, and the US Senate bill.

— What it means for you Tanzanians have faced largely closed US visas since 1 January 2026, a Senate bill would add sanctions and aid limits, and US investors in gas and minerals now compete with Chinese, Russian and Gulf offers.

Tanzania has ports, railways, uranium and gas on the Indian Ocean that every major power wants. This guide sets out what each power wants from Dar es Salaam, as of October 2026.

Tanzania geopolitics in October 2026 is a contest over ports, railways, minerals and gas on East Africa’s Indian Ocean coast. Washington is reviewing ties and Europe is pressing for reforms after the election, while China, Russia, India and the Gulf deepen theirs.

This explainer draws on government texts, ministry briefs, company statements and regional outlets, and it names the source of every casualty figure. For a US reader, the stakes are visa access, minerals supply chains and a corridor that links Zambia to the sea.

Daily coverage is in the Rio Times Tanzania section, with background in the Tanzania explainer and the Tanzania neighbours guide. Readers can also follow the Who Backs Whom in Africa guide for the wider contest.

Tanzania Geopolitics: Who Decides and What Each Power Wants

Samia Suluhu Hassan was sworn in for her first elected term as president on Monday, 3 November 2025, in Dodoma. She chairs the Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party that has governed Tanzania for decades.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Sudan's army chief sends Trump a message on peace” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Deogratius Ndejembi became Vice President on Saturday, 29 August 2026, after Emmanuel Nchimbi announced his resignation. Mwigulu Nchemba is Prime Minister and Mahmoud Thabit Kombo is Foreign Minister, the CIA directory of 5 October 2026 shows.

Hussein Ali Mwinyi is President of Zanzibar, the island government within the union. Zanzibar hosted an India-Tanzania defence committee meeting in February 2026, so the islands matter in foreign policy too.

Each power wants something different from Tanzania, and the pattern is clearest in a short list. The sections below give the dates, figures and sources behind each line.

United States: democratic reforms, easier access for US investors and a check on Chinese influence, as its review and a Senate bill show.

democratic reforms, easier access for US investors and a check on Chinese influence, as its review and a Senate bill show. China: railways, ports, minerals and political backing, which Beijing renewed in January 2026.

railways, ports, minerals and political backing, which Beijing renewed in January 2026. Russia: uranium, nuclear technology sales and military ties through Rosatom and defence agreements.

uranium, nuclear technology sales and military ties through Rosatom and defence agreements. European Union: human-rights conditions on direct support, while European export credit still funds the railway.

human-rights conditions on direct support, while European export credit still funds the railway. Gulf states: port operations, trade and mining, led by Dubai’s DP World and the United Arab Emirates.

port operations, trade and mining, led by Dubai’s DP World and the United Arab Emirates. Turkey: construction contracts and machinery exports, led by the builder Yapi Merkezi.

construction contracts and machinery exports, led by the builder Yapi Merkezi. India: trade, water credit, naval access and a say in Indian Ocean security.

The 2025 Election and the Western Reaction

Tanzania voted on Wednesday, 29 October 2025, and the electoral commission declared Samia the winner with about 98% of the vote. On Monday, 3 November 2025, the Southern African Development Community (SADC) observer mission said the vote fell short of the bloc’s standards.

It cited intimidation, internet shutdowns and the exclusion of opposition candidates, including the treason detention of opposition leader Tundu Lissu. It called its conclusion tentative and promised a final report within 30 days.

A presidential commission led by retired Chief Justice Mohamed Chande Othman gave its report to Samia on Thursday, 23 April 2026. It counted 518 deaths, including 21 children, and 2,390 people treated for injuries, and said the toll might not be final.

The commission did not name those responsible and urged a new constitution by 2028. On 23 April 2026 Samia said the commission found the violence planned and coordinated, and she defended the security forces.

On Thursday, 4 December 2025, UN human rights experts estimated at least 700 people killed and over 1,700 detained. Opposition party Chadema called the report a cover-up, and Human Rights Watch called it a missed opportunity on 5 May 2026.

The European Parliament adopted a resolution on Tanzania on Thursday, 27 November 2025, by 539 votes to 0, with 27 abstentions. It demanded the release of Lissu, an independent inquiry, a halt to direct EU support to Tanzanian authorities and possible Council sanctions.

Tanzania’s government said on 28 November 2025 that it was monitoring the matter and would issue a statement. On 5 December 2025 a group of Western missions in Tanzania urged an independent inquiry into the deaths.

The United States: Review, Visa Limits and a Senate Bill

The US State Department announced a review of the relationship on Thursday, 4 December 2025. The review includes Tanzania’s democratic trajectory, political repression and the impact of recent unrest on US businesses and regional stability.

On Tuesday, 16 December 2025, a proclamation suspended immigrant, tourist, business, student and exchange visas for Tanzanians from 1 January 2026. Existing visas stay valid, and the text cites visa overstay rates of 8.30% and 13.97%.

On Thursday, 21 May 2026, Republican Ted Cruz and Democrat Jeanne Shaheen introduced a Senate bill to reassess ties with Tanzania. It would allow visa bans and asset blocks, pause some US support and order a review of China’s activity in Tanzania.

The bill would also bar Millennium Challenge Corporation aid until Tanzania shows renewed commitment to democratic governance. Nominee for ambassador William Trachman cleared the Senate Foreign Relations Committee by 12 votes to 10 on Thursday, 4 June 2026.

The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) now runs to 31 December 2026, after senators trimmed a three-year renewal. BusinessDay reported that Tanzania remained among eligible countries in the US Trade Representative’s December 2025 update.

China: TAZARA Railway, Zero Tariffs and Rare Earths

China built the TAZARA railway between 1970 and 1976, linking Dar es Salaam port to New Kapiri Mposhi in Zambia. The railway marks 50 years of commercial operation in 2026.

On Monday, 29 September 2025, TAZARA signed a concession agreement with China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC), a Chinese railway contractor. TAZARA says phase one rebuilds track, bridges and signalling, and phase two adds new locomotives and wagons.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

In March 2025 The Citizen reported a proposed 30-year deal worth US$1.4 billion. That split US$1 billion for track and US$400 million for 32 locomotives and 762 wagons, but TAZARA’s release gives no figure.

TAZARA said on Tuesday, 13 October 2026 that its board approved a plan for operational recovery. The earlier Rio Times report on the Lobito corridor and TAZARA explains the Western rival route through Angola.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi visited Dar es Salaam on 9 and 10 January 2026 and issued a joint communique with Kombo. Beijing congratulated Tanzania on its October 2025 elections and backed its efforts to protect constitutional order, the text says.

China said African states with diplomatic ties keep zero-tariff access to its market, and Tanzania aims to double exports by 2030. Tanzania also reaffirmed the one-China principle in the same text.

Chinese capital also reaches Tanzania’s rare earths. Shenghe Resources, a Chinese group, agreed to acquire all of Peak Rare Earths, developer of the Ngualla project.

Tanzania’s Fair Competition Commission and Mining Commission consented to the deal by 18 September 2025, Peak told investors. Their approval satisfied the Tanzanian regulatory condition for the takeover scheme.

Russia: Rosatom, Uranium and Military Ties

Samia met Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Wednesday, 3 June 2026, the first such visit by a Tanzanian president since 1969. She addressed the St Petersburg International Economic Forum on Friday, 5 June.

The talks reviewed a 2016 military cooperation agreement and a military-technical agreement ratified in 2018. More than 300 Tanzanian officers train in Russian military academies, IPP Media reported.

Russian investment includes the Mkuju River uranium project in Ruvuma, run by Mantra Tanzania, a unit of state nuclear group Rosatom. In June 2026 Rosatom put the Nyota deposit at 58,500 tonnes of uranium and output at up to 3,000 tonnes yearly.

It puts the investment at about US$1 billion, with main-plant construction due in the fourth quarter of 2026 and commissioning in 2029. Its director general, Alexey Likhachev, also raised floating and small modular nuclear plants for the 2030s.

Russia supplies Tanzania with fertilisers, petroleum products, machinery, steel and wheat, and buys tea, tobacco and cashew nuts, IPP Media reported. Samia invited Russian firms to build fertiliser plants in Tanzania during the June 2026 visit.

Ports and Rails: The Gulf, India, Turkey and Europe

On Sunday, 22 October 2023, Tanzania gave Dubai’s DP World a 30-year concession for berths 4 to 7 at Dar es Salaam. DP World pledged more than US$250 million, and Parliament had endorsed the underlying agreement in June 2023, Business Recorder reported.

Opponents, including the Catholic Church, lawyers and opposition politicians, argued the terms favoured DP World, Business Recorder reported. The contract reviews DP World’s performance every five years.

India’s Adani Ports said in May 2024 that it signed a 30-year concession for Container Terminal 2 at Dar es Salaam. That terminal handled about 820,000 container units in 2023, roughly 83% of Tanzania’s container volume, Baird Maritime reported.

Bagamoyo is a planned port about 75 km north of Dar es Salaam that stalled after a 2013 framework deal. The developers are China Merchants Holdings International and Oman’s State General Reserve Fund.

In November 2025 the government said construction would start in December. Whether works have begun could not be confirmed.

European money still builds Tanzania’s standard gauge railway (SGR). On Tuesday, 28 April 2026, Tanzania signed US$1.277 billion for two more phases, backed by Swedish, Polish and Italian export credit agencies.

Standard Chartered backed the financing, The EastAfrican reported. The Rio Times report on SGR electric train revenue tracks how the finished sections are performing.

Turkey’s trade with Tanzania was about US$284 million in 2024, including US$217 million of Turkish exports, Turkey’s foreign ministry says. Turkey’s foreign ministry puts Turkish business investment in Tanzania at about US$40 million, without giving a date.

Samia visited Turkey from 18 to 21 April 2024, and six agreements covered education, investment, the diaspora and archives. Turkey’s visible footprint is the railway that Yapi Merkezi is building.

India’s foreign ministry puts bilateral trade at US$8.6 billion in 2024-25, making India Tanzania’s second-largest trading partner. Indian investment totals US$4.08 billion in the same April 2026 brief, according to the Tanzania Investment Centre.

India committed over US$1.1 billion in water credit lines by April 2026, including US$500 million signed on 10 May 2018. Samia’s visit to India from 8 to 11 October 2023 raised ties to a strategic partnership.

An Indian military training team has served at the Arusha staff college since December 2017. The joint defence committee met in Zanzibar from 2 to 4 February 2026.

The first Africa India Key Maritime Engagement was held in Dar es Salaam in April 2025. The warship INS Trikand visited Dar es Salaam from 3 to 6 April 2026, under India’s MAHASAGAR maritime vision.

Minerals, Gas and the Indian Ocean Corridor

Equinor and Shell lead a planned US$42 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) export project at Likong’o in Lindi region. ExxonMobil, Pavilion Energy, Medco Energi and state oil company TPDC are partners, Enerdata reported in January 2026.

In January 2026 Tanzania said it had closed commercial talks and was finalising legal issues, aiming to sign by June 2026. No signing is confirmed as of October 2026, and a final investment decision is not confirmed.

The East African Crude Oil Pipeline runs 1,443 km from Uganda’s oil fields to Chongoleani near Tanga on the Indian Ocean. It was 82% complete in April 2026, and its shareholders include TotalEnergies, Uganda’s UNOC, Tanzania’s TPDC and China’s CNOOC.

Black Rock Mining holds 84% of the Mahenge graphite project, and the Tanzanian government holds a free 16% interest. South Korea’s POSCO holds offtake for almost 40% of first-module output, and initial spending is US$231 million, TanzaniaInvest reported in April 2026.

Uranium, graphite, rare earths and gas each draw a different power. The Rio Times guide to Africa’s critical minerals places Tanzania in the wider scramble.

BRICS, the UN and the Regional Blocs

Tanzania is neither a BRICS member nor a partner country on the lists published as of September 2026. Four powers courted by Tanzania, China, Russia, India and the United Arab Emirates, are full members of the bloc.

On Wednesday, 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly voted 141 to 5, with 35 abstentions, on Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The Citizen reported that Tanzania abstained, as it did in April 2022 on suspending Russia from the Human Rights Council.

Tanzania belongs to both the East African Community (EAC) and SADC, and its geography links the two blocs. The Citizen reported on 18 August 2025 that Samia handed over leadership of the SADC security organ.

A joint EAC and SADC summit held in Tanzania on Saturday, 8 February 2025 called for an immediate ceasefire in eastern Congo. Defence chiefs of both blocs then met in Dar es Salaam, allAfrica reported.

What It Means for US Readers

For Tanzanian students, visitors and families, US visas have been largely closed since 1 January 2026, with reviews every 180 days. For US investors, the LNG signature, Mahenge financing and Rosatom’s plant are the signals to watch.

For policy readers, a Senate bill would tie aid and trade to reforms and order a review of Chinese activity. AGOA benefits lapse on 31 December 2026 unless Congress acts again.

For the economy behind these bids, see the Tanzania GDP rebasing report and the World Bank projects report. Visitors to the islands can use the Zanzibar city guide.

What Is Not Known

No official figure reconciles the commission’s 518 deaths with the 700 or more UN experts estimated, and higher figures are unverified. Lissu’s legal status in October 2026, the bill’s progress and whether the EU halted any direct support could not be confirmed.

The final TAZARA concession value, any works at Bagamoyo and any LNG signing since the June 2026 target could not be confirmed. Later UN votes, a final Senate vote on Trachman and any change to the US visa list were also not confirmed.

No foreign military base in Tanzania appears in the government texts reviewed, only training teams, defence agreements and port calls. Tanzania’s external debt by creditor, including any Chinese loans, was not reviewed for this guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Tanzania aligned with China or Russia?

Tanzania is not a formal ally of either. It has a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership with China, a military cooperation agreement with Russia and a strategic partnership with India.

What is the TAZARA railway?

TAZARA links Dar es Salaam to New Kapiri Mposhi in Zambia and was built with Chinese help between 1970 and 1976. A concession signed on 29 September 2025 with CCECC started its revival.

Did the United States cut ties with Tanzania after the 2025 election?

No, it announced a review on 4 December 2025 and has restricted most visas for Tanzanians since 1 January 2026. A Senate bill introduced on 21 May 2026 would go further.

Is Tanzania in BRICS?

No, Tanzania is not on the published lists of BRICS members or partner countries as of September 2026. China, Russia, India and the United Arab Emirates, however, are members.

How many people died in the 2025 election violence?

A presidential commission counted 518 deaths, and UN human rights experts estimated at least 700. Neither figure is independently verified, and the commission said its toll might not be final.

Who leads Tanzania in October 2026?

Samia Suluhu Hassan is president and Deogratius Ndejembi has been vice president since 29 August 2026. Mwigulu Nchemba is prime minister and Mahmoud Thabit Kombo is foreign minister.

World.title: Kenya Media Landscape Explained
World.content:
KENYA · MEDIA

Key Facts — The basics As of October 2026, Kenya has more than 100 radio stations, nearly 50 TV channels and four daily newspapers, led by Nation Media Group, Royal Media Services and the state broadcaster KBC.

— Why it matters Kenya votes in a general election in August 2027, and the owners, regulators and courts that shape the news will decide how freely voters, investors and Washington can follow the race.

— The numbers Kenya ranks 106th of 180 countries in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index, had 88.0 million mobile SIM subscriptions in June 2026, and Nation Media Group earned about US$46.6 million in 2025 revenue.

— Who is who Nation Media Group, whose 54.08% owner agreed in March 2026 to sell to Tanzanian businessman Rostam Azizi, owns Daily Nation and NTV, Royal Media Services runs Citizen TV, the Communications Authority licenses broadcasters, and the Media Council accredits journalists.

— What to watch Watch the August 2027 campaign, the police inquiry into the September 2026 abduction of a Standard Group editor, and any appeal against court rulings that quashed a live-coverage ban and website-blocking powers.

— What it means for you US readers should compare outlets across ownership camps, treat press freedom as a gauge of election risk, and remember that Meta, TikTok and Alphabet platforms carry much of Kenya’s online news.

Kenya media is a crowded market where a few owners, a government-linked regulator and the courts shape what people read and watch. This guide explains who owns what, how free the press is and how phones and social platforms carry the news.

Kenya media combines a few large private groups, a state broadcaster and a fast-growing online audience that depends on mobile phones. Reporters Without Borders (RSF) ranks Kenya 106th of 180 countries in its 2026 World Press Freedom Index, up from 117th in 2025.

That matters in the United States because Kenya votes in a general election in August 2027. Owners, regulators and courts shape how the race is covered, and Meta, Alphabet and TikTok platforms carry much of the online news.

Kenya Media at a Glance

RSF’s 2026 profile counts more than 100 radio stations and nearly 50 TV channels in Kenya, but only four daily newspapers. It names the Daily Nation as the most-read paper and Nation Media Group as the dominant Kenyan press group.

The Communications Authority of Kenya (CA), the sector regulator, had assigned 978 FM frequencies by 30 June 2026. Its report counts 1.55 million active paid television subscriptions on that date, up 4.9% in a year.

Press freedom is enshrined in the 2010 Constitution, and Article 34 guarantees media freedom. Access to public information is still very difficult despite a law on the subject, RSF says.

Ethnicity is often linked to political loyalties and plays a big role in Kenyan journalism, RSF says. Stories on national security, terrorism, religion and trafficking are especially sensitive.

Newspapers and Their Owners

Nation Media Group (NMG) publishes the Daily Nation, the Kiswahili daily Taifa Leo, Business Daily and The EastAfrican. NMG says it is the largest independent media house in East and Central Africa, with 30 media brands in four countries.

Standard Group PLC publishes The Standard and the weekly The Nairobian, and runs the Standard Digital news site, its website says. The group is listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) under the symbol SGL.

The Star is part of Radio Africa Group, whose website lists it as a brand. Its shareholders are not published in any filing found.

RSF says much of Kenya’s media is owned by political leaders or people close to the government. After President William Ruto’s 2022 election, it says, heads of major press groups and outlets were fired under political pressure.

Print is shrinking and audited circulation figures are not published in one public source. NMG’s 2025 results blame lower print revenue for a 3.1% fall in group revenue to KES 6.04 billion (about US$46.6 million).

Television and Radio Broadcasters

The Kenya Broadcasting Corporation (KBC) is a state corporation set up by an Act of Parliament, its website says. Its public mandate covers English, Kiswahili and other languages, with radio services such as Radio Taifa, an English Service and regional stations.
