World.title: Wet weekend ahead as excessive rainfall expected
World.content:
Wet weekend ahead as excessive rainfall expected

By Zoila Palma: The National Meteorological Service of Belize is warning of a wet weekend ahead, with excessive rainfall of 2 to 4 inches per day or more possible across the country over the next couple of days.

The Met Service says a moist and unstable airmass continues to prevail over Belize, creating conditions for showers, thunderstorms and periods of rain.

For today, mostly cloudy to overcast skies are expected, with showers, thunderstorms and periods of rain across the country.

The unsettled weather is expected to continue on Saturday, with mostly cloudy skies and showers, a few thunderstorms and periods of rain over most areas.

There is also a small craft caution, warning that winds may become gusty during heavy showers or thunderstorms, causing locally rough seas.

Operators of small crafts are advised to exercise caution.

World.title: Could YOU be Belize’s next millionaire?
World.content:
Could YOU be Belize’s next millionaire?

By Zoila Palma: The countdown is on, and your million-dollar moment could be closer than you think!

The Belize Government Lotteries has announced the return of its million dallaz Jackpot, with tickets set to go on sale on November 2, 2026.

Tickets will cost $5 each and will be available through the FiWeBoledo mobile app, the website fiweboledo.bz and sub-agents countrywide.

Try yuh luck!

World.title: Central Bank warns of phone call scam!
World.content:
Central Bank warns of phone call scam!

By Zoila Palma: The Central Bank of Belize is warning the public about fraudulent phone calls from individuals falsely claiming to represent the institution.

In an advisory issued on October 14, 2026, the Central Bank said it has received multiple reports of scammers using Google Meet to impersonate its representatives and request personal or banking information.

The Central Bank stressed that these calls are fraudulent and urged the public not to share passwords, PINs, banking details, credit card information or other sensitive data with unsolicited callers.

Members of the public are also advised to avoid engaging with unexpected callers requesting financial information and to end suspicious calls or online meetings immediately.

The Central Bank of Belize emphasized that it does not make unsolicited calls requesting banking credentials, passwords, PINs, credit card information or other sensitive financial details.

Anyone receiving such a request should treat it as suspicious and refrain from disclosing personal information.

The Central Bank is encouraging Belizeans to remain vigilant and share the warning with family members and friends to help prevent others from falling victim to the scam.

World.title: Nearly 1,000 CARICOM Nationals processed under Free Movement initiative in first year
World.content:
Nearly 1,000 CARICOM Nationals processed under Free Movement initiative in first year

By Zoila Palma: The Caribbean Community (CARICOM) says 939 nationals have been processed under its Free Movement under Enhanced Cooperation arrangement, one year after the initiative was launched on October 1, 2025.

Barbados, Belize, Dominica and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines were the first four participating member states to implement the arrangement, which aims to advance regional integration.

Under the initiative, eligible nationals of the four countries can enter and remain indefinitely in participating states, work without a permit and access specified services in accordance with national arrangements.

Nine applications were processed for Belize, 918 for Barbados, 5 for Dominica and 7 for St. Vincent and the Grenadines.

World.title: Belizean Tech Company NeoPeople expands operations to Grenada
World.content:
Belizean Tech Company NeoPeople expands operations to Grenada

By Zoila Palma: NeoPeople, a Tech Company developed in Belize, is expanding its presence in the Caribbean, with its implementation team arriving in Grenada to begin work with the Grenada Ports Authority. The team will implement the company’s Workforce Management and Payroll solution to support the authority’s human resource and administrative operations.

The expansion marks another milestone for NeoPeople, which currently serves clients in Belize, Barbados and Antigua and Barbuda.

The company says its entry into Grenada demonstrates how technology developed in Belize can compete regionally and provide solutions tailored to the needs of Caribbean organizations.

NeoPeople was established to help organizations manage employee information, payroll and workforce operations more efficiently. Its platform connects several human resource functions, including attendance, leave management, payroll processing, recruitment, approvals and workforce reporting, reducing reliance on disconnected systems and manual processes.

During the implementation, the team will work closely with the Grenada Ports Authority to configure the system according to its operational requirements. The company expects the solution to strengthen workforce management, improve payroll processing and enhance administrative efficiency.

Beyond the software implementation, NeoPeople says its regional expansion highlights the potential of Caribbean companies to develop technology solutions, build local expertise and create opportunities for skilled professionals.

World.title: U15 players to represent Belize at FIFA U-15 World Cup and festival in Azerbaijan
World.content:
U15 players to represent Belize at FIFA U-15 World Cup and festival in Azerbaijan

By Zoila Palma: Fourteen players from the Football Federation of Belize’s (FFB) Under-15 Boys National Football Team will represent Belize at the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival 2026 in Azerbaijan from October 24 to 30.

The FFB says that the team is scheduled to depart Belize on Monday for the three-day journey to Azerbaijan.

The selection process began with more than 30 young footballers from across Belize, all hoping to earn a place on the national squad. However, with only 14 players permitted per team, the selection process was challenging.

The FFB acknowledged the commitment and effort of all players who participated, including those who did not make the final roster.

The federation noted that participation in football helps young people develop discipline, teamwork, resilience, friendships and confidence.

The international competition will also give the Belizean players an opportunity to test their skills against teams from around the world, experience different styles of play and gain valuable experience to bring back to their clubs and communities. Players are expected to compete in between five and 10 matches across the festival’s seven match days.

For some members of the squad, the trip will be their first opportunity to travel abroad.

The FFB said the experience will expose the young players to new cultures and traditions while allowing them to connect with other young footballers who share their passion for the sport.

World.title: Team Belize defeat Nicaragua in AFECAVOL Women’s final four opener
World.content:
Team Belize defeat Nicaragua in AFECAVOL Women’s final four opener

By Zoila Palma: Belize’s national women’s volleyball team got off to a winning start at the AFECAVOL Women’s Final Four, defeating Nicaragua 3–1 on opening night in Managua, Nicaragua, on Thursday, October 15.

Belize secured the victory with set scores of 25–22, 25–22, 17–25 and 26–24.

Belize will return to the court today to face Costa Rica at 4:30 p.m. in Managua.

Fans can watch the match live on YouTube via Campeones TV.

World.title: Muffles College teacher placed on leave; police and social services investigate allegations
World.content:
Muffles College teacher placed on leave; police and social services investigate allegations

By Zoila Palma: Muffles College has placed a staff member on administrative leave following an allegation of misconduct involving a minor female student.

The school said in a statement that its administration received the allegation on October 6, 2026, and has launched an investigation.

The school reiterated that the allegation is extremely serious and said the staff member will remain on leave until the investigation is complete.

Muffles College also acknowledged investigations by the Belize Police Department and the Department of Social Services, adding that it will cooperate fully with both agencies.

“We are deeply concerned by the nature of this allegation and acknowledge the distress that this matter has caused to our students, faculty, staff, parents and the wider community,” the school stated.

Muffles College said it remains committed to due process and expects its staff to comply with established legal procedures, education-sector legislation and applicable codes of conduct.

World.title: UPDATE: Two men killed after gun battle with police in Sligoville
World.content:
ST CATHERINE, Jamaica — The two men who barricaded themselves inside a house with other occupants and engaged policemen in a gun battle in Sligoville, St Catherine, on Friday have been killed.

The morning shoot-out left one policeman dead and several other police personnel and a young girl injured.

The deceased officer has been identified as Corporal Trevoy Shaw, who was attached to the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Special Operations unit.

Another policeman, who sustained gunshot wounds to the head, is undergoing surgery. The injured girl is reported to be in serious but stable condition.

The confrontation began about 5:15 am when a team from the JCF’s Special Operations unit carried out an operation in the Five Miles area of Sligoville in search of wanted men.

The cops were reportedly clearing a building on a premises when they came under gunfire from the two men, who had barricaded themselves inside the house with other occupants.

A strong police presence remains in the area as investigations continue.

READ: Cop killed, others injured in Sligoville gun battle

— Llewellyn Wynter

World.title: Cop killed, others injured in Sligoville gun battle
World.content:
ST CATHERINE, Jamaica — An ongoing gun battle in Sligoville, St Catherine, has left several cops injured and at least one lawman killed, according to reports reaching Observer Online.

The Observer understands that the incident began about 5:15 am on Friday when a team from the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Special Operations unit was conducting an operation in the Five Miles area of Sligoville in search of wanted men.

The cops were reportedly clearing a building on a premises when they came under gunfire from two men who had barricaded themselves inside the house among other occupants.

During the exchange, a young girl who was inside the building reportedly sustained gunshot injuries. It is understood that she managed to escape from the house and was taken to hospital by a police team.

Sources described her condition as serious but stable.

Members of the JCF’s SWAT Team, Area 5 Area Fugitive Apprehension Team (AFAT), the Jamaica Defence Force (JDF) and other police personnel are on the scene as the operation continues.

More information to come.

— Llewellyn Wynter

World.title: DOMESTIC DISPUTE TURNS FATAL
World.content:
Nesta Anderson, a window maker and disc jockey who reportedly committed suicide after stabbing his wife who was taken hospital where she is said to be battling for life.

SAVANNA-LA-MAR, Westmoreland — The usually quiet community of New Market Oval in Savanna- la-Mar has been left in shock following a violent family dispute that left a nurse battling for life in hospital and her husband dead.

The husband, Nesta Anderson, a window maker and disc jockey, was from a neighbouring community. Police report that the couple had been involved in a dispute at their home when the woman was allegedly stabbed by Anderson.

Following the attack, Anderson used a ratchet knife to inflict stab wounds to his abdomen about 10:30 am Thursday.

He was rushed to hospital where he was pronounced dead. The Jamaica Observer was told that the couple, who had been together for more than a decade, has three young children.

Unconfirmed reports suggest the children witnessed the incident. When the Observer visited the community, police were processing the scene, while residents shied away from speaking publicly about the matter.

President of the Cooke Street Benevolent Society Bishop O’Neil Russell said he spoke with Anderson just a few days ago and that the incident came as a complete shock as the family was known to be quiet.

“We had a conversation because, you know, there were some things that the benevolent society was supposed to do for him.

We are always in constant dialogue, but he had not shown any sign of depression. It is so shocking. It comes as a shock to see really what took place,” stated Russell.

Councillor Julian Chang (Jamaica Labour Party, Savanna-la-Mar Division), who visited the scene, expressed sadness over the tragedy.

“It’s not anything to rejoice over. We all have issues, and we all have problems. We all go through things,” stated Chang.

She noted that the community, which was devastated by Hurricane Melissa last October, is already under stress and attempting to rebuild.

“We understand the constraints, but you know, we have to deal with our problems better than this, instead of taking our own lives or taking the lives of others,” stated Chang, who joined Russell in calling on people having problems to seek help.

Domestic violence, it can affect anyone regardless of our income, education, or social status. It stretches across all socio-economic backgrounds. We just have to understand that it is right in our midst and we should not be ashamed of it.

We should seek help. And I implore the persons in the Savanna-la-Mar Division, or anywhere for that matter in Jamaica, to seek help because I’m sure there are telltale signs even before it occurs,” Chang said.

She also emphasised the need for community sensitisation to stop judging victims and instead offer support, “because we all deserve to be safe in our own homes”.

World.title: Protecting Palisadoes
World.content:
An overhead shot of the Palisadoes Peninsula.

SPURRED into action by the warning from Hurricane Melissa which lashed sections of the island last year, the Cabinet has approved a US$56-million ($8.9 billion) coastal protection system for Palisadoes main road in Kingston which leads to Norman Manley International Airport and Port Royal.

The Category 5 storm, which hit Jamaica on October 28, 2025, reached wind speed of up to 190 miles per hour and devastated sections of the island’s southand north-western coasts, leaving several communities inaccessible.

With the pain from Melissa still fresh in Jamaicans’ minds, Minister of Energy, Telecommunications and Transport Daryl Vaz on Wednesday told a post-Cabinet media briefing that the Government is moving to provide even more protection for Palisadoes, the narrow approximately 14.2-kilometre strip of land that serves as a protective barrier for Kingston Harbour.

“The Government is advancing efforts to strengthen coastal protection along the Palisadoes Peninsula and Port Royal, safeguarding the Norman Manley International Airport, the main road that links from Harbour View to Port Royal, and surrounding communities against coastal erosion and storm surges,” Vaz said.

“The initiative represents a coordinated effort to protect critical transportation infrastructure, preserve access to Port Royal, and strengthen Jamaica’s resilience to coastal hazards.

So this is a far-reaching project that is going to once and for all protect the airport and access all the way to Port Royal,” added Vaz.

He underscored that over the last few years the Government has made efforts to protect the strip, which included approximately 4,500 metres of revetment work.

“We started back in 2007 when we did all of those boulders on the stretch.

As a result of Melissa and realising that, had Melissa come closer to Kingston, the access to the airport and, of course all the way to Port Royal, would be non-existent…

and seeing the work that has been done and what needs to be done, the Government has completed a comprehensive shoreline protection project [study] covering approximately 14.2 kilometres,” added Vaz.

He explained that proposed works will include strengthening revetments, rehabilitating dunes and mangroves, revegetation, and 12.1 kilometres of dunes [while] improving vulnerable road sections and installing coastal monitoring systems.

Underscoring that the country’s airports must also be built with resilience, Vaz noted that this project will be undertaken by the National Reconstruction and Resilience Authorities (NaRRA) under its work programme, with funding expected from its designated project pool.

He said with the project being under NaRRA, the Government will ensure that the procurement process is fast-tracked, which will result in it being completed in a timely manner.

“I just want to impress again, with all the noise that is being said about NaRRA, here is a project out of my ministry which has been approved by Cabinet as a NaRRA project.

Just to indicate that the noise is not always what you must listen to; you must watch the sale.

Here is a good sale.

Money that is going to be well spent [so] that if we have another catastrophe, God forbid, and it comes closer to Kingston, we will be able to respond how we responded to Melissa to get all the flights in with relief within hours,” Vaz told the media briefing.

The revetment work on Palisadoes came after Hurricane Ivan passed close to Jamaica’s south coast on September 10, 2024, leaving behind a trail of destruction not seen in the island since the passage of Hurricane Gilbert in 1988.

Ivan generated storm surge that caused the sea level to rise pushing mountains of sand and stones on the Palisadoes, leaving the vital roadway impassable.

The sand had also formed what was later referred to as the Palisadoes New Beach, essentially strips of land on the Kingston Harbour side up to 50 metres wide.

In 2007, sea water from storm surges associated with Hurricane Felix, which passed south of the island on September 3, flooded a section of the Palisadoes, making it impassable for several hours.

World.title: Insurers set to gain investment flexibility
World.content:
WILLIAMS... announced during the 2026/27 Budget Debate that the Government intended to simplify Regulation 47 to make it easier for life insurance companies to invest in corporate debt

Insurance companies could gain access to a wider range of investment opportunities under proposed changes to rules governing the sector, with the Senate’s Regulations Committee raising no objections to a measure that would remove a requirement for four conditions to be met simultaneously before certain investments qualify.

Deputy executive director of supervision at the Financial Services Commission (FSC) Nicolette Jenez told the committee on Thursday, during a virtual sitting, that the amendment to Regulation 47 of the Insurance Regulations is intended to widen insurers’ investment choices, which she said have been restricted by the existing rules.

Under the proposed change, insurers would be able to invest in certain obligations issued by solvent institutions if they satisfy any one of four conditions rather than having to meet all four at the same time.

The criteria include investments secured by adequate collateral and meeting prescribed fixed-interest requirements; investments rated as investment grade by an agency recognised by the FSC; obligations meeting prescribed earnings-coverage requirements; or obligations listed on the Jamaica Stock Exchange or another stock exchange recognised by the commission.

Jenez said the existing requirements, introduced through amendments in 2022, had limited insurers’ ability to diversify their portfolios, invest in corporate debt, and support infrastructure financing.

“While intended as prudential safeguards, this cumulative application of requirements has significantly restricted the range of investments available to insurers, limiting diversification opportunities, asset liability matching, participation in corporate debt markets, and infrastructure financing,” she said.

Asset-liability matching refers to ensuring that an insurer’s investments can provide the money needed to meet future claims and other financial obligations.

The FSC expects the amendment to broaden investment opportunities, support the development of Jamaica’s capital markets and make it easier for insurers to direct funds towards productive sectors of the economy.

The proposed change also forms part of the commission’s regulatory modernisation programme and its efforts to align Jamaica’s insurance supervisory framework with international standards.

Jenez stressed that the reform would not weaken the FSC’s oversight of the industry.

“What this amendment will not do is to reduce the FSC supervisory authority or existing prudential safeguards,” she said.

She pointed to other provisions in the Insurance Regulations, including 72(B), 72(G), 72(J), and 72(K), which set out requirements relating to insurers’ investment management and the handling of risk.

The amendment follows concerns that the existing rules have made it difficult for insurers to invest in some otherwise eligible corporate obligations because those investments must satisfy several conditions at once.

Finance Minister Fayval Williams announced in March, during the 2026/27 Budget Debate, that the Government intended to simplify Regulation 47 to make it easier for life insurance companies to invest in corporate debt.

The Government has argued that the existing requirements restrict investment choices and limit the development of the domestic corporate debt market.

World.title: Code Switch remixed
World.content:
450

Dancehall artistes Jahvillani and 450 have teamed up for the Code Switch remix, a collaboration that explores ambition, financial independence, and the determination to rise above challenging circumstances.

Released under YGF Records and Crown Boss Records, with distribution through VPAL Music, the track brings together two of contemporary dancehall’s distinctive voices, each offering his perspective on success and the sacrifices required to achieve it.

Through confident lyrics and a melodic hook, the entertainers reflect on their humble beginnings while expressing their aspirations for financial stability and a better quality of life.

For Jahvillani, working alongside 450 presented an opportunity to combine their individual styles while delivering a message that resonates with listeners navigating their own journeys towards success.

“Working with 450 was a good experience, because we both bring something different to the table musically. The energy was natural, and we understood the direction we wanted to take the song. It’s really about showing people that, regardless of where you start, you can work towards changing your circumstances,” Jahvillani told the Jamaica Observer’s Splash.

The collaboration blends Jahvillani’s commanding delivery with 450’s melodic approach, creating a sound that balances the celebration of material success with reflections on perseverance, resilience and personal growth.

Throughout the track, both artistes emphasise the importance of remaining focused despite setbacks, highlighting the discipline and sacrifices often required to achieve financial independence.

Jahvillani believes the song’s message extends beyond entertainment, particularly for young people who are working towards improving their circumstances.

“My ultimate hope is that this song reaches people everywhere, especially the youth who are trying to make something of themselves. Everybody wants a better life, but you have to stay focused and put in the work. I want people to enjoy the music, but also feel motivated to keep pushing towards their goals,” he added.

Accompanied by an official visualiser, Code Switch adds another release to both artistes’ growing catalogues.

The single is available on major digital streaming platforms.

World.title: ROCK MOBILE ROLL-OUT GETS EIB FUNDING
World.content:
THE European Investment Bank (EIB) has approved €4 million (approximately US$4.5 million) in financing for Rock Mobile — bringing Jamaica’s prospective third telecommunications provider a step closer to deploying its 4G broadband network islandwide.

The Luxembourg-based bank approved the financing earlier this month towards a €29-million (US$32.6-million) project to acquire and deploy a 4G wireless network across the Kingston Metropolitan Area and surrounding parishes.

The approved financing represents about 13.8 per cent of the estimated project cost for the company that had previously outlined plans to invest US$90 million in building its wireless data network — for which it is yet to fully launch commercial services.

The project, which is intended to deliver fixed wireless access services, comprises about 100 radio access network nodes to be installed at existing telecommunications tower sites, supported by core network systems, transmission equipment, service platforms and other technology.

“By supporting a new entrant into the Jamaican broadband market, the operation’s objective is to stimulate competition, which would result in improved service quality, affordability and digital inclusion by extending broadband coverage,” the EIB said in a summary sheet of its decision.

Rock Mobile secured rights to the 700-megahertz spectrum band in 2021 through an international bidding process, marking an important step towards establishing the company as a third major player alongside Digicel and Flow.

In 2022, the company signed an agreement with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to access market expertise and support for its network deployment, with a commitment to accelerate broadband access in unserved and underserved communities. Nokia has been contracted as the project’s sole network provider.

Rock mobile currently holds licences covering internet service provision, carrier services, international service provision and domestic voice services. Its stated goal is to provide nationwide internet coverage through wireless and fixed broadband offerings that addresses connectivity gaps and concerns about service quality and coverage.

“Since we began operation, we have been working hard behind the scenes to build a network and team that will bring the internet to Jamaica’s unserved and underserved communities,” the company noted in its bio.

“From the home, to the classroom, to the boardroom, we believe in data equity and that everyone deserves opportunities. Our big goal is to provide Jamaica with nationwide internet coverage through wireless and fixed broadband options. With incredible international partners like Nokia, our network will be world-class and will close the data gaps,” it added.

Government in welcoming news of the recent funding approval said it will continue to monitor the company’s progress towards launching its services as it expands broadband network islandwide.

The network’s completion and the commencement of commercial operations would introduce another competitor in the local telecommunications market, potentially widening consumer choice and improving access to broadband services.

Telecommunications Minster Daryl Vaz in his contribution to the 2025/26 Sectoral Debate in the House of Representatives last year had indicated that he was looking forward to the expansion of services and increased competition expected from the entry of a new provider.

“I, too, would have liked to have seen this third provider already offering services to the Jamaican people, but am cognisant that in a strong and fiercely competitive market, such as Jamaica, getting it right at the outset is important if the objectives are to be achieved,” he stated.

World.title: Purchase receipts take spotlight in Ruel Reid trial
World.content:
REID... has pleaded not guilty to fraud charges

A series of customer pick-up notes attached to six 2018 purchases made from a prominent local merchant were the subject of witness testimony during the fraud trial of former Education Minister Ruel Reid and his co-accused on Thursday.

The testimony and evidence put forward by the prosecution concerned who had purchased and collected the items: a Samsung Smart TV and an Android TV box bought on March 17, 2018, as well as a Proctor kettle, Hamilton Beach juicer, Black + Decker iron and a Conair footspa bought on April 29, 2018.

Thursday’s witness, who appeared in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court before Senior Parish Court Judge Sanchia Burrell, testified that he had provided direct oversight of safety and security at the merchant.

He said that when cash purchases, which can refer to cash, debit and credit card transactions, are made, a valid government- issued identification card must be provided.

Led during examination- in-chief, the witness confirmed to the court that an account is created for customers using that ID, customers’ first, middle, and last initials and their date of birth; and that no person can make a purchase on another person’s account.

Once a full cash payment is made, he confirmed, the system automatically releases that account and sends information to the merchant’s warehouse supervisor, who prints a delivery note or customer pick-up note.

The witness indicated that customers can then pick up the items from the warehouse, and this would entail both the customer and sales representative visiting the delivery area, verifying the delivery note/customer pick-up note, the sales rep testing the items in view of the customer, and the customer signing for the item and showing identification.

The witness noted that the customer pick-up note would detail the customer’s name, phone number, address, date of purchase, date of pick-up, product description, merchant stamp and serial number where applicable.

He then went on to confirm to the court that on February 5, 2019, a police sergeant called him and provided him with a telephone number.

The witness said a search of the merchant’s records database retrieved at least six customer pick-up notes associated with the phone number, under the name Ruel Reid, which were then printed and verified against the information in the database.

The witness confirmed that on February 20, 2019 he signed the six copies and, having been a justice of the peace (JP) at the time, stamped them, certifying that he had seen the original and that this was a true copy, signed the six documents with his signature and embossed each with a JP seal.

The prosecution then asked for six documents to be shown to the witness.

Attorney Anthony Armstrong, who alongside Linda Wright, represents Reid in the matter, was the only attorney present in court at the time.

Oswest Senior Smith, King’s Counsel, who represents Councillor Kim Brown Lawrence, joined later via Zoom.

Holding for the other attorneys, Armstrong showed all the defendants — Reid, Reid’s wife Sharen Reid and his daughter Sharelle Reid, former head of the Caribbean Maritime University(CMU) Fritz Pinnock, and Councillor Brown Lawrence — the documents before they were handed over to the witness.

The witness then confirmed that they were the six customer pick-up notes he had printed in relation to Ruel Reid.

The witness was asked whether the purchaser of an item could have another person pick it up, to which he responded that he had never had that experience, but that it could be facilitated via an authorisation note.

He then confirmed that no authorisation notes were attached to the six customer pick-up notes.

Under cross-examination by Armstrong, however, he was questioned on whether he, by looking at the pick-up notes, would be able to say which person picked up the items, to which he responded that he would not.

Armstrong also pointed out what he described as a note on one of the documents, which the witness said was a serial number not present on any of the other items.

Under re-examination, the prosecutor pointed out that the witness had said there were no authorisations present on the notes to indicate anyone else had picked up the items, but he had told the defence he would not be able to say who picked them up.

To this the witness responded that based on his understanding of the question asked by Armstrong, he had been referring to the fact that he had not seen who picked up the items.

The judge then asked the witness, based on the receipts, on the face of it, who picked up the items.

An objection was raised by Armstrong, who indicated that the witness had been clear in his answer that he would not be able to say who picked up the items, during cross-examination.

The objection, however, was overruled by Justice Burrell, who cited the witness’ clarification of that answer.

Upon being asked who, based on the customer pick-up notes, had collected the items, he told the court “Ruel Reid” in respect to all six items.

The judge also referred to the serial number on one of the documents and not present on the others, questioning what ‘originals’ he had signed to seeing, at which point he told the court, for the first time, that there had been physical documents alongside the electronic records that he had seen.

Reid and his co-accused are before the court on a 35-count indictment, accused of participating in a scheme with others unknown that siphoned off more than $25 million from the Ministry of Education and CMU.

They have pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Bail was extended for the accused in the case until court resumes on Tuesday.

World.title: Zelenskyy warns 20M Ukrainians could flee to Europe if Russia wins war
World.content:
The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.

BRUSSELS — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Friday that as many as 20 million Ukrainians could be forced to flee to Europe if his country falls to Russia.

“Russia is killing us,” Zelenskyy told reporters at a press conference on Friday during a summit of European Union leaders, adding Ukrainians were being “pushed” out of their country. “They [Russia] don’t want to stop.”

In the early days of Russia’s full-scale invasion, millions of Ukrainians fled their homes in Europe’s fastest and largest refugee crisis since World War II. Today, over 4 million Ukrainians live in EU countries under temporary protection status, with the largest populations in Germany, Poland and Czechia, according to Eurostat.

Zelenskyy’s stark warning comes as Ukraine heads into a brutal fifth wartime winter under Russian bombardment. Kyiv faces a budget shortfall of $30 to $35 million next year, according to projections from the International Monetary Fund — even accounting for a €90 billion loan Brussels agreed to provide last year.

The Ukrainian president traveled to Brussels to meet with European leaders and shore up financial support for his embattled country. While the EU is Ukraine’s staunchest backer, the bloc’s list of priorities is stacked with rising energy costs, looming elections, geopolitical crises and an impasse over its €2 trillion budget.

World.title: Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration
World.content:
The bloc’s 27 leaders were due to discuss migration during a special session on Thursday requested by Meloni and Frederiksen following a tense back-and-forth with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in June.

Tensions have risen further after Spain’s Ceuta exclave was overwhelmed by migrants during the summer and as far-right parties have made gains around the bloc.

The draft also “calls the Commission to explore [a] possible consultation mechanism to encourage coordination on national measures potentially affecting other Member States while respecting national competencies.”

While the last phrase does not name any one country, Sánchez has clashed with Meloni over his handling of the Ceuta migration crisis as well as Spanish measures to regularize around 1 million migrants.

However, language discussing the impact of migration on social housing was removed from the draft over concerns that it could be perceived as provocative toward Spain.

One of the diplomats — who, like the others, was granted anonymity to discuss confidential information — said the updated draft was unlikely to win unanimous support from all the leaders, but had been proposed to bring the language closer in line with political sentiment and spark debate.

World.title: Spanish opposition leader Feijóo calls for navy to be deployed to Ceuta
World.content:
Feijóo’s calls for a “firm response” are the latest in a wave of criticism of Sánchez’s government after more than 70,000 migrants arrived in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on the Moroccan border in late July. Migration ministers across the European Union have in recent months repeatedly demanded tough new EU migration policies.

His comments also come after unconfirmed reports that a Moroccan patrol boat remained in Spanish waters off the coast of Ceuta for hours Thursday, which the Spanish Civil Guard has denied. Moroccan warships also allegedly entered Spanish waters in July, though a European Commission spokesperson told Spanish press agency EFE Wednesday that it was “up to the Spanish and Moroccan authorities to clarify the facts.”

Feijóo spent Thursday morning at a summit of the center-right European People’s Party — of which the PP is a member — in Brussels, during which the EPP lashed out at the Spanish government over the Ceuta crisis in its closing statement, according to POLITICO’s Madrid Playbook. Conservatives have said they will implement measures to curb immigration if the government swings to the right after the snap election.

“Europe as a whole must recognize the failure of the Spanish government and exert the necessary pressure to prevent this crisis from becoming entrenched, spreading, or happening again,” Feijóo said in an opinion piece earlier this month.

Tensions over Ceuta and Melilla — which Morocco considers occupied territories — are becoming increasingly strained: A POLITICO poll earlier this week revealed that 58% of respondents believe an armed conflict between Madrid and Rabat is “likely” within the next decade.

In a landmark visit to the exclaves also this week, King Felipe VI said that Ceuta and Melilla were “an inalienable part of the political and national reality that is Spain. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of our country are not negotiable.”

The last time a Spanish head of state visited the territories was in 2007, when former King Juan Carlos I traveled to Ceuta and Melilla amid a diplomatic spat with Morocco.

World.title: EU prosecutors asked to investigate advisory body
World.content:
The EPPO did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“The EESC was informed by OLAF yesterday that this case has been transmitted to the EPPO,” an EESC spokesperson told POLITICO.



“Under these circumstances, the EESC cannot comment further except to re-confirm that when these matters first arose, the EESC president immediately and proactively referred the allegations to OLAF. The EESC will continue to respect fully the independence of this process.” Séamus Boland of Ireland was elected president in October 2025.

“The EESC and its senior leadership take this matter very seriously and remain fully committed to integrity, transparency and accountability,” the spokesperson added.

The EPPO has significantly stronger enforcement powers than OLAF. Whereas OLAF conducts administrative investigations, the EPPO investigates crimes against the financial interests of the EU, and can search private homes or seize evidence.

OLAF has also been investigating a report that EESC executives tried to smoke out a staff whistleblower who raised the alarm about the funding concerns, the EU Ombudsman told POLITICO.

Anonymous letters, seen by POLITICO, say that IT workers at the EESC were asked by senior managers to identify which staffers had connected to the OLAF website in previous weeks.

The EESC said those anonymous letters contained “serious personal threats” and added that they were not made through the EESC’s “robust formal whistleblower process.”

World.title: France, Germany strike bargain on Made in Europe, car emissions
World.content:
France and Germany now want to soften the 2035 target to 90% but without having to offer investments in alternative fuels to compensate the remaining 10%, as proposed by the European Commission.

“This balanced approach will enable the European Union to pursue its climate objectives while strengthening the technological sovereignty, industrial base and international competitiveness of its automotive industry,” the two countries said in a joint statement.

The agreement, first reported by POLITICO in July, was due to have been announced Thursday, during a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels. But it was held up at the last minute by disagreements within Germany’s governing coalition.

“We hope that this Franco-German dynamic can swiftly lead to an agreement with our partners, for our jobs and our industry,” French President Emmanuel Macron said in a post on social media.

An Elysée official on Friday made clear that, under the Franco-German deal, the scope of Made in Europe for automotive can be extended to the U.K. and Switzerland under certain conditions. — addressing a key concern of Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government ahead of a Nov. 20 U.K.-EU summit in Brussels.

The agreement was reached after the German Social Democratic Party, the junior partner in Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s coalition government, dropped its opposition.

World.title: Man arrested as police probe Your Party database dispute
World.content:
Officers also previously interviewed a woman in her 30s under caution in connection with the same investigation. The spokesperson added: “The investigation continues.”

Scotland Yard did not name any political party in its statement, and the spokesperson did not confirm which political party its investigation related to.

However, three other people with knowledge of the circumstances, all of whom were granted anonymity to discuss an ongoing case, said the investigation relates to a long-running dispute connected to the establishment of Your Party.

The left-wing party was co-founded in summer 2025 by the former Labour Leader Jeremy Corbyn and the former Labour MP Zarah Sultana, both of whom now sit as Your Party MPs in the House of Commons.

The two MPs clashed publicly over a September 2025 email that was sent to around 800,000 people on the new party’s mailing list, encouraging them to sign up as paying members. Sultana had promoted the membership portal while Corbyn described its launch as “unauthorised.” Sultana later said her sole aim had been to “safeguard the grassroots involvement that is essential to building this party.”

Neither the man arrested, nor the woman interviewed by police, are MPs and neither have been charged with an offence. Neither Corbyn nor Sultana are accused of wrongdoing.

World.title: Korrektur zu: Merz und Macron finden Einigung zum Verbrenner-Aus und „Made in Europe“
World.content:
Damit haben sich Berlin und Paris auf das gemeinsame Papier (hier) verständigt, über das POLITICO bereits berichtet hat.

Umweltminister Carsten Schneider hatte die Einigung jedoch zunächst mit einem Brief an Kanzler Friedrich Merz am Mittwoch aufgehalten. Darin verlangte der SPD-Minister mehr Konditionierung für grünen Stahl, erzählten mehrere Beteiligte POLITICO. Am Freitagmorgen gab es Gespräche der SPD-Minister über das weitere Vorgehen. Im Anschluss daran gab Schneider seinen Widerstand schließlich auf. Aus Kreisen des Umweltministeriums hieß es, die Beschaffung von grünem und recyceltem Stahl könne man auch national regeln.

„Mir war wichtig, dass wir bei dieser Gelegenheit auch klima- und industriepolitische Fortschritte für die Stahlindustrie erreichen“, sagte Schneider in einer Mitteilung. „Es soll Anreize geben, damit Autos künftig mit klimafreundlichem grünem Stahl gebaut werden.“

Laut dem Abkommen würde Deutschland strengere „Made in Europe“-Kriterien für den Automobilsektor im „Industrial Accelerator Act“ akzeptieren, auf die Frankreich gedrängt hat, im Gegenzug wird das Verbrennerverbot weiter aufgeweicht, eine der langen Forderungen Berlins.

„Wir wollen nicht, dass in Deutschland nur noch Komponenten aus Asien zusammengeschraubt werden, sondern dass entscheidende Komponenten hier entwickelt und hier produziert werden“, sagte Vizekanzler und Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil in einer Mitteilung. „Dazu gehört auch die Batteriezellfertigung und alles, was wir für deutsche E-Autos brauchen. Er verspricht der Autoindustrie „mehr ‚made in Germany’ und ‚made in Europe’“. Nun seien die Automobilhersteller in der Verantwortung, „in die Zukunft der deutschen Standorte zu investieren und Arbeitsplätze zu sichern“, so Klingbeil.

Derzeit sieht das Ziel der EU vor, dass Unternehmen die Emissionen von Verbrennungsmotoren bis 2035 um 100 Prozent gegenüber dem Niveau von 2021 senken, wobei sie die Möglichkeit haben, sich durch Initiativen wie Ausgleichsmaßnahmen und Investitionen einen Spielraum von 10 Prozent bei den Emissionen zu „erwerben“.

World.title: Trump slams Ukraine’s decision to resume energy strikes as a ‘disgrace’
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during a luncheon in the Rose Garden of the White House on Oct. 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. | Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images

U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday that Ukraine’s announcement to end the truce on Russian energy facilities was “a disgrace,” following reports that an oil refinery was hit in Russia’s Ryazan region.

Regional Governor Pavel Malkov said the Ryazan refinery was struck in a large Ukrainian drone attack Thursday, though Ukrainian authorities have not confirmed this. It is the first reported strike on Russian energy infrastructure since Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Kyiv and Moscow last Sunday.

Russia continued to hit Ukrainian energy sites despite Trump’s announcement, while Ukraine held fire on Russia’s energy sector. On Wednesday, however, Zelenskyy announced the pause was over — a decision Trump sharply criticized, saying it would drive up global oil prices.

World.title: Uzbekistan signs $4.7bn energy deals and outlines plans for two more nuclear power plants
World.content:
Uzbekistan has signed six energy agreements worth $4.7bn (€4.19bn) and announced plans for two more nuclear power plants, as President Shavkat Mirziyoyev seeks to attract foreign investment and meet rising demand from industry and data centres.

 

The agreements, signed during talks in Tashkent on Friday, cover 3,000 megawatts (MW) of new generating capacity and 400 MW of energy storage, according to the presidency.

Companies named in a project list obtained by Euronews include Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power and Saudi Tabreed, the UAE's AMEA Power, Japan's Toyota Tsusho and Sojitz, France's EDF, Qatar's Nebras Power, StorEn and CRE International.

A new approach to energy investment

Uzbekistan has attracted $35bn (€31.2bn) in energy investment over the past decade, according to President Mirziyoyev.

But he acknowledged that allowing developers to choose plant locations had concentrated generation in some areas and increased transmission costs elsewhere.

“We need an integrated energy system, not isolated power plants,” he said.

Future projects will undergo competitive tenders with grid connections and electricity purchase terms disclosed in advance. Six solar and wind projects totalling 2,200 MW will be tendered separately from the newly signed agreements.

The country's first National Energy Master Plan, covering the period to 2050, is due by July 2027, with a map of grid connection opportunities expected in March.

By 2030, the government aims to add 22 GW of generating capacity, build 5,000 kilometres of power lines and 16 substations, and expand storage capacity to 4.5 GW.

Annual electricity output is targeted to exceed 129bn kWh, with renewables, including hydropower, expected to account for 54% of generation, up from 31% today, according to the presidency.

The government has also proposed 12 manufacturing projects worth $850m (€758m), aimed at increasing domestic production of energy equipment.

Najy Benhassine, the World Bank's division director for Central Asia, said fast growth would require more generation and better networks. “All of this will need energy, will need more generation, but will also need the transmission infrastructure and efficient distribution to power the future growth of the country,” he told Euronews.

Neil McKain, the International Finance Corporation's country manager for Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan, identified a further weakness. “In the energy sector, I think it's energy efficiency. This is still a highly energy-intensive economy,” he told Euronews.

McKain said competitive tenders and higher electricity tariffs had also made projects more attractive to investors. He cited a 1.6 GW gas-fired plant in Syrdarya, financed with international partners and expected to start operating this year.

Nuclear expansion

President Mirziyoyev said Uzbekistan planned to build a second and a third nuclear power plant, with talks involving potential investors in the second project scheduled for Saturday.

“We have started the first nuclear power plant, and we have plans for the second and third as well,” he said.

Construction of the first plant, developed with Russia's Rosatom in Jizzakh, began in June.

Its two large and two smaller reactors would provide 2,110 MW. The project is estimated to cost up to $9.5bn (€8.48bn), with initial technical commissioning scheduled for 2029 and completion planned for 2034–2035.

Partners, costs and timetables for the additional plants have not been announced.

Oil and gas investment

Britain's BP and Azerbaijan's SOCAR are involved in exploration across six blocks in the Ustyurt region. Uzbekistan has prepared another 128 blocks for foreign investors.

Preliminary government estimates suggest these additional blocks could contain 5.8 trillion cubic metres of natural gas and 560mn tonnes of liquid hydrocarbons.

The government also wants to expand domestic processing through a methanol-to-olefins project in Bukhara, in south-western Uzbekistan, which would turn methanol into chemicals used to make plastics. It also plans to upgrade two oil refineries and introduce private participation in liquefied petroleum gas distribution.

Energy links to Europe

President Mirziyoyev said plans to export renewable electricity towards Europe through Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan were advancing.

The proposed Caspian Green Energy Corridor, backed by the Asian Development Bank and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, envisages a connection across the Caspian Sea and onward links through the South Caucasus and Black Sea.

The corridor remains at the feasibility stage.

International investors call for further reforms

President Mirziyoyev acknowledged persistent barriers to investment. “We have serious problems, shortcomings, bureaucracy and corruption,” he said.

A new Energy Investors' Council, chaired by Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, will seek to address obstacles including land allocation and grid connections.

At the meeting, Mohammad Abunayyan, founder and chairman of Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power, called for reforms to Uzbekistan's financial and capital markets.

“We need reform in the financial sector. We need reform in capital market,” he told the president. He also urged stronger requirements for employing Uzbek workers and using local suppliers in future projects.

Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, chief executive officer of UAE-based Masdar, said his company had invested more than $2bn (€1.78bn) since 2019, developed over 2 GW of renewables and committed to another 2 GW.

“In return, we require predictability, certainty and stability in policy, regulation and the agreements underpinning our investments,” he said.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass as recovery from cancer surgery progresses
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital at noon on Friday after medical tests confirmed that his condition continues to improve following lung cancer surgery, according to the Vatican.

 

“His post-operative recovery allows him to carry out his normal daily activities completely on his own,” said a medical update signed by Leo’s personal physician Dr. Luigi Carbone and the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli hospital, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.

The service was attended by off-duty medical and nursing staff, as well as members of the Vatican City State’s Gendarmerie Corps. During his homily, the Pope thanked hospital workers for their daily care of patients and, in particular, for the care they have provided him.

Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital alongside his secretary as he recovers from lung cancer surgery, 16 October 2026. (Vatican Media via AP)

Pope's appeal to governments: Food as an 'obligation of justice'

In a message to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) marking World Food Day on Friday, Pope Leo XIV warned against using food as a weapon of war and urged governments to redirect military spending towards sustainable agriculture.

He said hunger was largely caused by a lack of political will and collective solidarity, stressing the importance of guaranteeing universal access to safe and sufficient food.

“It is an obligation of justice that binds both individual states and the international community,” the pope said.

What comes next for Pope Leo XIV?

Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin said it was too early to predict when the pope would resume his duties, suggesting his pontificate may need to be adjusted depending on his recovery and medical advice.

“We can’t make any type of predictions,” Parolin said Thursday. as reported by LaPresse and ANSA news agencies.

“The question now is when he will return, under what circumstances he will return, and what the doctors say. And based on all these factors, the pope will then adjust his pontificate, if it needs to be adjusted.”

The Vatican is moving ahead with preparations for Pope Leo XIV’s planned trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November, despite uncertainty over his recovery.

World.title: Palestinians in Gaza dread another winter with nowhere safe to shelter
World.content:
When it rains, Abdullah Siyam moves his family’s bedding to the one corner of his house in Al-Mughraqa, in central Gaza, where water does not seep through the roof.

 

Bombardment that struck neighbouring homes left cracks in the ceiling, and the family has no alternative. “We move our mattresses there and sleep. That is the solution,” he told Euronews.

More than 4,000 damaged buildings in Gaza need to be fully or partially demolished, including more than 2,300 still inhabited by nearly 44,000 people, according to preliminary estimates cited in this month's report by the UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

As the fourth winter since the war began approaches, families across the Palestinian territory are bracing for the rainy season in cracked houses and worn-out tents.

Abdullah Siyam inside his home in Al-Mughraqa, west of Gaza City محمد نشبت- يورونيوز

Siyam is not alone in Al-Mughraqa. His neighbour Mariam Abu Hazein spends rainy days pushing water out of her home before her blankets soak through.

She borrowed three from her daughter after her own became waterlogged, then returned them when they dried.

Water falls in the rooms and the bathroom. She has placed containers on the floor to collect it and uses a floor wiper to push it outside. “It is as if we were in the street,” she said.

Mariam Abu Hazein, a Palestinian woman, on top of the rubble of her home in Al-Mughraqa, west of Gaza City محمد نشبت- يورونيوز

Mohammed Bardawil, from the same area, said he feared facing the upcoming winter with worn-out tarpaulins, which he could not afford to replace.

“Honestly, we really do not want winter to come,” he told Euronews, saying that wind and rain create hardship “whether we are in houses or in tents.”

At the Deir al-Balah market, tarpaulin prices rose from 120 to 180 shekels (€35 to €53), with larger sizes at around 230 shekels (€68). A dome tent went up from 1,300 shekels (€384) to 1,700 shekels (€502).

The remains of a house destroyed by shelling in Al-Mughraqa, west of Gaza City, Gaza Strip محمد نشبت- يورونيوز

Ahmed al-Siqali, displaced from Khan Younis, told Euronews by phone that equipping and reinforcing his tent cost him around 1,200 shekels (€355), covering timber for beams and two tarpaulins, a sum he raised with his brother’s help from outside the strip.

According to a June assessment cited by the Norwegian Refugee Council, 71% of families surveyed in damaged buildings said they could not afford repair materials.

The 2023-2025 Israel-Hamas war in Gaza, which resulted in the deaths of more than 70,000 Palestinians — mostly women and children — has left large parts of the Palestinian territory in ruins.

It also triggered one of the worst humanitarian crises in the region’s recent history, with aid agencies warning of famine conditions and a near-total collapse of the strip's health infrastructure.

Everything could collapse

The danger in some structures goes beyond leaks. On 16 September, the Al-Saada residential building in Gaza City collapsed, killing 21 Palestinians including 12 children and five women.

Gaza civil defence said residents received prior warnings but stayed because no alternative shelter was available, and that structural damage from the last war caused the collapse.

Civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Basal warned on 17 September that damaged towers collapsing in crowded areas could threaten both residents and people in surrounding tents.

A room inside a house damaged by Israeli shelling, Al-Mughraqa, west of Gaza City محمد نشبت- يورونيوز

He said the service received around 150 distress calls from people in dangerous buildings within 24 hours.

Gaza’s Government Media Office announced on 20 September a plan to evacuate and demolish around 255 buildings at risk of collapse and provide temporary shelter for affected families, noting shortages of heavy machinery, funding and safe land, and saying some families had not left despite warnings.

UN humanitarian coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov called for the urgent delivery of rescue equipment, machinery, fuel, tents and tarpaulins to the most vulnerable groups within four weeks after the Al-Saada collapse.

Not letting aid in

The response faces a supply blockage. The Norwegian Refugee Council said Israeli authorities approved 36,960 pieces of timber and 660 emergency shelter kits in August, then blocked their entry on 26 August and 2 September and later rejected a renewed UN coordination request.

Israel’s Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) told international media in September it would not allow heavy equipment or reconstruction materials to enter before Hamas was disarmed, accusing it of exploiting aid, a charge the group denies.

As of 18 September, the UN Shelter Cluster had received 26% of its required funding, amounting to $193.7 million.

A UN report in late September counted around 17,000 tents, tarpaulins and shelter kits across organisations’ stocks and ongoing purchases, expected to support around 50,000 families — supplies at various stages of readiness rather than items waiting at crossings.

Signs of destruction inside a flat in Deir al-Balah, in the centre of the Gaza Strip محد نشبت- يورونيوز

On the ground, preparations include cleaning drains, raising shelters off the ground, repairing sewage networks and identifying sites for voluntary relocation.

A survey of more than 400 displacement sites found 217 at medium to high flood risk, hosting around 235,000 people. Making those sites safe requires clearing explosive hazards, levelling land and providing water, drainage and road access.

Siyam believes rain in Gaza is a blessing, but he does not wish for it given the state of his house. “Who would wish to drown?” he asked.

World.title: Belgium: Pumpkimania festival takes over Groot-Bijgaarden Castle
World.content:
Thousands of pumpkins have transformed the grounds of Groot-Bijgaarden Castle near Brussels into a colourful autumn wonderland for the annual Pumpkimania festival. This year's theme, “The Magic of the Forest”, features towering sculptures of foxes, owls and deer covered in pumpkins of every shape and size, sourced from Belgium, Germany and Portugal.

 

The star attraction is a giant pumpkin weighing 772 kilograms, grown for the castle's traditional weigh-off on 26 September. Visitors can also watch giant pumpkins being turned into makeshift kayaks for rides across the castle lake.

Organisers expect around 50,000 visitors before the festival closes on 1 November. Families can take part in pumpkin-carving workshops at weekends, while the Halloween programme will see the castle open daily until 7pm from 24 October. The festivities will end with a giant pumpkin-smashing event.

Despite a difficult growing season following a hot summer, the displays have filled the estate with thousands of pumpkins. Located in Dilbeek, about 10 kilometres from central Brussels, the festival costs €16 for adults and €9 for children aged 5 to 14, with free entry for younger children.

World.title: Paris Motor Show: Renault and Citroën unveil electric concepts inspired by classic cars
World.content:
Some of Europe's best-known cars are making a comeback at the Paris Motor Show, reinvented for the electric age.

 

Renault, Citroën and Fiat are drawing on decades of motoring history to develop new electric models, from family cars to affordable city runabouts, as European manufacturers face growing competition from Chinese rivals.

Renault’s E-Space concept reimagines its pioneering family car, first launched in 1984, with six seats across three rows, while Citroën is looking to revive the iconic 2CV as an affordable car for ordinary people.

The Paris Motor Show runs until 18 October.

World.title: '‘It’s easier dealing with Trump than Putin,’ Zelenskyy tells Euronews amid US tensions
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has rejected Donald Trump's claim that he is more difficult to deal with than Vladimir Putin, telling Euronews that negotiating with the US president is easier than dealing with the Russian leader.

 

Speaking to Euronews on Friday at an EU summit in Brussels, Zelenskyy was asked about Trump's criticism and whether European leaders supported Ukraine's continued strikes on Russian oil refineries despite pressure from Washington to halt them.

"Well, it's easier dealing with him than with Putin. I'm talking about Trump," Zelenskyy said.

"I've had several meetings with the President of the United States of America, and we always find topics for discussion and decision-making."

The remarks come amid tensions between Kyiv and Washington over Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and Trump's decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel. The US president has criticised the strikes, blaming them for contributing to rising global fuel prices.

Zelenskyy said his priority was to defend Ukraine's national interests, regardless of external pressure.

"I defend the interests of Ukraine and the Ukrainian people exclusively. We were attacked, occupied, and our people were killed. It is only logical that we have the right to defend ourselves," he said.

"This is entirely lawful, and so we will do just that. We will stand firm."

He did not directly address whether European leaders had backed further strikes on Russian refineries, instead reiterating Ukraine's right to defend itself.

Zelenskyy accuses Putin of blocking peace efforts

The Ukrainian president said Ukraine remained committed to ending the war through negotiations but accused Putin of having no genuine interest in a peace agreement.

"Putin does not want negotiations right now, in any format," he said, describing Moscow's rhetoric as "a parody of a genuine desire to end the war".

"He does not want the war to end. I am convinced that this is why even the Donbas is too small for him."

Zelenskyy warns against easing sanctions on Russia

Zelenskyy also warned that easing restrictions on Russian diesel could lead to further concessions, undermining Western efforts to limit Moscow's ability to finance its war against Ukraine.

"In my view, we cannot accept these diesel deals, these agreements, because gas deals will follow. I am absolutely certain of this. After gas, sanctions will be lifted on other things as well," he said.

"It will all come down to the banking system, individuals, and the chemical industry."

He also voiced concern over the future of frozen Russian assets, suggesting they could be at risk if Western countries continued to make concessions to Moscow.

"If I do not defend this, who will do it for us? I mean diplomatically," Zelenskyy said.

European leaders have meanwhile sought to maintain pressure on Moscow despite Washington's decision to ease some sanctions.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Friday that the EU would not lift its sanctions until Russia ended the war. European Council President António Costa called for increased pressure on Moscow rather than further concessions.

World.title: Could Tesla’s flying car send sales and shares soaring?
World.content:
Elon Musk, Tesla’s CEO and co-founder of SpaceX, recreated a “Knight Rider” moment, showing off his companies’ engineering capabilities with a supercar equipped with cold-gas thrusters developed using SpaceX technology.

 

Tesla's share price increased on Friday, largely due to the hype, but while the demonstration impressed, analysts see limited commercial value in the new model.

Mamta Valechha, consumer discretionary analyst at Quilter Cheviot, described it as a “headline-grabbing engineering moment” designed “to generate excitement around the brand”.

Rico Luman, senior sector economist, transport and logistics, at ING, called the presentation “a publicity stunt which emphasises Tesla’s image as an innovative company, which offers brand value”, adding that cars are still about emotion and lifestyle, so the demonstration makes an impression.

Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, called the demonstration on X “an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers”.

Valechha noted that even Elon Musk had previously played down the Roadster’s likely financial impact. “The commercial value is likely to be strengthening Tesla's innovation narrative rather than generating meaningful profits.”

Musk said production is expected to start in 2028. Tesla has opened reservations, although the flying Rocket version is available by invitation only. The company has not announced final selling prices.

The Roadster was unveiled in 2017, and a year later Musk suggested that thrusters might allow it to fly. This was followed by repeated delays, as the production was originally promised for 2020. "Credibility and execution risks remain high,” summarised Valechha.

Could flying cars reach a wider market?

The flying features of the Roadster are not approved for public road use, adding another hurdle to any ambitions of a wider roll out of the technology, on top of the high production costs.

Luman said the flying car has been designed as a niche sports vehicle, but “larger scale flying car activity won’t be realistic in the foreseeable future as the same airspace rules apply as for aircraft and certification as aircraft by EASA (in Europe) is then required”.

Whether the Roadster falls within aviation regulations depends on its design, capabilities and intended operation, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) told Euronews Business.

The agency said it does not comment on “specific certification applications or activities involving individual manufacturers”.

However, “any vehicle intended to operate as an aircraft would need to meet the applicable aviation safety requirements”, the agency said. These could include pilot qualifications for the driver.

Luman added that, on top of the complex rules that apply, airspace is already rather full, particularly with increasing drone activity.

“Large numbers of uncontrolled flying cars won’t likely be allowed by authorities for safety reasons.”

Valechha also sees limits to how widely the technology could be used.

“Some technologies could filter into other vehicles over time, but flying or thruster-assisted features are unlikely to be economically viable for higher-volume cars in the foreseeable future due to cost, complexity and regulatory hurdles.”

Luman agreed, adding that some space technology could be useful in high-end cars.

“Flying cars in general may be a cheaper alternative for private jets, but not in this concept”.

Pressure to turn technology into profits

Like many big tech companies, Tesla is growing, but faces pressure to turn expensive technology projects into stronger profits.

The company is investing heavily in new technology, while profit growth is failing to keep pace with sales.

Second-quarter revenue rose 26% year on year to $28.24bn (€25.20bn), but net profit attributable to shareholders fell about 5% to $1.11bn (€990m).

First-half capital spending more than doubled to $8.28bn (€7.39bn). Tesla expects capital spending above $25bn (€22.31bn) in 2026, driven by AI and manufacturing investments.

Investors have been pricing the company's value gradually lower than at the beginning of the year, when Tesla shares traded at $438, whereas on Thursday they cost more than $362, amounting to a 14.6% fall in 2026 so far.

Other analysts also mentioned that Tesla valuation is largely based on its self-driving ambitions, the Optimus model, and SpaceX merger hopes.

Merging SpaceX and Tesla?

The technology in Tesla's Roadster, borrowed from SpaceX, fuelled expectations that the two companies are going to be merged in the future.

Barclays analyst Dan Levy has suggested an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting, according to Barron’s. However, a deal remains speculative, with no certainty about whether or when it would happen.

For now, the Roadster’s clearest appeal may be to wealthy enthusiasts.

“This new futuristic model is great for fans and lovers of gadgets who have the ability to spend the money on it. And I’m sure there are quite some around,” added Luman.

World.title: Vatican releases first photos of Pope Leo XIV after lung tumour surgery
World.content:
The Vatican has released the first photographs of Pope Leo XIV since he underwent surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung.

 

The images, published on Friday, show the pontiff celebrating Mass at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, where he is recovering following the operation.

The Vatican said the Pope’s condition was continuing to improve, with his post-operative recovery allowing him to carry out daily activities independently and remain in good spirits.

World.title: Pope Leo recovering from surgery, will deliver Sunday prayer
World.content:
The Vatican has announced that Pope Leo XIV is recovering from lung surgery. Photos released on Friday showed the pontiff celebrating Mass at Rome's Gemelli Hospital unaided.

The Vatican on Friday announced that Pope Leo XIV is swiftly recovering from lung surgery and will make his first public appearance on Sunday, when he will deliver the traditional noontime Angelus Prayer.

Vatican representatives did not specify whether he would deliver the prayer at St. Peter's Square or from the hospital.

Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin said Friday that a recitation from the hospital was a possibility but would depend on Leo's post-operation recovery.

Leo, who is 71, shocked the world and its 1.4 billion Catholics last Sunday by announcing that he would be undergoing surgery within days. Two day's later, on October 13, doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung after the pontiff was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

Doctors are awaiting the results of Leo's biopsy, which will tell them about the make-up of the tumor and give insight into whether his cancer has spread, allowing them to determine whether he may need to undergo further treatment, such as radiation or chemotherapy.

On Friday, the Vatican said Leo was going about normal activities on his own and released photos of the pontiff saying Mass at Rome's Gemelli Hospital. He was seen wearing vestments and standing next to his personal secretary, Edgard Rimaycuna, a Peruvian priest.

Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass alongside his personal secretary, Peruvian priest Edgard Rimaycuna Image: Vatican Media/AFP

"His post-operative recovery allows him to carry out his normal daily activities completely on his own," said a medical update signed by Dr. Luigi Carbone, Leo's personal physician, and Dr. Stefano Margaritora, head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital.

The doctors said blood tests and chest x-rays had confirmed Leo's steady improvement.

"At the moment, we have not received any communication from the doctors ⁠regarding ​his discharge, other than what we ​were told from the beginning about a one-week timeframe," a Vatican spokesman ​said.

"The question now is when he will return, under what circumstances he will return, and what the doctors say. And based on all these factors, the pope will then adjust his pontificate, if it needs to be adjusted," said Cardinal Parolin, who added, "We can't make any predictions."

One of the first questions raised by Leo's hospitalization and surgery was whether he would be able to go through with a planned papal trip to South America in just a few weeks' time.

Though this remains an open question, the Vatican on Friday said planning was "going forward" regardless, releasing the names of those journalists accredited to travel with Leo to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17.
