World.title: Trump’s new press secretary says China lacked ‘proper’ toilets
World.content:
Washington – White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked “proper toilets” in an interview that aired on Thursday.

Zacharia, 41, is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials, after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.

The press secretary, who previously lived in China, recalled in an interview that the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.

“We were all being told Hillary (Clinton) was going to win. The golden days or the glory days of America were over. That China was on the horizon,” Zacharia told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.

“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,” she added.

There was no immediate comment from Chinese authorities.

Trump has boasted about his “great relationship” with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During a Washington summit in September, the two leaders discussed topics ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year.

Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday and only answered questions from three journalists.

She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative spokesperson, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.

Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. She also said she had worked at a law firm in Beijing.

Asked about her legal background on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move with her husband to China.

Zacharia said that she did not retake the bar exam upon returning to the United States due to the birth of her first child.

World.title: Indonesian stocks dive 11% as MSCI weighs market reclassification
World.content:
Jakarta – Indonesian stocks plunged more than 11 percent Friday as index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain the country’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities in Jakarta said in April they had completed reforms, hoping to avoid the downgrade, which could deal a blow to government efforts to kickstart Southeast Asia’s biggest economy, and have a significant impact on investment decisions.

But on Friday MSCI said investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”.

“Despite the announced reforms, significant concerns remain around market dysfunction, including continued suspected coordinated trading behaviour and lack of evidence of meaningful enforcement.

“Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate and is launching a consultation on a proposal to reclassify Indonesia as a Standalone Market.”

“A reclassification to Frontier Markets would not properly recognise the depth of the market problems,” it said.

A standalone classification could force investment funds tracking the MSCI’s emerging market indexes to sell Indonesian holdings.

Argentina, Lebanon and Palestine are among the markets with the designation, with none in Asia, according to Bloomberg.

The Jakarta Composite Index collapsed eight percent at the open, sparking a trading halt. When trading resumed it was down 11.1 percent, its heaviest fall since early 1998 and sitting at its lowest level since 2020.

The index has now fallen more than 40 percent since the start of the year.

– Rupiah weakens –

In reaction to the news, the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) said it “respects MSCI’s independence in assessing and determining market classification based on its proprietary methodology”.

“However, considering the various progress and reform measures that have been taken, the IDX will request further clarification from MSCI regarding the basis for the considerations and assessments behind this announcement.

“We also need to emphasise that this MSCI announcement is still part of the consultation process, with input being accepted until April 30, 2027, and does not constitute a final decision.”

The rupiah dropped about 0.8 percent against the dollar to sit at around around 18,060, having hit 18,209 in June, its weakest level on record.

Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, the Indonesian central bank’s head of monetary management and securities, said the bank would take action to ensure stability of the rupiah, which had already tumbled around eight percent this year to a record low.

“Amid rising global risk-off sentiment, which has driven US dollar strengthening and put pressure on domestic financial markets, capital outflows from domestic portfolio assets are expected to continue.

“Bank Indonesia is committed to maintaining a presence in the market to uphold Rupiah exchange rate stability in line with its fundamentals and to ensure that market mechanisms function properly.”

The central bank had carried out several rate hikes earlier in the year to shore up the rupiah, after it came under pressure over the state of Southeast Asia’s biggest economy.

The bank is due to hold its next monetary policy meeting on Wednesday.

New York-based MSCI produces international indexes used by investors as a benchmark to balance their portfolios.

It has a significant impact on investment decisions through its flagship emerging markets index, which contains 1,200 companies with a market capitalisation more than $10 trillion.

Fund managers worldwide keep a close eye on what countries are included or excluded in MSCI’s indexes as that can trigger adjustments to their portfolios.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new cabinet ministers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — On Thursday, Iraq’s parliament confirmed 11 cabinet nominees and three deputy prime ministers, including Laith al-Khazali, a key member in Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq who faces US terrorist sanctions.

The nomination is a politically risky decision for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, whose administration is dealing with strained regional ties and severe economic challenges as a result of the continuing US-Israeli war against Iran.

Al-Khazali is the brother of Qais al-Khazali, the commander of Asaib Ahl al-Haq, which Washington listed as a foreign terrorist organization in 2020.

Both brothers were classified as specially designated global terrorists, and the US Treasury sanctioned them individually in 2019 for suspected participation in violence against Iraqi demonstrators.

Their US designations also included references to assaults on American troops, such as a 2007 operation that killed five US soldiers.

The parliamentary decision raises concerns about al-Khazali’s nomination and its ramifications for Baghdad’s relationship with Washington, especially as al-Zaidi wants to reinforce Iraq’s sovereignty and manage ties with neighboring nations.

The appointments come as Iraq faces a deteriorating economic crisis, with oil export interruptions and liquidity shortages putting strain on the government’s budget.

Al-Zaidi has declared a significant depreciation of the Iraqi dinar, warning that the government confronts unprecedented economic and security problems.

The presence of a US-sanctioned militia member in the government’s high leadership may hamper Baghdad’s attempts to preserve fruitful relations with Washington.

World.title: ‘Mixed feelings’: AI cracks centuries-old ciphers
World.content:
Tokyo – Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the wartime missive written in code, creating a puzzle that went unsolved for more than 200 years — until AI cracked it in a matter of hours.

Artificial intelligence is helping non-specialists unlock the secrets of historical sources, a trend described as a “turning point” in a field previously the preserve of scholars and dedicated hobbyists.

One new sleuth is Carter Church, a 27-year-old AI engineer who decrypted a 19th-century letter to one of Napoleon’s generals.

Without digital tools, the task could have taken weeks, but the latest model from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI broke the cipher in just six hours.

“What AI mostly brings is persistence,” Church told AFP, saying he felt “an unbelievable sense of satisfaction and excitement when I saw the result”.

The message from 1809 — detailing French and allied troops’ positions in two dozen lines of symbols, numbers and letters — had lain ignored in an online academic archive.

Because traditional, low-tech methods to crack ciphers are effective but time- and labour-intensive, historians “have more important problems to solve, so many ciphers like this often sit unattended”, said Church.

To find the solution, Church, who works at US cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, needed to learn “very little” about code-breaking techniques or the historical period.

He spent some evenings going over it, then consulted Japanese patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online list of unsolved ciphers, to verify it.

“2026 will be remembered as a turning point for codebreaking of historical ciphers,” Tomokiyo wrote on his website Cryptiana, a go-to resource for the small but enthusiastic global community of amateur cryptographers.

– ‘Mixed feelings’ –

Researchers were already developing AI models to break ciphers, but the public release of state-of-the-art generalist tools has unleashed dozens of new solutions.

Although Church used OpenAI’s most powerful model, GPT-6 Astra, other people have used top offerings from rival US lab Anthropic instead.

Tomokiyo said that since mid-September, most of the ciphers on his list have been cracked using AI.

“There remain some tough problems” which could stay an enigma for years to come, because there is less relevant data available to help AI figure them out, the 58-year-old told AFP.

“I’m excited long-time problems are now solved, but on the other hand, I have mixed feelings, because AI seems to have solved these difficult problems so easily,” he said.

With technology draining the satisfaction of being first to crack a cipher, a fellow code-breaker told Tomokiyo: “I feel useless.”

AI is surpassing human abilities in pursuits from mathematics to computer programming, while threatening to alter or even eradicate many jobs.

The technology is transforming the work of historians not only by decoding documents, but also by analysing millions of medieval manuscripts or helping read ancient scrolls.

Too fragile to be unrolled without risking destruction, the Herculaneum Papyri — hundreds of papyrus scrolls carbonised in the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD — are now being X-rayed and analysed by AI to reveal the hidden writing inside.

Researchers in Italy announced in June the first complete virtual unrolling of a scroll, which turned out to be a treatise on ethics.

– ‘Facebook of the past’ –

AI is also being used to build a huge, searchable collection of previously inaccessible sources on Jewish history and culture by transcribing 10 million pages of Hebrew manuscripts.

“It’s gigantic. No human being could process such a quantity” of data, said project leader Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra, of the Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes in Paris.

Researchers hope the databases created using the digitised text — which he likens to a kind of “huge Facebook of the past” — could help bring to light links between people, places and ideas.

And at the French capital’s Notre Dame Cathedral, an AI system has been trained to transcribe 14,600 Latin pages from the church’s medieval archives — a task not dissimilar to code-breaking.

“These are minutes drawn up by notaries who abbreviate their decisions. The script is highly administrative, very pragmatic… with rather technical vocabulary,” said historian Julie Claustre, who leads the e-NDP project.

With character recognition rates ranging between 88 and 94 percent, the project has revealed information about the cathedral’s daily life, its building work, its staff and the care of abandoned children.

Doing the same by hand would take “several decades”, said Claustre, but “it’s not just a time-saver”.

Automation enables “inquiries that were not previously possible; it transforms the conditions of research.”

World.title: Using AI to help find Mexico’s legions of missing children
World.content:
Mexico City – Veronica Rosas is one of tens of thousands of Mexican mothers looking for a child that has disappeared into a vortex of violence fueled by brutal cartel turf wars.

Now artificial intelligence may be able to help the loved ones of Mexico’s legions of disappeared.

Two new AI tools are being developed to help in the search for the more than 134,000 people being sought.

Rosas’ son, Diego, went missing at the age of 16 in the central town of Ecatepec in September 2015 after leaving his home to meet some friends.

The state prosecutor’s office said he was kidnapped by a criminal gang but have not established which group, why, or whether Diego is still alive.

“It’s been 11 years and I still don’t know where Diego is. There’s no line of investigation leading us to find out what happened to my son,” Rosas, 52, told AFP at one of the demonstrations held regularly in Mexico City to demand justice.

Cases like Diego’s have prompted two universities to develop AI tools they hope will provide answers.

Regresa (Return) was developed by Mexico’s main public university, UNAM. It uses anthropometry — human body measurements — to create an image of how the faces of minors, which remain frozen in time in missing persons posters, may have changed over time.

With investigations generally dragging on for years, these updated likenesses are a recurring demand of the families.

Countries like the United States, India and China already use facial recognition and age progression software to search for kidnapped children.

In Mexico, some prosecutors’ offices use the technology but most software relies on open-source photo databases that don’t reflect typical Mexican traits.

Regresa’s developers took a different approach.

They created their own image bank from hundreds of photos and data from 75 Mexican volunteers to make portraits that feature more typically Mexican features.

Anthropologist Ana Juarez, one of the project’s founders, explained that Regresa also uses different technology to age the children.

“Many software programs only work with facial contours or textures, or add filters that simulate wrinkles. We seek to develop a scientific approach that shows how a person grows in craniofacial terms,” she explained to AFP, referring to imagining that predicts the developments of the skull.

– Peace boxes and posters –

In Mexico, the inaction of authorities over many years has prompted many families to carry out their own investigations.

AI is also being used by an anthropologist at the private Ibero-American University to help facilitate those searches.

Emiliano Zolla is mapping the missing by gender, age and the circumstances of their disappearance, in the hope that it will help families refine their search.

Among his observations, based on data about cases in the State of Mexico, the country’s most populous, are that many of the missing are young women who disappear either going to or returning from school or work.

The use of AI could be a game-changer, Rosas said, on learning about Regresa from AFP.

“This initiative is very important because they’re not the little people who were taken back then,” she said.

Rosas has erected a makeshift mailbox bearing a picture of 16-year-old Diego on Mexico City’s main avenue to receive clues as to his whereabouts or greetings for him on his birthday.

Karla Lechuga created a search collective after the disappearance of her 19-year-old son, Jeshua Cisneros, in 2025.

Groups like hers have installed dozens of “peace boxes” in churches across the country to gather information.

They also post photos of their missing loved ones in public spaces and urge criminal groups to provide anonymous tipoffs.

“We have found some people alive, unfortunately others not,” Lechuga said.

World.title: NCW steps in after video shows senior J&K IAS officer 'abusing' woman subordinate

NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Women (NCW) on Friday said it had taken suo motu cognisance of a

purportedly showing a senior Jammu and Kashmir IAS officer verbally abusing a junior female officer and sought an action taken report (ATR) within seven days.

âNCW Chairperson Smt. Vijaya Rahatkar has written to the Chief Secretary, Jammu & Kashmir, seeking verification of the video, an impartial inquiry and appropriate disciplinary and legal action if the allegations are established,â the NCW posted on X.

âThe Commission has also called for safeguards against workplace harassment, victimisation and professional retaliation, along with protection and support for the woman officer.

Every woman officer is entitled to a safe, respectful and dignified workplace. Abuse of authority and workplace humiliation must be addressed with utmost seriousness,â the women's rights body added.

The NCWâs action came after a video purportedly showed senior IAS officer Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, administrative secretary of Jammu and Kashmirâs Department of Labour and Employment, allegedly abusing a junior female officer during a video conference meeting, calling her âbloody sh*tâ.





What happened during the video meeting

In the purported video, Ranjan can be seen questioning Beenish Wani, a Jammu and Kashmir Administrative Service (JKAS) officer posted as Assistant Director, Employment, in Ganderbal, over her performance.

Wani told him that she had written to the deputy commissioner and additional deputy commissioner after the district officer of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) said targets could not be achieved and that officials would not cooperate.

Ranjan asked her to obtain the response in writing and says she should have informed him directly about the matter.

âWhy do you need NRLM if others are doing the work? Do you only have to write letters and seek the medal? They are just a helping tool, not the main authority,â Ranjan is heard saying in the video.

NEW DELHI: India has expanded its crude oil supply network from 27 countries to 41 and will continue to diversify imports, increase refining capacity and explore new sources of oil amid geopolitical tensions, minister for petroleum and natural gas Hardeep Singh Puri said.âWe have diversified our sources of supply from 27 to 41,â he said, while speaking at the Pathways to Viksit Bharat Conclave at Shri Ram College of Commerce, ANI reported.Puri said disruptions to international shipping routes could have a direct impact on Indian industries and household expenses.âA disruption along a distant shipping route can alter the costs of an Indian factory and the budget of an Indian household,â Puri said.Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the event, Puri said India was importing more than 5 million barrels of oil per day while exporting around 1 million barrels, supported by its expanding refining capacity.He said Indiaâs crude oil procurement would continue to be guided by the availability of supplies at competitive prices. He also pointed to emerging tensions in the Red Sea, saying the government was monitoring the situation and working to ensure uninterrupted supplies.The minister said India would also need to raise domestic energy production to meet growing demand as economic expansion and industrial activity drive up consumption.He expressed confidence that the Samudra Manthan scheme, which supports deep-sea oil and gas exploration, would help strengthen domestic output over the next three years. World.title: HM Shah slams Punjab govt on murders of anti-drugs crusaders, MHA seeks report on 3 recent cases
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Home minister

on Friday raised the recent cases of suicides and murders related to the narcotics menace in Punjab, saying that they point to the rising threat of drugs, gangsterism and organised crime and also raise serious questions about the law and order in the AAP-governed state.

Simultaneously, the home ministry on Friday sought separate reports from the Punjab govt on three recent cases involving drug-affected families and crusaders fighting the narcotics problem in the state. These include the Sept 7 suicide by Gulzar Singh, father of a young man addicted to drugs who had named an AAP minister in a video statement before taking his own life; and the murders of anti-drugs activists Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa disrict on Oct 13 and Bikramjit Singh in Batala, Gurdaspur, on Thursday.

In a post on X on Friday, Shah said with Punjab grappling with the aforesaid threats, "the biggest question before the Punjab govt is -- who will ultimately take responsibility for the security of Punjab's people?"

"In Dirba (Sangrur), a father taking poison under pressure, and in Mansa, the broad-daylight murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota, who had raised his voice against drugs, have raised serious questions about law & order in Punjab.





Parvinder's father has levelled grave allegations against the Punjab government and their MLA," he stated.

Shah alleged that the

in Punjab flourishing, the threat of organized crime is growing, and questions raised about the safety of those who speak out against drugs. "Mr Chief Minister, the people of Punjab do not want publicity - they want answers; not announcements, but results; decisive crackdown against drug networks, and an impartial probe into any political patronage provided to criminals.

Our goal is clear â crackdown against the drug trade, protection of our youth's future, strict action against criminals, and the rule of law in such a way that no citizen is forced to live under the shadow of fear," he said, directly addressing chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann.

On Friday, the MHA wrote to the Punjab chief secretary, seeking detailed reports on each of three recent cases, including two highlighted by Shah on X.

The letter seeking Punjab govt's response on Gulzar Singh's suicide in Dirba, refers to reports alleging that the deceased had "questioned the availability of synthetic drugs in his area and raised allegations against a minister in the govt of Punjab." The reports further alleged that Gulzar was "subjected to systematic harassment and pressure by the local panchayat, which purportedly forced him to take his own life.

"

In a second parallel communication sent to the Punjab chief secretary, the MHA raised the killing of Parwinder Singh Jhota, reportedly a "crusader against the rampant sale and abuse of narcotics and psychotropic drugs in Punjab" on Oct 13 in Mansa, Punjab, and the following protests in the state.. "The state govt is requested to furnish a comprehensive, factual report regarding the incidents, and steps taken by the state govt in this case," states the MHA letter.

A third communication by MHA to the Punjab chief secretary seeks a detailed report on the attack on Bikramjit Singh and two others, Nishan Singh and Gurmukh Singh, in Batala tehsil of Gurdaspur, during which Bikramjit died and the other two were critically injured. "It has been alleged that these attacks are related to narcotics drugs..in view of the potential law and order ramifications of this issue in the state, the state govt is requested to share a detailed report on the incident," states the MHA letter signed by undersecretary Subodh umar Jayaswal.

World.title: Marine experts call for satellite-based decision support system for sustainabler fisheries amid climate crisis
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As climate change alters ocean temperature, marine habitats and distribution of fish stocks, scientists from govt institutions, including Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), have called for using satellite-based decision support systems and a framework for sustainable fisheries management in the country where the livelihood of about 30 million fisherfolk is linked to fisheries and allied activities.

They, while participating in the 47th Asian Conference on Remote Sensing this week, proposed strengthening early warning and fisheries advisories using satellite technologies, underlining that timely information on ocean conditions, potential fishing zones and weather-related risks could help fishers make better-informed decisions.

With the climate change leading to marine heatwaves and shifts in the distribution of marine species, affecting fish availability, fishing operations and the livelihoods of communities dependent on marine resources, Shubhadeep Ghosh, ICARâs assistant director general, said, âThese challenges underscore the need for science-based monitoring systems and adaptive fisheries management.â

Marine experts, including scientists from ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) and Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), during the conference explored the potential of remote sensing to help address these challenges by integrating satellite-derived information on sea surface temperature, ocean colour and other oceanographic conditions with fisheries data, field observations and scientific assessments.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





They said such integration can strengthen understanding of changing marine environments and support more informed fisheries planning, and pitched for improved communication and last-mile delivery of advisories to translate scientific information into practical benefits.

ICAR-CMFRI in its handbook on âapplication of GIS as a decision support tool in marine fisheriesâ noted that Remote Sensing (RS) is the first satellite-based technology which overhauled marine fisheries prediction, based on ocean temperature, ocean colour and chlorophyll content.

It said, âSatellite based technologies, which are capable of handling spatial data, revolutionized natural resource management over a period of time".

World.title: 'Interfering in electoral practices': India pulls up US lawmaker for claims on voter roll deletions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Friday strongly rejected US Congresswoman

's remarks concerning the country's electoral process, calling them âunwarranted and uninformedâ and accusing her of interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy.

Responding to a question during a bi-weekly media briefing in New Delhi, ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the remarks undermined democratic principles.

âWe find the remarks of the Congresswoman unwarranted and uninformed and tantamount to interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy. This is an approach that undermines democracy itself,â Jaiswal said.

The response followed Jayapal's expression of concern over reports of names being removed from India's electoral rolls.

The Democrat representing Washington state wrote on X, âI am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls.â

Indian ambassador also rejects allegations

India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, had also dismissed Jayapal's allegations on Thursday, describing them as interference in India's internal affairs.

âThe remarks by Rep. Jayapal on India's electoral and political processes are unacceptable interference in India's internal affairs,â Kwatra wrote on X.





He added that India had strong constitutional institutions and a long record of conducting free and fair elections.

âIndia is a vibrant democracy with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections. Always open to constructive conversation with the Congresswoman to dispel her misconceptions,â he said.

World.title: PM-SETU clears Rs 1,195 crore for five ITI clusters in 3 states, J&K
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has approved investments worth Rs 1,194.92 crore to upgrade five clusters of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across Maharashtra, Odisha and Jammu & Kashmir, taking the cumulative investment cleared under the PM-SETU scheme to Rs 3,687 crore.

The five projects will be implemented in partnership with Tata Steel Foundation, BVG India, Belrise Industries, Eagle Infra India and Inderdeep Infra India. The investments are aimed at modernising ITI infrastructure, introducing industry-aligned courses, upgrading trainer capabilities and strengthening links between technical training and employment.

The approvals were given at the sixth meeting of the National Steering Committee of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU), chaired by skill development secretary Debashree Mukherjee on Friday.

The Pune cluster in Maharashtra has been allocated Rs 241 crore, while the Kataka cluster in Odisha will receive Rs 240.50 crore. The Jammu cluster has been approved Rs 240 crore, followed by the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar cluster at Rs 238.01 crore and the Srinagar cluster at Rs 235.41 crore.

Each cluster will have a hub ITI and four spoke institutes, with the hub expected to anchor training and other capacity-building efforts across the cluster.





Mukherjee said the approvals would help strengthen ITIs, improve training and increase industry participation. She also urged the clusters to work towards ISO certification and include at least one WorldSkills-aligned trade or competency area in their approved implementation plans.

She said progress in Jammu & Kashmir was encouraging and reflected a commitment to strengthening skilling and expanding opportunities for young people in the region.

Under the approved plans, state governments, industry partners and participating ITIs will work together to upgrade facilities, introduce new-age training programmes and improve the relevance of courses to employersâ requirements.

World.title: 'Once again, an abduction': Aides claim Neha Bora taken to unknown location by police
World.content:
AISA chief Neha Bora was detained by the police from Mandi House.

NEW DELHI: Aides of All India Students' Association (AISA) chief Neha Bora on Friday claimed that she had been taken to an unknown location after being detained by Delhi Police while on her way to participate in the ''Lehra Do Tiranga' protest in the national capital."Neha Bora detained alone, taken to unknown location," a post on her X account read adding that she did not have her phone with her."Delhi Police must answer: where is Neha?" the message said, describing the incident as âonce again, an abductionâ.Bora was detained at Mandi House, a short while after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke was picked up from his residence in Jhandewalan, as both headed to participate in the proposed protest on Friday.The detentions triggered jostling among protesters, camera crews and security personnel amid heightened security arrangements across the capital.Police sources told news agency PTI that Dipke was taken to Jafarpur Kalan police station after being detained. The location where Bora was taken was not immediately clear from the information available.Earlier in the day, more than 20 Delhi Police personnel visited Dipkeâs residence in Jhandewalan and served him a notice directing him to refrain from any action that could prejudice the rights of citizens, traders, commuters, patients and others.A senior police officer confirmed the detention of both leaders, saying the situation remained peaceful.âWe have detained Dipke and Bora. The situation is very peaceful. Some protesters have reached Connaught Place and will be removed soon. Our main objective is to maintain law and order and ensure smooth traffic movement,â the officer said.Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar visited the DCP New Delhi office at Parliament Street police station to review security arrangements.Security personnel cordoned off Central Park in Connaught Place, forming a human chain along its metal railings. A tear gas vehicle and a Vajra vehicle were stationed outside the park, while Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed inside. Traffic police personnel were also deployed to regulate movement along Connaught Place's inner and outer circles.Hundreds of protesters, including members of CJP and student organisations, gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House for a series of flash protests, waving the national flag amid heavy police deployment.

World.title: CPI(M) to launch agitation over ESA areas in Kannur
World.content:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] will launch a major public agitation against the Keralam government for the latter’s alleged failure to address the concerns of residents of hill regions over the notification of Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESA) in Kannur district.

Protests will be held continuously after October 25, focussing on Kottiyoor, Cheruvanchery and Aralam regions, CPI(M) district secretary K.K. Ragesh said.

Mr. Ragesh alleged that the State government had remained indifferent to the concerns of people living in the hilly areas of the district, while the Centre continued to refuse to accept the revised report submitted by the State on ESA boundaries.

The ESA notification introduced by the United Democratic Front (UDF) government in 2014 had caused extremely serious consequences for the hilly regions of the district. A ground-level survey was necessary to identify the actual ESA areas, he said.

However, instead of conducting such a survey, the Oommen V. Oommen Committee prepared what Mr. Ragesh described as a hastily compiled report in 2013. Based on this, the UDF government independently identified the State’s ecologically sensitive areas in 2014 and submitted a report to the Centre.

That report continues to form the basis of the seventh draft of the ESA report. The areas recommended by the committee remain designated as ecologically sensitive in the State and this, Mr. Ragesh said, was the fundamental reason for concerns among residents of hilly regions.

After the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government came to power, it conducted a detailed study and concluded in 2018 that the ESA provisions should apply to only 92 villages. Objections to the proposed boundaries were examined at the district level, and the revised report was submitted to the Centre after excluding residential areas and including forest areas.

The Centre, however, refused to accept the revision. It questioned how the State could amend a report it had previously submitted.

Official’s transfer

The transfer of Vigilance Deputy Superintendent of Police (DySP) who had exposed corruption in the Kannur Corporation was suspicious, Mr. Ragesh said.

The officer had entered the Corporation office and seized several documents, Mr. Ragesh said, adding that he was transferred soon afterwards as a consequence of these actions.

World.title: Telangana, Karnataka can form integrated industrial value chain: IT and Industries Minister Sridhar Babu
World.content:
Telangana and Karnataka can combine their complementary strengths to build an integrated industrial value chain spanning aerospace, life sciences, semiconductors, textiles and technology services, Telangana IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu said on Friday (October 16, 2026).

Speaking at the Bengaluru roadshow of Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026, organised in association with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), he invited Karnataka-based companies to participate in the summit scheduled to be held at Bharat Future City, Hyderabad, from December 7 to 9.

Describing the two States as “two halves of one value chain”, Mr. Sridhar Babu said Telangana was seeking partnerships with Karnataka rather than competing with it for investments. The two States could leverage their respective strengths in research, design, manufacturing and large-scale production to strengthen India’s industrial ecosystem, he said.

He cited opportunities for aircraft engines designed in Bengaluru to be machined in Hyderabad’s aerospace parks, vaccines developed in Bengaluru’s biotechnology laboratories to be manufactured at scale in Genome Valley, and semiconductor designs to be integrated into electronics manufactured in Telangana. Similarly, cotton produced in Telangana could be processed at the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park and supplied to Bengaluru’s garment manufacturers serving global brands.

Global companies with their first Indian capability centres in Bengaluru could consider Hyderabad for their subsequent facilities, drawing on the talent pool and innovation ecosystem comprising institutions such as the Indian Institute of Science, IIT Hyderabad, the Indian School of Business and IIIT Hyderabad, besides startups supported by T-Hub, he said.

Outlining the State’s Telangana Rising 2047 vision, the Minister said the government aimed to build a $1 trillion economy by 2034 and a $3 trillion economy by 2047 under the leadership of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.

He identified Bharat Future City, envisioned as a net-zero greenfield urban development with an AI City and a dedicated Mobility Valley, as a key component of the State’s growth strategy. Other initiatives included the Young India Skills University, the Regional Ring Road, new industrial corridors and the Musi rejuvenation programme.

The Minister assured prospective investors of time-bound clearances through the Telangana State Industrial Project Approval and Self-Certification System (TG-iPASS), along with support from the government in facilitating investments. He also thanked investors for the confidence they had placed in Telangana at the Telangana Rising Global Summit held in December last year.

World.title: Plea to repair dilapidated buildings in SC habitations
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Friday directed the State to file a counter affidavit to a public interest litigation petition that sought a direction to authorities to repair dilapidated buildings in Scheduled Caste habitations.

While hearing the petition filed by K. Muruganandam of Pudukkottai district, a Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and R. Poornima issued the direction. The petitioner is the district coordinator of Neelam Panpattu Maiyam in Pudukkottai district.

He said the issue concerned basic facilities such as safe houses, roads, access to burial and cremation grounds, drinking water facilities, sanitation, community halls, anganwadi buildings, health facilities, libraries and other public assets serving the SC habitations.

The damaged houses, roads, overhead tanks, sanitation facilities and public buildings affected the residents. The government’s own survey records showed that several deficiencies required attention, he said.

He said the Constitution required the State to take special care for the advancement of the weaker sections. Article 46 of the Constitution required the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections and to protect them from social injustice and exploitation. Article 21 of the Constitution protected the right to live with dignity.

The petitioner sought a direction to the authorities concerned to identify and repair damaged infrastructure and other public buildings in SC habitations in Ramanathapuram, Theni, Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Tenkasi and Dindigul districts. The court posted the matter for hearing to November 6.

World.title: Keralam govt. to consider special rehabilitation package for P&T flats residents
World.content:
The State government will consider a special package to rehabilitate the affected families at the P&T Apartment Complex at Mundamveli in view of safety concerns, Minister for Local Self-Governments K.M. Shaji told the Assembly on Friday.

Responding to a calling attention motion moved by Mohammed Shiyas, MLA, he said the government was considering a comprehensive investigation into construction defects and corruption allegations regarding the housing complex built under the LIFE Mission Scheme.

“The government is convinced that it is imperative and necessary to take further steps as soon as possible. The procedures for this will be started very soon. Another demand is that they [residents] should get the title deeds. Currently, they are only allowed occupancy on the GCDA [Greater Cochin Development Authority] land. However, details of the rehabilitation process will be examined later as the process is being considered. Not only are many of the housing complexes under the LIFE project stalled, they are also uninhabitable due to unscientific construction,” the Minister said.

He added that the government had already announced a Vigilance investigation and initiated a preliminary inquiry into irregularities in the construction of the housing complex.

“Despite repeated instructions, the Thrissur District Labour Contract Cooperative Society, the contractor, was not ready to carry out the necessary repairs. Subsequently, members of the technical committee formed by the government visited the site and terminated the society, which was responsible for the construction work and did not complete the work as per the contract. However, no investigation was conducted later regarding the losses caused due to the negligence on the part of the agency. The company was only terminated,” said the Minister.

World.title: Jagtial man remains in Dubai jail, family seeks Telangana government help
World.content:
Aegurla Mallesham of Jagtial district is reportedly still in a Dubai jail despite completing his six-month prison term, as he is unable to pay a fine of AED 1,50,000 (approximately ₹ 39 lakh) imposed by a local court.

His family has sought the Telangana government’s intervention for his release and repatriation to India. Mallesham, a native of Mothukuraopet village, went to Muscat, Oman, in 2018 in search of employment. According to sources, he later entered the UAE from Oman without a passport or visa and remained in Dubai for nearly eight years before being apprehended during an inspection on March 8.

A Dubai court sentenced him to six months in prison and imposed the fine, followed by deportation, in connection with his entry into UAE from Oman without a passport of visa and alleged illegal stay there. His wife Latha and mother Buchavva recently petitioned Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy through CM Pravasi Prajavani in Hyderabad, seeking his release and repatriation to India.

Mandha Bheem Reddy, Vice-Chairman of the Telangana Government’s NRI Advisory Committee, said the government had obtained details of the case through the Indian Consulate in Dubai. Consulate officials visited Awir Jail and met Mallesham on July 23, he said. According to Mr. Reddy, consultations are being held with legal experts on the possibility of waiving the fine, seeking a pardon or pursuing other available legal remedies to secure Mallesham’s release and facilitate his repatriation to India.

World.title: Jharkhand: Congress, youth wing activists scuffle with police during protest outside CEO office
World.content:
Activists of the Jharkhand Congress and its youth wing on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) scuffled with the police as they tried to break through barricades during a demonstration outside the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office in Ranchi, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

After they failed to enter the premises, the agitators blackened the official name board of the Election Commission.

Also read: CEC row LIVE updates

Hundreds of workers of the Congress and its youth wing marched from near the Old Assembly premises, and the march culminated at the office of the CEO in Dhurwa. Workers carrying placards raised slogans such as "Where will you find the vote thief? In the BJP office," "Gyanesh Kumar Resign" and "Vote thief, vacate your seat of power."

"People of the country have prepared a chargesheet against the CEC. Allegations against the CEC are enough for a person holding a constitutional post to resign," Subodh Kant Sahay, a former Union Minister, said.

"People across the country are looking for Gyanesh Kumar, asking where the traitor has fled. This is happening because he worked to snatch the voting rights of citizens of this country. The CEC has murdered democracy through the SIR," Kumar Gaurav, State president of the Youth Congress, said. He said the protest sought to give voice to ordinary individuals who were making rounds of offices with their certificates to get their names enrolled in the voter list.

"Democracy is being murdered... Two other members of the Election Commission had raised questions on Gyanesh Kumar's style of working, but now irregularities committed by him have come out," Kumar Raja, president of the Congress's Ranchi Mahanagar unit, said. The entire electoral system could not be transparent until the CEC resigned, he said, adding that the party would continue its struggle.

The protests came after a report by The Indian Express claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders they said were issued without their knowledge, even as the nationwide rollout of the SIR was under the supervision of the full Commission.

World.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered boasts upgraded action and marginally better visuals
World.content:
One of the hottest developers in the world right now is undoubtedly Polish based CD Projekt Red, from their humble beginnings with Witcher 1, to releasing one of the best action roleplaying games the world has seen in 2015 with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.

The game not only redefined the open world genre, but also set the template and inspired a decade of excellent action RPGs such as Assassin’s Creed Origins and Odyssey, Ghost of Tsushima and the Horizon games. With gamers still playing through the game today (many on their very first playthrough veering off the main path), making a remastered version was a more than a welcome addition, and the best way to play or replay the game.

Before 2015, not many had heard of The Witcher, based on the Andrzej Sapkowski fantasy novels of the same name. The game not only garnered a huge following, but also roped in fans that included Superman Henry Cavill who sought out, and was eventually chosen for, the role of Geralt of Rivia in the Netflix series. Now more than a decade later, you have a new excuse to step into the shoes of Geralt, the mutant witcher who earns his living hunting monsters across the land. In The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, Geralt searches across a war-torn continent for his missing adopted daughter, Ciri, only to realise that she has been pursued by an ancient otherworldly evil that is about to bring the end of times.

Built on years of rich lore, The Witcher 3 thrives on its deeply personal connections. As Geralt’s journey unfolds, it brings together a memorable ensemble of old friends and past flames — from his loyal bard buddy Dandelion, to the formidable sorceress Yennefer of Vengerberg, the enduring love of his life. The story weaves threads that connect them all, while a spectral army, the Wild Hunt, snaps at his heels. Yet, there is always time to help a friend, attend a masquerade ball or pick up a host of monster contracts.

The Wild Hunt boasts some of gaming’s most memorable quests, none more so than the tragic story of the Bloody Baron. In a world where monsters and humans collide, the game delivers storytelling at its absolute finest.

Now, here is where the 2026 updates to the game come in and they are worth your time. First off, you get a fully reworked skill tree. After the extensive skill overhaul in Cyberpunk 2077 resulted in vastly improved build variety, Witcher 3 Remastered receives a similar treatment, adopting a more conventional branching skill tree in which investing points into core abilities unlocks additional perks.

Gone is the arbitrary tier-gating that forced you to dump points into unwanted skills just to reach higher levels. With most abilities now capped at three ranks instead of five, every ability point feels instantly impactful, and just like the new Cyberpunk 2077, it lets you assemble specialised builds faster and gives returning players a fresh slate with a full point reset upon launching. As of this review, other platforms were buzzing with new build guides, breathing life into the system.

Among the mechanics, combat receives a healthy dose of changes to fluidity, animation and finishers for Geralt, but the enemies have also received updates, especially monsters, making combat far more visceral and dynamic, with not only better animation, but new counterattacks, attacks and behaviours.

The original combat was no slouch, but making it more dynamic makes Geralt more nimble. This also translates to jumping, vaulting, climbing and traversal. Cameras have also been updated to translate that dynamism in combat, and they work at giving you a better sightline into your enemies’ movements.

Signs, which are Geralt’s magic spell system, have received updates in its particle effects, impact and its own finishers, and now comes with its own skill tree enhancements.

However, the biggest upgrades are on the graphics, and while there are many videos scrutinising the original game versus the remastered, it is important to note that over the years The Witcher has got a fair amount of polish and refreshes. What the remastered brings is a larger sense of detail, and a cleaner, more expansive look overall, with a lighter tone, and new Path-tracing lighting systems, that are quite demanding on your system but makes for excellent lighting.

The game is supported on all the latest Nvidia, AMD and Intel upscaling tech, and if you happen to own a Playstation 5 Pro, then you get native PSSR (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution), based on the latest news from Sony on the release of the lighter QSSR for the base PS5; hopefully, the remastered should get support for that as well.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Publisher and Developer: CD Projekt Red Price: Free for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt owners. Those who own the base game get the two complete edition DLC free.

Regardless of the system you are on, Witcher 3 Remastered looks incredible, even at lower graphic fidelities, and the new animation systems and finishers are incredible. If you have the hardware to support 2K or 4K gaming at the highest levels with Path-tracing on, you are in for a treat, especially with the now free DLC’s Blood and Wine, which looks absolutely stunning with its Southern France- and Italy-inspired setting.

The new graphics updates make The Witcher 3 stand even taller than other games today, and it made me want to hit New Game for the third time in 10 years since the original, just to see how much has changed, and how much love has been put for this groundbreaking game.

A 100 years into the future, when people look at the past through museums, they will view The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt as an important work of art, something which many believe is true today too. A masterpiece in every way, from graphics, story, world-building, combat and its place in our hearts, Songs of the Past is already looking great and so is the upcoming Witcher 4 focused on Ciri’s tale.

The remastering was not a required step; people would have played Songs of the Past anyway as an important bridge between the old and the new game. However, CD Projekt RED take their craft seriously and have given us much much more than a coat of paint. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered is not just an update, but a way to experience the game once more before its final song.

World.title: Prepare Rohith Vemula Bill draft in three months: Bhatti
World.content:
Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka has directed officials to prepare a preliminary draft of the proposed Rohith Vemula Telangana Bill within three months, with a focus on preventing discrimination based on caste and social background in higher educational institutions.

Chairing the second meeting of the Cabinet sub-committee on the proposed legislation, he directed the Scheduled Castes Development Department to lead the drafting exercise and ensure the participation of the Law, Education and Home departments, along with relevant institutions, including the University Grants Commission (UGC).

The meeting discussed the proposed law’s framework, the composition of the committee, legal aspects and the process of consultations with stakeholders. He said the draft should take into account the problems faced by students on campuses, instances of discrimination and challenges likely to arise during implementation of the legislation.

The committee also discussed seeking technical and legal assistance from NALSAR University of Law in drafting the Bill. Scheduled Castes Development Department Secretary Vijendra Boi said the university had agreed to extend its expertise in framing the provisions.

Mr. Bhatti directed the departments concerned to coordinate closely and complete the preliminary exercise within the stipulated three-month period so that the draft could be taken up for further scrutiny. Ministers Ponnam Prabhakar and Adluri Lakshman Kumar were among present.

World.title: Political party head upset over not being appointed KP governor, claims Naqvi
World.content:
LAHORE: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday claimed that the “head of a party” was “extremely upset” about not being appointed the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, without naming anyone.

“The head of a party is extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship,” Naqvi alleged while speaking to journalists in Lahore.

He was seemingly referring to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP.

This politician, he continued, had remained “dependent on the establishment for decades to advance his political career”.

“These are the same politicians who remained in politics for decades with the support of the establishment, and this politician even relied on the establishment to arrange air tickets for the members of his party,” he further alleged.

He said such politicians had little justification for criticising others now, particularly after having benefitted from the same system they currently denounced.

“Political differences are part of politics. But instead of using inappropriate language and making allegations, political leaders should speak on the basis of arguments and facts,” the minister said.

Naqvi’s remarks come days after the Centre imposed a governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Fazl, as well as Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan.

In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI had was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI. Both sides had held separate meetings with Fazl, reportedly for his intervention to help break the deadlock in the negotiations.

And after the federal government imposed governor’s rule in KP, Fazl accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts for mediation.

Addressing a press conference at his residence, he had said his party rejected the decision to impose governor’s rule in KP “word for word” and that the JUI-F would challenge the decision through all available democratic and constitutional forums, including in the public, parliament, and courts.

“We are not prepared to bow, even for a moment, before such unconstitutional measures,” he had added.

More recently, Fazl again censured the Centre, accusing it of depriving the provinces of their rights.

He further recalled that his party had expressed reservations over the merger of tribal areas into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa after the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018. “We were not against the merger, but we said that it was an issue of the political future of the people of tribal areas,” he said, alleging that the people of those areas were not consulted on the merger.

Former Fata districts and security situation

During his interaction with journalists, Naqvi was also critical of concerns regarding the allocation of resources to former tribal areas. “When the districts … were not getting their rightful share for years, why were these people silent?” he questioned.

The minister commented that political leaders had failed to speak out for the rights of the people of the former tribal areas at the time, and stressed that the rights and resources of the people of those areas should be treated as an issue above political interests.

Naqvi further said KP was facing serious security challenges, and called on political leaders to play a constructive role in restoring peace and combating terrorism.

“Instead of fanning the flames and creating unrest, political leaders should play their role in restoring law and order and eliminating terrorism,” he said, maintaining that the province needed peace, stability and collective efforts rather than political confrontation.

World.title: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier made the remarks during a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He welcomed the envoy to Pakistan and congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities.

Ambassador Albugamy, assumed his diplomatic responsibilities in Islamabad on Thursday, reaffirming the commitment to strengthening the strategic and fraternal ties between the two countries.

During the meeting, PM Shehbaz said Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations had made significant progress in recent years and reaffirmed Islamabad’s commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation across various sectors.

He “strongly condemned” the recent escalation in Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, which had resulted in deaths and injuries, including among Pakistani nationals, the statement said.

The prime minister also said the two countries had always stood by each other, adding that the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance marked “historic milestones” in their longstanding fraternal relations and reflected their shared commitment to regional peace and security.

PM Shehbaz also thanked the Saudi leadership for its longstanding economic and financial support to Pakistan and assured the ambassador of Pakistan’s full support and cooperation in further strengthening bilateral ties.

Ambassador Albugamy also met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, where the latter underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

He also reaffirmed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia’s “shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity”.

The FO added that the new Saudi envoy conveyed greetings from the kingdom’s leadership to Pakistan, with Dar reciprocating and conveying his best wishes to Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and other Saudi leaders.

The meeting comes amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. On Wednesday, Yemen’s Houthi rebels said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in Riyadh housing the energy giant’s operations centre.

Powerful explosions also rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.

On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen, targeting fuel and energy facilities it said were being used to support missile and drone attacks, as the Yemeni group threatened a “harsh and painful” response against Saudi airports, refineries and oil installations.

Hours later, Saudi authorities issued warnings of potential hostile aerial threats in the kingdom’s eastern province and Riyadh.

Loud explosions were heard near Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, according to witnesses. Later, a Saudi energy ministry official confirmed the attack. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said that four people — two women, a man and a child — were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

Against this backdrop, Pakistan has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia. On October 5, in an emergency meeting of the Makkah pact in Riyadh, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, maintained that Pakistan and Turkiye had “presence in theatre” and only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

On September 18, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

World.title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
World.content:
Police detained India’s ‘cockroach’ movement founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday, live images from his group showed, ahead of a protest called by him in capital Delhi’s central business district, the latest rally to demand the resignation of India’s election chief.

The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Dipke called Friday’s protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.

The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi’s busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.

The live video on CJP’s Instagram handle showed Dipke coming out of a house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, hauled him into a police car and drove away.

“We are detaining you right now,” a police officer could be heard telling Dipke.

“I have not broken any law right now…how can you detain me?” Dipke asked the police officers as he was taken away.

There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention.

Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.

Park closed ahead of protest

Authorities closed the central New Delhi park before the protest over the voter-roll revision, which critics say has disenfranchised millions.

Dipke urged supporters to rally at Central Park after two of his colleagues were detained for breaching security barricades at Jantar Mantar, where they had gone to wave the national flag.

Earlier this week, police removed authorisation for Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.

On Friday, thousands of security personnel were deployed in parts of the city, with yellow-coloured metal barricades put up at key intersections.

Earlier, Dipke said he was undeterred despite the possibility of being arrested ahead of Friday’s protest.

“Why are you so afraid of cockroaches?” Dipke said.

“I want to tell Narendra Modi that we are not afraid… if waving the Indian national flag lands you in jail, we are ready,” he said Thursday.

Delhi’s municipal authorities said they were closing the Central Park for two days for “administrative” reasons.

Delhi Police have barred public gatherings around Connaught Place citing concerns about public order and safety.

Violation of the orders would “attract suitable legal action”, police said Thursday, but added that they would allow “selected persons” to gather at a “suitable place”.

In recent days, the Indian capital has seen street protests over a large-scale voter roll revision exercise overseen by chief election commissioner Kumar.

Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.

Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

On Friday, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh dismissed the allegations, saying the sole agenda of the opposition parties was “to destroy democratic institutions and create unrest in the country”.

“Their fight is not for electoral reform… not for Gyanesh Kumar, not for the bright future of the country’s youth,” he said at a news conference.

“Rather, this is their conspiracy to seize power by creating anarchy in the country.”

World.title: Hina Javed murder case: Postmortem, crime scene samples match DNA of victim's domestic worker, husband
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: Forensic evidence collected from the crime scene in the Hina Javed murder case has matched with the DNA samples of her husband and domestic servant, according to DNA analysis report.

The report, a copy of which is available with Dawn, concluded that the DNA samples of Hina’s domestic servant matched with postmortem swabs collected from her body. The analysis also finds a match with his sperm samples, with the report stating that “traces of spermatoza” were found on several items while seminal material was found on stained pieces of a carpet.

His DNA profile also matched several other samples collected from the crime scene.

Hina’s husband DNA also matched with samples collected from multiple items at the crime scene, according to the report.

The reports says that the Y-STR profile — a DNA test that examines the Y chromosome — from Hina’s shalwar found a mixture of DNA from at least three individuals, and her husband, father-in-law and domestic servant cannot be excluded as contributors.

Hina, a 45-year-old digital media executive, was found dead at her residence in Rawalpindi in August, with police noting signs of torture. Her husband and their domestic worker were arrested as Hina’s family accused them of murdering her, while her father-in-law was questioned as part of the investigation.

Earlier, her family had written to the National Commission on Human Rights, requesting intervention in the investigation of the murder case and alleging that the probe was compromised.

Last month, the Punjab government has constituted a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation into the murder, in which Hina’s husband and domestic servant have been sent on judicial remand.

World.title: Karachi court acquits alleged drug baroness Anmol alias Pinky in two more cases
World.content:
KARACHI: A sessions court in Karachi on Friday acquitted alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky in two narcotics cases.

The first case was registered with the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in 2018 while the second case was registered at the Gizri police station in 2021.

Anmol, who had been declared a proclaimed offender in both drug cases, had filed separate applications Section 265-K (power of Court to acquit accused at any stage) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for her acquittal.

She appeared before the South additional and sessions judge via a video link at the hearing of her applications today, and the court acquitted her, citing a lack of evidence in both cases.

The court ordered her release from jail if she was not required in any other case.

Her brother, Nasir, has already been acquitted in the 2018 case.

In August, a sessions court had acquitted Anmol in three narcotics cases registered at Karachi’s Gizri police station.

Anmol’s arrest came to light in May when she appeared before a Karachi court. The arrest was made in connection with two cases, pertaining to the possession of drugs and an unlicensed weapon, registered at Karachi’s Garden police station.

The incident gained attention when a video of her being escorted to court without handcuffs went viral on social media.

World.title: Trump's new press secretary admits to failing bar exam as her credentials face scrutiny
World.content:
New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia acknowledged on Thursday that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practising law in the United States, as her credentials face scrutiny.

Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

But the legal credentials of the press secretary, who President Donald Trump appointed last week, were called into question after she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.

The 41-year-old graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law.

In a Fox News interview on Thursday, host Sean Hannity asked Zacharia: “You took the bar exam, but you didn’t pass the bar exam, correct?”

“Yes,” she responded.

In a separate interview with conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move to China with her husband.

“The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn’t need the bar in China,” she said.

Foreign nationals cannot sit China’s bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.

Hannity later asked Zacharia if she had ever taken the bar exam a second time, to which she said: “I did not.

“I had four kids in six years,” she said. “It was never my intent to go into the practice of law.”

Zacharia said on Real America’s Voice that “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer,” given her law degree and experience in business law gained in China, where she worked at a Beijing law firm. She added that she could “provide legal analysis, not legal advice”.

“I was very careful how I executed this.”

The Campaign for Accountability, a political ethics organisation, called on Wednesday for the California Bar Association to launch an investigation.

“In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime,” the organisation said in a press release.

Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday with an unusually short press conference, answering questions from only three journalists.

She succeeds Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative press secretary, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.

World.title: FO condemns Indian minister’s ‘provocative’ remarks threatening aggression against Pakistan
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday condemned Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s “provocative remarks” threatening aggression against Pakistan, saying such statements highlighting the neighbouring country’s “hegemonistic mindset”.

Singh on Thursday had warned Pakistan that any “fresh terrorist activity from across the border would invite a strike even bigger than the last time”, according to Indian news agency ANI.

On Friday, FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan was asked about the comments during his weekly press briefing.

“Pakistan rejects and condemns the Indian defence minister’s provocative remarks entailing a threat of Indian aggression against Pakistan. Such reckless statements reflect India’s hegemonistic mindset and the risk its belligerent posture poses to regional peace and stability in South Asia,” he said.

“We wish to remind India of the consequences of its military aggression in May last year, when Pakistan demonstrated both its capability and resolve to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity and gave a befitting response and reply to Indian aggression,” he said, referring to the brief military conflict between the two countries.

He said that there should be “no ambiguity” that Pakistan remained fully prepared to safeguard its “sovereignty and territorial integrity” against any “ill-advised aggression”.

Haider said Pakistan’s “restraint and commitment to peace” should not be mistaken for weakness, warning that any aggression would be met with a “forceful response”.

“India should draw an appropriate lesson from last year’s experience and abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric and act with responsibility for lasting peace in the region,” he said.

During the briefing, the FO spokesperson was also asked about China’s comments regarding India’s move to recognise and standardise the names of 28 geographical features in Ladakh, a disputed territory claimed by India. China had opposed the move, terming it “illegal”.

The spokesperson was asked about the development in the context of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.

Khan said that said India’s actions on Aug 5, 2019, which revoked the special autonomy of occupied Kashmir, were “illegal and void”.

He added that the move could not alter the fact that Jammu and Kashmir was an internationally recognised disputed territory whose final status must be determined in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri people.

Digitisation of attestation services

During the press briefing, the FO spokesperson was also asked about the reforms introduced to the ministry’s attestation and apostille services.

Last month, the Federal Investigation Agency’s Anti-Corruption Circle Islamabad had busted a network allegedly involved in the preparation and use of fake apostille stickers in connivance with officials from the foreign ministry.

Khan said on Friday that the foreign ministry was progressively digitising and automating apostille services to make them faster, more transparent and accessible.

He said that e-attestation had been launched through the ministry’s portal, while the transition to e-apostille services was under way.

He added that eligible applicants could be exempted from “physical appearances, subject to prescribed safeguards”, a move that would particularly facilitate overseas Pakistanis.

“This is a massive leap forward,” he said, adding that the process was ongoing and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar had personally steered the initiative.

He said that an inquiry into irregularities regarding the services was underway and the results would be announced when it was completed.

World.title: Short-term inflation surges to 11.38pc due to costly food
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose to 11.38 per cent year-on-year in the week ending October 15, driven largely by higher food prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

Of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, prices of 23 commodities (45.10pc) increased, while those of seven items (13.72pc) declined, the data showed. Meanwhile, the prices of 21 items (41.18pc) remained unchanged from the previous week.

Short-term inflation has remained in double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum prices.

The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly fell 0.04pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items.

Unwilling to ease the petroleum levy, the government has continued to raise petrol and diesel prices on a daily basis. The surge in energy costs is not only fuelling inflationary pressures but also indirectly boosting sales tax collections through higher prices of goods and services.

This is cost-push inflation, in which rising energy costs are followed by increases in food prices. As a result, households are under pressure from higher consumer prices.

The index, which comprises 51 items whose prices are collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services.

The items whose prices increased the most over the previous week included pulse gram (4.97pc), wheat flour (3.36pc), chicken (3.31pc), eggs (0.99pc), pulse mash (0.98pc), pulse masoor (0.95pc), firewood (0.69pc), shirting (0.58pc), cooked daal (0.55pc), diesel (0.47pc), LPG (0.42pc) and tea prepared (0.28pc).

The items whose prices declined week-on-week included tomatoes (23.05pc), onions (4.90pc), bananas (2.59pc), petrol (0.70pc), rice basmati broken (0.65pc), sugar (0.62pc) and gur (0.36pc).

On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included onions (75.19pc), LPG (68.95pc), electricity for Q1 (58.59pc), petrol (49.60pc), diesel (43.98pc), wheat flour (35.13pc), chicken (20.77pc), chilies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.90pc), beef (12.27pc), bread plain (9.02pc) and tea prepared (8.36pc).

In contrast, tomatoes prices fell by 63.65pc, followed by potatoes (39.93pc), sugar (23.20pc), eggs (19.83pc), salt powder (14.86pc), pulse masoor (8.97pc), gur (8.92pc) and pulse moong (7.83pc).

The index, which comprises 51 items whose prices are collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services.
